province.description: Two-letter code (BC, AB, SK, MB, ON, QC, NB, NS, PE, NL) or TERR.

region.description: A region slug from list_regions, e.g. kings-county.

water.description: Only land with this frontage (any: ocean, lake, river or creek).

tools.name: search_land

tools.description: One AcreScout listing by its id (8 hex characters, as in https://acrescout.ca/#l=<id>) or its acrescout.ca/land/... page URL: price, size, price per acre, place, how exact the map point is, water, value check, listed date and price cuts, with links.
tools.name: get_listing

description: Independent data on US-listed ETFs and benchmarks for model portfolios, recomputed nightly from public filings and prices. Every figure comes with its source and as-of date and a ready citation. No API key needed.

tools.description: Find US listed ETFs by ticker, fund name, or a word from the name. Use this FIRST when the user names a fund loosely, then etf_profile with the ticker it returns. Refuses rather than returning a near match.
tools.name: etf_search

tools.description: Everything ETFIQ publishes about one fund: issuer, desk, and each figure with its source and as-of date, plus a one sentence verdict on how it did against what its own label promises.
tools.name: etf_profile

tools.description: What a fund holds, by weight, and how old that is. ALWAYS read lag_days before presenting it: an issuer file read today and a filing from two months ago both come back here and are not the same answer.
tools.name: etf_holdings

tools.description: Every US listed fund in a theme, largest first, with what each charges and how much of it is already in the S&P 500. USE THIS for any "what X ETFs are there" or "top X ETFs" question: it returns the whole published set rather than a sample.
tools.name: etf_theme

tools.description: Every theme ETFIQ publishes and how many funds each holds. Call when unsure what a theme is called, then etf_theme.
tools.name: etf_themes

tools.description: Read ANY published ETFIQ page as text: a theme hub, a ranking, a comparison of two funds, an issuer, a methodology note, a dated study. Takes a path like /themes/cyber or a full etfiq.com URL. This reaches all 40,000 pages, including everything the typed tools above do not cover, and returns the page content rather than its navigation.
tools.name: etfiq_page

tools.description: What ETFIQ publishes, section by section, with a page count for each. Start here when the question is not about one fund: it names every section and what is in it.
tools.name: etfiq_sections

tools.description: The pages inside one section, optionally filtered to those whose address contains a word. Use after etfiq_sections to find a page, then etfiq_page to read it. The count returned is the whole matching set even when the list is capped.
tools.name: etfiq_list

tools.description: Every fund matching some filters, largest first, each with its net assets and the source and date that figure came from. Use for "find me all X" questions rather than repeated searches. Fees are percentages, not basis points. Funds with no published size are set aside from a size filter and counted in no_size_figure rather than treated as small.
tools.name: etf_screen

tools.description: How much of their weight two funds hold in common, as ETFIQ published it on the comparison page for that pair. Use when asked whether two ETFs are the same thing, or whether owning both adds anything. Refuses rather than estimating when the pair is not compared or either holdings book is incomplete.
tools.name: etf_overlap

tools.description: What ETFIQ published on a given date, from its frozen dated archive. Use when a question is about a past date, or when a figure needs to stay true after it is quoted: every other tool here answers about today and today moves overnight. Takes YYYY-MM-DD. Covers the pieces written that night, not an arbitrary per-fund figure on an arbitrary day.
tools.name: etfiq_as_of

tools.description: Which US listed ETFs hold a given company, ranked by how much of each fund it is. USE THIS for any "which ETFs hold X", "which fund holds the most X", or "how do I get exposure to X" question, where X is a company rather than a fund, and for "which bond ETFs hold X's debt". Takes a company name or its ticker. Returns every fund holding its shares with the weight its issuer published and the date that book was filed, and separately every fund holding its bonds or other debt. Covers 31,019 companies.
tools.name: etf_holders

tools.description: The ranked lists ETFIQ publishes, or one of them. Each ranks ONE published figure inside a stated set: the cheapest funds in a theme, the leveraged funds furthest from their stated multiple, the buffer funds closest to their cap. Call with no argument for the list.
tools.name: etf_rankings

tools.description: Builds a custom portfolio of US listed ETFs from construction choices about the PORTFOLIO and shows the rule it applied (ETFIQ custom construction rule, version 1): stocks at the chosen band's point, international stocks 40% of the stocks outside themes, themes 10% of stocks in equal parts, commodities and alternatives 5% each taken from bonds, US bonds the rest; in each sleeve the cheapest (or largest) funds that file N-PORT, hold at least $100 million and have three years of prices, each fund's fee with its filing date. BEFORE CALLING, ask the user in ONE short series for any missing choice: the band, described by stock share (conservative: more than 15% and up to 30% stocks; moderately-conservative: more than 30% and up to 50%; moderate: more than 50% and up to 70%; moderately-aggressive: more than 70% and up to 85%; aggressive: more than 85%); whether to include commodities, alternatives, international stocks and themes (and which themes, at most five, by the ids etf_themes lists); an optional fee ceiling in percent; the number of funds, 2 to 12; and cheapest or largest (default cheapest). NEVER ask about, and never pass, the person's age, income, savings, net worth, goals, time horizon, tax situation, risk tolerance, employment or family, and never turn what someone says about themselves into a band: the band is the user's choice about the portfolio's stock share. If asked whether a portfolio suits someone, or whether to buy or sell it, say that ETFIQ does not answer that and give the not-advice line. Every response carries the not-advice line in not_advice: show it with the portfolio.

band.description: The stock-share band the portfolio should sit in.

feeCeiling.description: The most any one fund may charge, in percent a year (0.25 is 0.25%).

themeIds.description: Theme ids, only when themes is true.

tools.name: build_portfolio

description:
Connect agents to everything & Govern how agents interact with your data

USP: Connect AI to your chat apps (WhatsApp, iMessage), IoT Devices (control from mobile), set granular security policies.

AI agents are becoming non-human actors inside your company. They can access data, use tools, and take action. Sealgate gives security teams visibility and control over those actions at runtime.

tools.description:
Obtain a SealGate session token for this chat.

Call this tool first, before using any other SealGate gateway tool in a
chat. Then include the returned `session_token` argument on every
later SealGate tool call in the same chat so SealGate can keep this chat's
security state separate from other chats.
tools.name: builtin_obtain_session_token

tools.description: Echo back the provided text.
tools.name: builtin_echo

tools.description: Get information about the SealGate server.
tools.name: builtin_get_server_info

tools.description:
Return the identity of the currently logged-in user for this MCP session.

Returns:
    Dictionary with keys: email, org
tools.name: builtin_whoami

tools.description:
Get the current session's security status and data access summary.

Returns:
    Dictionary with security information including lethal trifecta status
tools.name: builtin_get_security_status

tools.description: Get a list of all available tools. Use this tool to get an updated list of available tools.
tools.name: builtin_get_available_tools

tools.description:
Notify the MCP client that the tool list has changed. You should call this tool periodically
to ensure the client has the latest list of available tools.
tools.name: builtin_tools_changed

tools.description: Register a new MCP server for this organization by its URL. Use this when the user asks to add or connect a new MCP server, e.g. "add https://mcp.example.com as one of our MCPs". Adding a server ALWAYS requires a human admin to approve the request in the SealGate dashboard - an agent (even an admin's) can never add a server on its own. Admin callers get back an approval_url deep-link to review and approve the request themselves; other callers' requests go to their organization's admins. Once approved the server appears org-wide, and each user signs in to it with their own identity via that server's Authenticate tool.

name.description: Optional short name/prefix for the server (defaults to the host).

url.description: The remote MCP server URL (must be https://... or http://...).

tools.name: builtin_register_new_mcp_url

tools.description: Call another one of your available tools indirectly, by name. Use this when a tool appears in your tool list but you are unable to invoke it directly - typically because it was connected after your tool list was cached. Pass the tool's exact name as `tool` and its arguments as an `arguments` object matching that tool's own input schema. The call runs exactly as if you had invoked the tool directly, and is subject to the same permissions, security policies and approvals; it is not a way to reach tools you do not already have access to.

arguments.description: Arguments object for that tool, matching its input schema.

tool.description: Exact name of the tool to call, as it appears in your tool list.

tools.name: builtin_call_tool

tools.description: Send terse feedback on the SealGate gateway. Caveman style: keywords only, drop filler/articles/hedges. E.g. 'auth flow confusing. token step unclear.'

category.description: Optional short label, e.g. "bug", "dx", "suggestion".

message.description: Feedback, terse (required). Keywords only, no filler words.

description:
Cook County / Chicago, Illinois **property records** for AI agents: resolve a street address to a parcel PIN (**free**), then fetch parcel records, a full **property dossier** (recorded sales & deed history, building permits, property-tax assessment history), or **comparable sales** with an implied valuation range.

 These are joined, derived answers the raw county open data can't return — permits are linked to PINs here (the city permit feed has no PIN field), addresses are joined to parcels, and comps are arm's-length filtered. ~1.9M parcels, refreshed nightly. Public records only — no owner or occupant personal data.

**Tools:** `get_free_sample` ($0) · `search_chicago_property_by_address` (free) · `get_cook_county_parcel` ($0.01) · `get_cook_county_property_dossier` ($0.03) · `find_chicago_comparable_sales` ($0.10)

Paid tools use [x402](https://x402.org) (USDC on Base or Solana) — no signup, no API key. Try the free sample and the [free live example parcels](https://api.ingest0r.com/pricing) before paying. Remote endpoint: `https://api.ingest0r.com/mcp` (streamable-http, nothing to install). Use cases: real-estate due diligence, automated valuation/comps, title research prep, lead enrichment.

tools.description:
Resolve a Cook County / Chicago street address (full or partial) to its
parcel PIN(s) — ranked candidates with address, city, ZIP, and match score.
Call this FIRST when you have an address but not a PIN, then pass a returned
pin to get_cook_county_parcel / get_cook_county_property_dossier /
find_chicago_comparable_sales.
tools.name: search_chicago_property_by_address

tools.description:
Cook County, IL parcel record (address, assessor class, township,
neighborhood, ward, schools, lat/lon) for a 10- or 14-digit PIN.
tools.name: get_cook_county_parcel

tools.description:
Full Cook County / Chicago property dossier (parcel basics, recorded
sales & deed history, building permits, property-tax assessment history,
location context) for a PIN — the one-call due-diligence record.
tools.name: get_cook_county_property_dossier

tools.description:
Recent arm's-length comparable sales (comps) in the same Cook County
assessor neighborhood and property class as the given PIN, with an implied
low/median/high price range — a lightweight automated valuation.

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.

description: a graphing calculator

tools.description:
Build a link that opens the equation.io grapher with the given equations already rendered, validating every row through the app's own parser. Pass the COMPLETE graph in "equations": a flat array of strings, one equation or definition per string, in display order — when editing an existing graph (see read_graph), include the unchanged rows too.

Rows can be: equations and inequalities in x,y (curves, regions; z makes it 3D), bare expressions (scalar fields; complex plots via w), points (rows report "draggable"), parametric tuples in u,v — and definitions: "a = 2" (a draggable slider), "f(x) = x^3 - a x", coordinate fields like "r = sqrt(x^2+y^2)" for polar. t animates. Also derivatives d/dx, integrals int[a..b] f dx, sums sum[n=1..N], domain()/conformal()/iter() for complex plots, y' = … slope fields, random variables "X ~ Normal(m, s)"/"P(0<X<2)"/"E(X^2)", and "view(x = -5..5, y = -2..2)"/"camera(theta, phi)" framing rows. That is a menu, not the syntax: before your first non-trivial graph, read the "syntax" MCP resource (also at https://equation.io/llms.txt).

The result attaches a PNG preview — a simplified CPU sketch (t = 0, 3D as wireframes) for checking shape and framing. It draws LESS than the app: rows it cannot draw are listed in "preview_omits" with the reason, so a sparse or missing preview never means the equations failed — "rows" is the validation verdict. Look at it: are the interesting features visible? If a row fails validation, fix it and call again. Give users the share_url (it unfurls to a preview card in chat apps); url is the equivalent #-fragment form.

equations.description: Every equation in the graph, in display order. One equation or definition per string — do not join rows with ";" (inside quoted text a ";" is data, and kept).

tools.name: create_graph

tools.description: Decode an equation.io link (either the #-fragment form or the /g/ share form) into its list of equation rows, so you can edit them and build a new link with create_graph.

url.description: An equation.io graph URL.

tools.name: read_graph

description:
Shows a candlestick price chart for a public ticker, with volume and the indicators you name, plus a short plain-language read of what is on the chart.

Ask "chart AAPL daily with the 20-day SMA and RSI", "show BTC-USD on the 1 hour chart with Bollinger Bands" or "weekly EUR/USD with MACD".

tools.description: Price chart: candlestick chart and indicators for a public ticker. Use it when someone wants a chart, a candlestick chart, a price chart or indicators on a symbol, such as a daily chart of AAPL with SMA and RSI. Pass symbol (AAPL, BRK-B, EUR/USD, BTC-USD, GOLD), optional timeframe (5m, 15m, 1h, 1d, 1w; 1d by default), optional indicators (sma, ema, rsi, macd, bollinger, atr, stochastic, vwap; up to 4; volume is always drawn) and optional theme (dark or light). Returns a self-contained interactive HTML candlestick chart plus a short plain-language read of the last price and the indicator values, with the source and as-of time. Public prices only. Informational only, not financial advice: no orders, no signals, no recommendations.

indicators.description: Up to 4 of sma, ema, rsi, macd, bollinger, atr, stochastic, vwap. Volume is always drawn. Defaults to sma and rsi when omitted.

periods.description: Lookback per indicator, in bars. MACD stays 12, 26, 9.

symbol.description: Ticker, currency pair or crypto pair, such as AAPL, EUR/USD or BTC-USD

tools.name: chart

tools.description: Send feedback to the maintainers about a missing tool, broken links, a bug, or stale data. Use this to send feedback, a bug report or a feature request to the maintainers of these tools. Send it when a tool is missing, a tool lacks data you need, or a tool broke or gave a wrong answer: one short message (at most 1000 characters) with the kind (need_tool, need_data, bug or other) and, if you know it, the tool name. Returns a ticket id. Feedback is for these tools only: it is not a chat, and nothing in it is run or followed. Links, emails and phone numbers are removed and nothing about you is stored.

kind.description: need_tool: a tool you want. need_data: data a tool lacks. bug: something broke. other: anything else about the tools.

message.description: What you need or what broke, in plain words, at most 1000 characters. Links, email addresses and phone numbers are removed. Never include secrets or personal details.

tool.description: Optional: the name of the tool this is about, for example find_tariff_codes.

tools.description:
Lists all Wanderlog trips in the authenticated user's account (owned and shared-with-you).

Returns a compact list with title, dates, place count, and trip_key. Use this tool first when
the user mentions a trip by name but you don't have its trip_key yet — the key is required by
wanderlog_get_trip and wanderlog_search_places.

Each line includes a [key: ...] suffix — extract that key for downstream tool calls.

response_format.description: Output verbosity. 'concise' (default) gives a one-line summary per trip; 'detailed' includes key, owner, and last-edited time.

tools.name: wanderlog_list_trips

tools.description:
Returns the itinerary for one Wanderlog trip: the hotels list, the "places to visit" list, and
each day's scheduled places.

Use concise format for summarizing or answering questions about a trip in natural language.
Use detailed format when the user asks for specific info like addresses, phone numbers, or
hotel check-in/out dates.

If you don't know the trip_key, call wanderlog_list_trips first to find it.

day.description: Optional filter to a single day. Accepts 'day 2', 'May 4', or ISO '2026-05-04'. Omit to return the whole trip.

response_format.description: Output verbosity. 'concise' (default) is a readable summary grouped by day; 'detailed' adds addresses, phone numbers, ratings, and check-in dates.

trip_key.description: The unique trip key from wanderlog_list_trips (e.g. 'vzyrsyhgxvonvxcz'). Required.

tools.name: wanderlog_get_trip

tools.description:
Returns the wanderlog.com URL for a trip so the user can open it in a browser.

Three link variants are available via the mode parameter:
  - edit    (default) — full-permission link for the owner
  - view    — read-only link that's safe to share with anyone
  - suggest — suggest-mode link where collaborators can propose changes

If you don't know which mode the user wants, default to edit.

mode.description: Which link variant to return. 'edit' (default) is the primary link with full permissions. 'view' is a read-only share link. 'suggest' is a suggest-mode share link where collaborators can propose changes.

tools.name: wanderlog_get_trip_url

tools.description:
Search for real-world places (restaurants, attractions, hotels, parks, landmarks) near the
destination of a Wanderlog trip. Returns candidate results with names and short descriptions.

Use this to resolve user requests like "find a good coffee shop in Queenstown" into specific
place candidates. Results are geographically biased toward the trip's location, not global.

If the user wants to *add* a place to a trip, call this first with concise format to present
options, then call again with detailed format to get place_ids for downstream actions.

query.description: What to search for. Examples: 'sushi restaurant', 'hiking trail', 'coffee near the hotel'.

response_format.description: Output verbosity. 'concise' lists name + description only; 'detailed' adds the Google place_id needed for downstream tool calls.

trip_key.description: The trip to scope this search to. Search results are geographically biased toward the trip's destination.

tools.name: wanderlog_search_places

tools.description:
Creates a new Wanderlog trip for the given destination and date range. The trip is created
empty (no places yet) with one pre-generated day section per day in the range.

After creating a trip, populate each day using ALL of these tools together — places alone
make a flat list, but notes and checklists are what make an itinerary actually useful:

1. wanderlog_add_place — add attractions, restaurants, and activities
2. wanderlog_add_note — add between places for transit directions, practical tips, time
   warnings, or local recommendations (e.g. "Walk 10 min south along the river to the next
   stop" or "Closed Mondays — check hours before visiting")
3. wanderlog_add_hotel — add accommodation with check-in/check-out dates
4. wanderlog_add_checklist — add a packing list to the trip, or per-day task lists
   (e.g. "Day 1 prep: print tickets, charge camera, pack umbrella")

A good itinerary has notes after most places — think of them as the connective tissue that
turns a list of pins on a map into a real travel plan.

Returns the new trip key so you can reference it in subsequent tool calls.

destination.description: City or region name to plan the trip around (e.g. 'Lisbon', 'Tokyo', 'Banff'). Resolved via Wanderlog's geo autocomplete — the top-ranked result is used.

end_date.description: Last day of the trip, YYYY-MM-DD.

privacy.description: Trip visibility. 'private' is the safe default.

start_date.description: First day of the trip, YYYY-MM-DD.

title.description: Optional custom title. If omitted, Wanderlog auto-generates one like 'Trip to Lisbon'.

tools.name: wanderlog_create_trip

tools.description:
Adds a place to a Wanderlog trip. Searches for the place near the trip's destination, picks the
best match, and inserts it into either a specific day or the general "Places to visit" list.

PREFERRED: Use the "note" parameter to attach practical context directly to each place — transit
directions, what to order, booking tips, time guidance. This is better than a separate
wanderlog_add_note call because the note lives on the place itself in the itinerary. Use the
"start_time" and "end_time" parameters to give the place a scheduled time window.

Use standalone wanderlog_add_note only for freestanding commentary between places (neighborhood
context, multi-stop transit, day-level tips that aren't about a specific place).

Returns a confirmation including the resolved place name and where it was added.

day.description: Optional day to add the place to. Accepts 'day 2', 'May 4', or ISO '2026-05-04'. Omit to add the place to the trip's 'Places to visit' list (unscheduled).

end_time.description: Optional end time in HH:mm format (e.g. '11:30'). Only used with start_time.

note.description: Optional inline note attached directly to this place. Use for practical context: transit directions, what to order, booking tips, time guidance. Appears on the place itself in Wanderlog (not as a separate note block).

place.description: Name of the place to add. Examples: 'Sensō-ji', 'a ramen place in Shinjuku', 'Louvre'. Will be matched against Google Places near the trip's destination; if multiple match, the top result is used.

start_time.description: Optional start time in HH:mm format (e.g. '09:00'). Adds a scheduled time to the place.

trip_key.description: The trip to add to. Use wanderlog_list_trips if you don't know the key.

tools.name: wanderlog_add_place

tools.description:
Adds a hotel booking to a Wanderlog trip with check-in and check-out dates. If the trip does
not yet have a "Hotels and lodging" section, one is created automatically.

Returns confirmation with the resolved hotel name and the booking window.

check_out.description: Check-out date, YYYY-MM-DD. Must be after check_in.

hotel.description: Hotel name to search for. Examples: 'Park Hyatt Tokyo', 'the cheap hostel near the train station'. Matched against Google Places near the trip's destination.

trip_key.description: The trip to add the hotel to.

tools.name: wanderlog_add_hotel

tools.description:
Adds a text note to a Wanderlog trip. Notes appear inline between places in a day, acting as
the connective tissue of the itinerary. Every well-built day should have notes between stops.

When to add a note (do this after adding each place or group of places):
- How to get there: "Walk 15 min along the South Bank, or take the Jubilee line one stop"
- Practical tips: "Book tickets online at least 2 days ahead — sells out in summer"
- Food/drink recs: "Try the salt beef bagel at Beigel Bake — cash only, open 24hrs"
- Time guidance: "Budget 2-3 hours here. Open 10am-6pm, closed Tuesdays"
- Neighborhood context: "This area is great for wandering — no rush, just explore the lanes"

Returns a confirmation of where the note was added.

day.description: Optional day to add the note to. Accepts 'day 2', 'May 4', or ISO '2026-05-04'. Omit to add to the 'Places to visit' list.

text.description: The note text. Plain text — can be multi-line.

trip_key.description: The trip to add the note to. Use wanderlog_list_trips if you don't know the key.

tools.name: wanderlog_add_note

tools.description:
Adds a checklist to a Wanderlog trip. Each item starts unchecked and can be ticked off in the
Wanderlog app.

Add at least one checklist per trip. Common patterns:
- On the trip (no day): a packing list or "before departure" checklist
- On day 1: an arrival-day checklist ("pick up Oyster card", "check into hotel", "buy SIM")
- On specific days: day-of tasks ("bring swimsuit", "charge camera", "carry cash for market")

Returns a confirmation including the checklist title and item count.

day.description: Optional day to add the checklist to. Accepts 'day 2', 'May 4', or ISO '2026-05-04'. Omit to add to the 'Places to visit' list.

items.description: Checklist items. Each string becomes one checkbox item, initially unchecked.

title.description: Optional title for the checklist (e.g. 'Packing list'). Omit for an untitled checklist.

trip_key.description: The trip to add the checklist to. Use wanderlog_list_trips if you don't know the key.

tools.name: wanderlog_add_checklist

tools.description:
Updates an existing place in a Wanderlog trip with an inline note, start/end time, or both.
Use this to enrich places that were already added — set practical context, scheduled times,
or both in one call.

At least one of note, start_time, or end_time must be provided.

The place is resolved by natural-language reference (same syntax as wanderlog_remove_place).
If ambiguous, returns a disambiguation list without making changes.

end_time.description: Set or replace the end time (HH:mm format).

note.description: Set or replace the inline note on this place. Practical context: transit, tips, timing, what to see.

place.description: Natural-language reference to the place. Examples: 'Sensō-ji', 'the hotel', 'Queenstown Gardens on day 2'. Supports ordinals for duplicates: '2nd Starbucks'.

start_time.description: Set or replace the start time (HH:mm format).

tools.name: wanderlog_annotate_place

tools.description:
Adds a budget expense to a Wanderlog trip linked to a specific place. Expenses appear in the
trip's budget tracker on the linked place.

Use this after adding places to give the trip a cost dimension — estimated meal costs, entrance
fees, transport passes, etc. The place must already exist in the trip.

Returns confirmation with the expense amount and description.

category.description: Expense category.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. 'USD', 'JPY', 'EUR'). Defaults to USD.

date.description: Date of the expense, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today if omitted.

description.description: What the expense is for (e.g. 'Lunch at Ichiran Ramen', 'Subway day pass').

place.description: Natural-language reference to link this expense to a place in the trip (e.g. 'Sensō-ji', 'the hotel'). Required — every expense must be linked to a place.

trip_key.description: The trip to add the expense to.

tools.name: wanderlog_add_expense

tools.description:
Removes a place (or flight, train, hotel — any block) from a Wanderlog trip based on a
natural-language reference.

Supported reference forms:
  - Exact or partial name: "Queenstown Gardens", "Gardens"
  - Role keywords: "the hotel", "the flight", "the train"
  - Day filter: "Queenstown Gardens on May 4" or "... on day 3"
  - Ordinal prefix (for duplicates): "1st Queenstown Gardens", "second X", "last X"
  - Combined: "2nd Queenstown Gardens on May 4"

If the reference is ambiguous (multiple places match), the tool returns a numbered list of
candidates and does NOT make any change. Re-call with an ordinal prefix ("1st X", "2nd X") or
a more specific filter to pick the one you want.

place_ref.description: Natural-language reference to the place you want to remove. Examples: 'Queenstown Gardens', 'the hotel', 'the sushi place on day 3'. Supports ordinal prefixes for duplicates: '1st Queenstown Gardens', 'second Queenstown Gardens', 'last Queenstown Gardens'. Supports day filters via ' on ': 'Queenstown Gardens on May 4'. Ordinals and day filters can be combined: '2nd Queenstown Gardens on May 4'.

tools.name: wanderlog_remove_place

tools.description:
Changes the date range of an existing Wanderlog trip. Preserves content on days that remain
in the new range (they're kept in place with their blocks intact), adds empty day sections for
newly-included days, and removes day sections for days no longer in range.

SAFETY: If the new range would delete days that currently contain places or notes, the tool
refuses by default and returns a list of the content that would be lost. Pass force: true to
override, or move the content to other days first.

Does not affect the Hotels, Flights, Transit, or Places-to-visit sections — only the
per-day sections are added/removed.

end_date.description: New last day of the trip, YYYY-MM-DD. Must be >= start_date.

force.description: If true, allows the update even when it would delete days that currently contain places. DEFAULT false — the tool refuses destructive removes with a helpful error listing what would be lost, so the user can move content first.

start_date.description: New first day of the trip, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: wanderlog_update_trip_dates

description:
**Pay-per-call API marketplace on Base (USDC).**

x402-market lets AI agents discover and invoke any listed API end-to-end with one tool call. The MCP server handles HTTP 402 payment challenges automatically using your wallet, so Claude (or any MCP client) pays for API calls on its own.

## How it works

1. `list_catalog` — discover available paid APIs in the marketplace
2. `get_listing` — inspect endpoint schema, pricing, and usage notes
3. `pay_and_call` — invoke the API end-to-end; pays the seller via x402 / USDC on Base if a 402 challenge is returned
4. `claim_refund` — auto-judge refund for failed calls or >30s upstream latency

## Setup

- `MCP_BUYER_PRIVATE_KEY` (required): Hot wallet on Base mainnet with a small USDC + ETH balance. **Use a separate wallet, not your main one.**
- `MCP_MAX_PRICE`: Hard cap per call (USDC). Default `1`.
- Other params have safe defaults.

## Links

- npm: `@x402-market/mcp-server`
- GitHub: https://github.com/AsaiShota/x402-market
- Marketplace API: https://x402-market-api.lien-studio-akiyama.workers.dev

tools.description: Use this tool when the user asks what APIs are available, or you need to discover paid APIs to satisfy a task. Returns a JSON array of active marketplace listings with seller_slug, listing slug, name, description, price_usdc, category, use_cases, and tags.
tools.name: list_catalog

tools.description: Use this tool when you already have a listing slug and need its full schema before invoking it. Returns one listing as JSON (request_schema, response_schema, when_to_use, output_format_description, example_calls).
tools.name: get_listing

tools.description: Use this tool when the user wants to actually invoke a paid API and receive its response. End-to-end: GET the 402 price, send USDC on Base from the configured buyer wallet, retry with X-Payment, return the upstream JSON. Returns { status, data, tx_hash, price_paid_usdc, pay_to } as text.
tools.name: pay_and_call

tools.description: Use this tool when a previously paid call failed and the user asks for a refund. Auto-judge approves on upstream failure or >30s latency, rejects otherwise. Returns the API's HTTP status + JSON response. Signs the request with the configured buyer private key.
tools.name: claim_refund

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.
tools.name: marketplace

Or paste it here for a session-only login: call with { token: "<jwt>" } after the user pastes, or with no args to get the link.

tools.description: Current prices and limits for Phoenix Motion clips and Cloud Restore, in US dollars. Free, no key needed.
tools.name: get_prices

tools.description: Exact price in US dollars to restore one video clip in the cloud, from its length and resolution. Free, no key needed.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the clip in seconds.

height.description: Frame height in pixels, if known (default: standard definition).

quality.description: standard: denoise, deinterlace, 2x upscale. enhanced: adds AI detail reconstruction, for badly degraded footage. studio_max: enhanced, delivered at up to 4K.

width.description: Frame width in pixels, if known (default: standard definition).

tools.name: quote_restore

tools.description: Start a cloud restore of an old video (tape, DVD, film scan, old phone clip): denoise, deinterlace, rebuild detail and upscale. Returns an upload_url; PUT the video there, then call start_restore. With an agent key it is paid from the balance now (pay_with 'balance'), and refunded to the balance if it fails. With pay_with 'checkout' (or no key) the user pays through a checkout link that start_restore returns. Up to 2 GB; standard up to 30 minutes, enhanced and studio_max up to 6 minutes.

content_type.description: The video's MIME type, e.g. video/mp4.

duration_seconds.description: Length in seconds. The GPU checks it; a file much longer than declared is refused and refunded.

email.description: Needed for pay_with 'checkout': where the receipt goes.

filename.description: The video's file name, e.g. wedding-1994.mp4.

pay_with.description: Default: balance when this connection has a key, otherwise checkout.

quality.description: standard: denoise, deinterlace, 2x upscale. enhanced: adds AI detail reconstruction, for badly degraded footage. studio_max: enhanced, delivered at up to 4K.

size_bytes.description: File size in bytes, up to 2 GB.

width.description: Frame width in pixels. Bigger frames cost more; the GPU checks the real file.

tools.name: create_restore

tools.description: After the video is uploaded: starts a balance-paid restore on the GPU, or returns the checkout_url the user must open to pay for a checkout restore (it starts once they have paid).
tools.name: start_restore

tools.description: Status of a restore. When status is 'done', download_url is the restored video (valid 24 hours).
tools.name: get_restore

tools.description: Phoenix Motion: turn one still image into a five-second video clip at 24 fps, with sound made in the same pass, from a prompt describing the motion, camera and sound. Costs the listed price (see get_prices) from the balance; a clip that fails or is refused costs nothing. Pass image_url to start at once; otherwise PUT the image to the returned upload_url and call start_clip.

content_type.description: Needed only when uploading instead of image_url.

image_url.description: Public link to a JPEG, PNG or WebP image, up to 20 MB.

loop.description: Seamless loop: only what the prompt names moves, and the clip ends where it starts.

prompt.description: What moves, how, and what the camera and sound do. Up to 800 characters.

seed.description: Reuse a clip's seed to get the same take again.

size.description: 480p costs $0.59 and is quicker; 720p costs $0.99 and is sharper.

tools.name: make_clip

tools.description: After uploading the image to make_clip's upload_url: start making the clip.
tools.name: start_clip

tools.description: Status of a clip. When status is 'done', video_url plays it and download_url saves it (both valid 24 hours).
tools.name: get_clip

tools.description: The most recent clips made with this key, newest first.
tools.name: list_clips

tools.description: Cancel a restore or clip whose file was never uploaded, and get its price back on the balance at once.

job_id.description: A restore's job_id (cloud_…) or a clip_id (motion_…).

tools.name: cancel_job

tools.description: The Phoenix balance this key can spend: the balance, and this key's limit, amount spent and amount left.
tools.name: get_balance

tools.description: A checkout link the user opens to add money to the balance (US$5 to $200). Nothing is charged until they pay.

email.description: For the receipt, if the balance doesn't have one yet.

tools.name: create_top_up_link

tools.description: Add money to the balance by paying USDC on Base yourself, with x402 (for assistants that hold a crypto wallet). Call it without a payment to get the payment requirements back (an x402 PaymentRequired error), sign the EIP-3009 transfer, then call it again with the signed payment in _meta['x402/payment']. $1 to $200; 1 USDC adds $1. No gas needed: the facilitator pays it.
tools.name: top_up_with_usdc

description:
Read-only access to a real crypto and traditional investment portfolio: holdings, profit and loss, portfolio score, FIFO capital-gains figures and live market data. Authenticated with the user's own API key. The server never receives private keys and cannot move funds. Available on the Premium plan.

To connect, create an API key in Account on https://chainfolioai.com and paste it into the apiKey field. Documentation: https://chainfolioai.com/developers

tools.description: Devolve o último snapshot do portefólio do utilizador: saldos por rede (ETH, SOL, BTC, ADA), CEX, DeFi e ativos manuais.

year.description: Ano civil das vendas (opcional; sem ele devolve tudo).

tools.name: get_realized_gains

tools.description: ESTIMATIVA de imposto sobre mais-valias num país, na moeda desse país: método de custo do país (FIFO, preço médio, LIFO, pool britânico, soma anual), cada operação convertida à taxa do BCE da sua data, regras do ano da venda, prazo de detenção, isenção anual e, onde a lei deixa, perdas de anos anteriores. Não é uma declaração fiscal. As opções de cada país estão em list_tax_countries (campo options).

alternative.description: Só BR, PT, AR e AT: a opção alternativa de onde estão as moedas (BR exchange estrangeira; PT corretora fora da UE/EEE sem convenção; AR venda em pesos; AT plataforma austríaca).

country.description: Código do país em duas letras (ex.: PT, ES, US). Ver list_tax_countries.

marginalRate.description: Só onde a taxa depende do rendimento (DE, GB, US, CA, AU, LU, MX): a taxa marginal da pessoa em fração (0.35 = 35%). Sem ela usa-se a taxa máxima.

marginalRateLong.description: Só US: a taxa de longo prazo da pessoa em fração (0, 0.15 ou 0.20, mais 0.038 de NIIT se aplicável).

year.description: Ano fiscal das vendas (opcional). No Reino Unido e na Austrália é o ano em que o ano fiscal começa (2025 = 2025/26).

tools.description: 列出可开岗的数字员工模板。用于：想知道"系统能开哪些岗位"、或用户要开通新岗位时。返回每个模板的 templateId / 名称 / 说明 / canOpen / missingHandlers / 动作清单。别用它找"已开好的岗位"——那是 list_my_staff。canOpen=false 的模板不可开通（缺实现），别推荐用户选。参数：无。
tools.name: list_templates

tools.description: 列出我名下的数字员工岗位（slug / 名称 / 模板 / 画布链接）。用户问"我有哪些岗位"用它；后续所有按岗位操作的工具都要 slug，slug 一律从这里拿，不要凭记忆拼。参数：无。
tools.name: list_my_staff

tools.description: 为岗位生成画布链接 + 会话 ID。用于用户需要"看得见的界面"（看报告/看商品/做检测）。参数：slug 必填；hostUserId 宿主用户标识（强烈建议带，会话归属和离线补推都靠它）；targetId 关爱/业务对象；app 指定画布页（如 aicare-kf）。返回 {url, session_id}——把 session_id 存下来，get_session_log / push_screen 都用它。会话在返回时已建立：现在就能 push_screen 给"还没来的人"备卡片，用户打开链接即补推；人打开后聊天/埋点都归到同一个 session_id。

app.description: 画布页面，默认岗位配置的；AICare 康护可传 aicare-kf

hostUserId.description: 宿主系统的用户标识，如 AICare 的 userId

targetId.description: 关爱对象/服务对象 ID（AICare 类岗位用）

tools.name: open_canvas

tools.description: 读岗位配置：personaPrompt / serviceFlow / promotionConfig / productSources / contextMode / layoutStyle / templateId / llmMode（只说是否 BYOK，不给密钥）/ tts。参数：slug 必填。改之前先读，否则会用"想当然的人设"覆盖客户调过的版本。
tools.name: get_staff_config

tools.description: 局部修改岗位配置，patch 只放要改的字段：personaPrompt(人设) / serviceFlow(服务流程，一行一步) / promotionConfig({categories:[{name,priority,url}]}) / productSources([{key,label,searchUrl,weAppId?,weAppUsername?}]) / layoutStyle(split|pip|classic) / contextMode(inline|webhook) / contextWebhookUrl / name。参数：slug、patch 都必填。这是写操作，改的是客户的岗位，改完立刻生效；不确定用户真要改时先复述一遍再调。
tools.name: patch_staff_config

tools.description: 列出这个岗位（按其模板）能做的动作：id / title / description / cost / credits / anonymous / job / params(JSON Schema)。参数：slug 必填。调 canvas_action 前先调它，不要猜 action 名——各岗位动作集不同，params 按它给的 schema 填。
tools.name: list_actions

tools.description: 执行一个岗位动作（如 AICare 的 preflight / list_checks / gen_report / run_detection / resolve_user）。参数：slug、action 必填；params 按 list_actions 的 schema 填；session_id 想让结果落在某次会话里就带；hostUserId 宿主用户标识可选。返回 {ok, mode:"sync", data} 直接用；{ok, mode:"job", jobId, pollSec} 用 get_job 轮询。代价：list_actions 标 paid 的会从岗位出资人余额扣 credits（出报告 5 / 跑检测 2），失败不扣；同键（如同对象同一天）重复调用返回缓存结果（cached 标记）不重复扣，用户催第二次可放心重试。典型编排：list_actions → canvas_action(preflight) 拿背景 → canvas_action(gen_report) → get_job → 用自然语言讲给用户。公共岗位：gaia-academy（龙虾学院 · Agent 进修）的动作标 public:true——任何持有效 Key 的调用方都能跑，不需要拥有该岗位；学员身份取调用方 Key 的用户，非 public 动作对非归属方仍 403。典型用法：canvas_action(gaia-academy, search_courses → start_exam → submit_exam → get_principle)。

params.description: 按 list_actions 给的 JSON Schema 填

session_id.description: 可选，open_canvas 给的会话 ID，动作记录会挂到该会话

tools.name: canvas_action

tools.description: 按 job_id 查长任务：queued / running / done(带 result) / failed(带 error)。建议每 3 秒查一次。error 是人话（如"关爱对象不存在或已删除"），照原话转述给用户，不要改写成"系统繁忙"，也不要拿同参数重试。
tools.name: get_job

tools.description: 岗位一段时间的汇总：会话数、真人对话轮数、埋点数、动作调用数、tokens、按日曲线。参数：slug 必填；from/to ISO 时间，默认最近 30 天。用户问"这岗位最近怎么样/今天多少人来"就用它，不要靠聊天历史猜数字。需要有效 Key，匿名不开。
tools.name: get_stats

tools.description: 岗位的访客会话列表（最近优先）：session_id、宿主用户标识、轮数、时间。参数：slug 必填；q 按宿主用户标识模糊搜；from/to；limit；cursor 翻页传上一页返回的 nextCursor。想看"最近都服务了哪些人"用它，再拿 session_id 看明细。需要有效 Key，匿名不开。
tools.name: list_sessions

tools.description: 单个会话按时间正序的完整流水：用户消息 / AI 回复(带 tokens) / 埋点 / 动作调用 / 推屏。参数：slug 和 session_id 两个都必填（slug 用于显式鉴权）。调用前先从 list_sessions 或 open_canvas 拿到合法 session_id。隐私边界：只能读自己岗位的记录。需要有效 Key，匿名不开。
tools.name: get_session_log

tools.description: 跨会话按类型拉事件（倒序）：type = chat_user / chat_assistant / track / action_call / page_open / push。参数：slug 必填；type、from/to、limit(≤500)。每条带 source（mcp / page / server，看得出谁发起的）；action_call 的 payload 有 params/ok/ms/credits/cached/jobId——计费与排障的证据链；push 的 payload 有 preview。需要有效 Key，匿名不开。
tools.name: query_events

tools.description: 把内容推到某个画布会话的屏上。参数：session_id 必填（来自 open_canvas 或 list_sessions）；content 必填，写成一条"助手回复"文本，可含 ```canvas-md（Markdown 卡片）/ ```canvas-html（完整 HTML 文档）/ ```canvas（JSON 块）围栏，围栏外文字显示为字幕；speak=true 朗读字幕；title 可选。会话在线立即上屏；不在线（含还没人打开过的）存为待展示，该会话或同岗位同一 hostUserId 下次打开自动补推。屏属于会话不属于人：别复用别人的 session_id；要执行有副作用的动作（出报告/跑检测）用 canvas_action。需要有效 Key，匿名不开。

description:
# Prefeitura SP São Paulo: Regularidade OTTC

Prefeitura SP São Paulo: Regularidade OTTC, consulta em fonte oficial. Hospedado pela plataforma, sem credenciais da plataforma, pague por consulta com crédito pré-pago.

Funciona em qualquer cliente MCP. Servidor remoto: `https://api.mcp.ai/p_pref_sp_sao_paulo_ottc`

tools.description: Prefeitura SP São Paulo: Regularidade OTTC, consulta em fonte oficial. Hospedado pela plataforma, sem credenciais da plataforma, pague por consulta com crédito pré-pago. Consulta informação de fontes e órgãos oficiais brasileiros (a mesma disponível ao cidadão), não é dado sigiloso. O cliente é o controlador dos dados e responde pela finalidade legítima (LGPD).
tools.name: pref_sp_sao_paulo_ottc_consultar

tools.name: report_bug

tools.description: Returns connection status and URLs. When all providers are connected, returns authenticated:true and empty pending[]. When credentials are missing, returns connect_url for the toolkit and per-install URLs.
tools.name: connect

tools.description: Returns the current toolkit state: installed MCPs, their connection status, the accounts connected to each one, and how many catalog tools each exposes.
tools.name: toolkit_info

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.
tools.name: marketplace

tools.description: MCP.AI for IDE agents (Cursor, etc.): log in in the browser, copy the access token. Best: add it to this server's config as a header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for a permanent, non-expiring connection. Or paste it here for a session-only login: call with { token: "<jwt>" } after the user pastes, or with no args to get the link.
tools.name: authenticate

x402 Text Summarizer compresses text, Markdown, or JSON into structured summaries using Claude AI. Part of the x402 micropayment task market — pay per call with $0.005 USDC on Base mainnet, no subscriptions or API keys required.

Two tools included:
summarize_text — full access. Accepts plain text, Markdown, or JSON input up to 100KB.

description: Create, manage, and analyze online forms and surveys. Collect submissions, view responses, and build workflows from form data.

tools.description:
Search forms by title and/or submissions by natural language query.
Submissions scope: Provide form_id to search submissions of a single form. Without form_id, submissions are searched only within forms matched by form_query (there is no global all-forms submissions search).
Queries: form_query is an array of plain strings for form title matching (OR logic). submission_inquiry is a single natural language sentence describing the desired submission filter (IMPORTANT: send it as a plain string, never as an array). Regex is not supported.
Empty form query: Empty form_query lists your forms.
Submission inquiry: When search_submissions is true, submission_inquiry is REQUIRED and must contain a non-empty natural language string. Empty submission_inquiry will return an error when searching submissions.
Toggles: Use search_forms and search_submissions to include forms and/or submissions in the result. limit controls the number fetched per underlying request.
Examples: (1) form_query=["invoice"] to find forms; (2) form_id="123" and submission_inquiry="payments above 100 usd" to find matching submissions in that form; (3) form_query=["order"], submission_inquiry="customers requesting refunds" to search submissions only within forms whose titles match "order".

form_id.description: Optional: ID of a single form. Required to search that form's submissions directly. When omitted, submissions are searched only within forms matched by form_query (no global all-forms submissions search).

form_query.description: Array of plain strings matched against form titles (OR logic). Regex is not supported. Empty array lists your forms.

limit.description: Maximum items fetched per underlying request (default: 20).

search_forms.description: Include forms matched by form_query in results (default: true).

search_submissions.description: Include submissions matched by submission_query in results (default: true). Without form_id, searches only within forms matched by form_query.

submission_inquiry.description: REQUIRED when search_submissions is true: Using the user_query, provide a single natural language sentence that filters the submissions (plain string only; do NOT wrap it in an array). e.g., "people who filled vegan as yes".

user_query.description: The exact user query written in the chat.

description:
OnRamperX is a non-custodial value router for AI agents and humans — the one
MCP tool to onramp fiat to crypto, offramp crypto to fiat, swap any token
across 80+ chains, and settle agent payments.

- Onramp: buy USDC on Base with a US debit card / Apple Pay / Google Pay
(Coinbase Headless Onramp v2), human-in-the-loop for the fiat tap.
- Swap & bridge: convert ETH, SOL, USDT, or any token on any chain into USDC
on Base in one signature via Relay (~2.7s median, cross-chain, gas-abstracted),
earning claimable app fees.
- Agent payments (x402): pay-per-call settlement in USDC on Base via the
Coinbase CDP facilitator, listed in the x402 Bazaar. AP2 / a2a-x402 aligned.
- Rail-selection engine: quotes every eligible rail and returns ranked,
non-custodial paths with fees, ETA, KYC burden, and plain-English reasoning.
- Wallets: provision a gasless, user-exportable CDP Embedded Wallet on Base.

Non-custodial by design — the platform never holds funds mid-flow. Settlement
centers on USDC on Base. Callable from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and framework
agents. Tools: get_route_quote, create_swap, check_swap, create_onramp_session,
provision_wallet. Built on MCP 2025-06-18, A2A 0.3, x402 v2, OAuth 2.1
(RFC 9728 PRM + RFC 8414 + RFC 7591 DCR + PKCE-S256) with a client_credentials

PAT for framework agents. Human swap UI at https://router.mudko.com/swap.
homepage: https://router.mudko.com

description: Agent-readable and agent-playable data for **The Floor**, an on-chain strategy game on Robinhood Chain. 22 tools: read live desks, alpha, emissions and reinvest-vs-dump analytics; get per-wallet strategy math; and prepare **unsigned** transactions to join, recruit, upgrade, collect PnL, and swap ETH↔FLOOR. Remote (streamable HTTP), no install, no keys held. Unofficial companion to thefloor.sh.

tools.description: The whole state of the floor in one call: price, market cap, supply, burned, emissions/halving, global alpha, player count, and the reinvest-vs-sell split. Start here for context.

tools.description: Do desk owners reinvest or dump? Splits FLOOR flow into player / trader / routed / liquidity. playerSellShare is a share of ATTRIBUTABLE sells only; routed = aggregator/bot flow with no identifiable human; liquidity (LP adds/withdrawals) is excluded from buys and sells entirely. Use these buckets — deriving "sells" from raw pool transfers double-counts LP deposits as dumps.

tools.description: Build the UNSIGNED transaction that opens a desk (joins the game). Returns {to, value, data} for the caller to sign with their OWN wallet — this server never sees, holds, or asks for a private key, and never broadcasts. Costs 0.01 ETH. IMPORTANT: the recruiter is written on-chain at desk creation and can NEVER be changed afterwards; it defaults to this dashboard's address (which earns 5% of what the player later spends, paid from the game treasury, costing the player nothing). Pass `referrer` to set your own, or the zero address for none. Always tell the user who the referrer is before they sign.

tools.description: The decision-relevant math for one wallet, so an agent can reason about its next move: current alpha/share, FLOOR earned per day (and USD), pending PnL waiting to be collected, seat + bandwidth headroom, the next desk upgrade (cost and what it unlocks), each operator's payback in days at the current emission rate, and the halving countdown (emissions ~halve after it). These are FACTS and paybacks, not instructions — the agent decides. Ignores halving decay in payback (best case). Needs the wallet to have a desk.

address.description: 0x wallet to analyze

tools.name: get_strategy

tools.description: Everything needed to swap ETH↔FLOOR on Robinhood Chain: the Uniswap V3 router, WETH address, the FLOOR/WETH pool and its 1% fee tier, and the LIVE spot price (FLOOR per ETH) read from the pool. Note the pool is thin (~tens of $k liquidity) so large buys move the price hard — size accordingly. Read this before prepare_swap_eth_for_floor, or to construct/verify a swap yourself.

tools.description: Build the UNSIGNED Uniswap V3 swap that buys FLOOR with WETH (exactInputSingle). Full buy flow is 3 signed steps: (1) prepare_wrap_eth, (2) approve WETH to the router [included as approveWeth when `from` is given and allowance is short], (3) this swap. amountOutMinimum is computed from the LIVE pool price minus your slippage, so you are protected from a bad fill — but VERIFY the numbers before signing; this spends real money and the pool is thin. Selling FLOOR for ETH is the reverse and not built here.

recipient.description: Address to receive the FLOOR (the signing wallet).

slippagePct.description: Max slippage tolerance in percent (default 2). amountOutMinimum = live quote × (1 − this).

description: Optimal Social Security claiming, in minutes. MySSAgent's free estimator takes a birth month and year and the full-retirement-age benefit from an SSA statement, and returns a benefit table for every claiming age still open, up to 70, with the breakeven age for waiting. Full retirement age is set by birth year, and every early-claiming reduction and delayed-retirement credit uses SSA's month-level factors. The numbers come from a deterministic calculation engine, not from the language model, so the same inputs always return the same answer. No account, no sign-up, and no Social Security number: the estimator never asks for one and turns away any request that contains one. Nothing sent to it is stored. Results are estimates, not financial advice. For a full analysis against an actual SSA earnings record, visit myssagent.com.

tools.description: Computes Social Security claiming-age figures from the person's birth month and year and their estimated benefit at full retirement age. As of today's date (Eastern Time) it returns only the claiming ages still available, from their current age up to 70, with each flagged as before or at-or-past full retirement age (FRA varies by birth year and can land between whole ages, such as 66 and 10 months for 1959). Each age shows SSA's month-level adjustment (5/9 of 1% per month for the first 36 months early, 5/12 of 1% beyond, and delayed-retirement credits of 2/3 of 1% per month) and the resulting monthly benefit. For the live choice it also returns, for claiming now versus each later age through 70, the cumulative breakeven age and the dollars forgone while waiting, and notes the retroactive-benefit window for someone past FRA, so every figure is already computed in the output. Inputs are user-provided; the day of birth is never requested, no SSA data is accessed and nothing is stored. The output ends with its assumptions, a disclaimer, and source links (SSA's my Social Security page, MySSAgent's full-analysis and advisor pages). Directional estimate, not advice.

birth_month.description: The month the person was born, 1 (January) to 12 (December). Month and year only; the day of birth is not needed.

birth_year.description: The year the person was born (e.g. 1962).

fra_monthly_benefit.description: Their estimated monthly benefit at full retirement age, in dollars — shown on their SSA statement at ssa.gov/myaccount. If they only know a different age's figure, use that statement's FRA number, not the age-70 number.

married.description: Optional. Whether the person is married — spousal and survivor coordination can change the picture materially, which this estimator does not compute.

tools.name: estimate_claiming_strategy

Use this FIRST whenever the advisor refers to a client by name — the ids it returns are what get_client_report and run_client_analysis take. Read-only; nothing is changed.

tools.description: For financial advisors (requires a MySSAgent advisor account — sign in with your myssagent.com advisor account when prompted). Returns the stored Social Security claiming analysis for one of YOUR clients: optimal and recommended claiming ages, the benefit-by-claiming-age table computed from their actual earnings record, lifetime values, survivor analysis when present, and risk flags. Requires the advisor_client_id from list_clients — call that first when you only have a name. Read-only; the branded PDF report is generated from the dashboard link in the output.

tools.description: For financial advisors (requires a MySSAgent advisor account — sign in with your myssagent.com advisor account when prompted). Re-runs the full MySSAgent engine for one of YOUR clients on the earnings record and household data already on file, then stores the refreshed results. Use after an engine update or when the advisor asks for fresh numbers. It cannot add a new client or ingest an SSA statement — new clients are provisioned in the advisor dashboard. Requires the advisor_client_id from list_clients. For pay-per-client accounts, re-runs are included while a household's 12-month coverage is active. This updates the client's stored analysis (it does not delete source data).

description:
# Shopee MCP

Connect your AI assistant to Shopee marketplace data via [SEA MCP](https://seamcp.com/shopee) — search shops, listings and the category tree across 8 Shopee markets through the Model Context Protocol.

Markets: Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan and Brazil. Prices stay in each market's own currency.

## What it's for

- **Market research** — size up a category or niche in any market: who the biggest sellers are, how many followers and listings they have, and how their ratings compare.
- **Competitor analysis** — benchmark rival shops on followers, catalogue size, rating, response rate, cancellation rate and how long they've been selling.
- **Finding regional stores** — list sellers in a specific city, district or province (e.g. every shop in Bandung or Surabaya), or the sellers shipping from a given location.
- **Supplier and reseller sourcing** — find manufacturers, distributors and wholesalers on Shopee by product, brand or region.
- **B2B lead generation** — build prospect lists of merchants by region, size and seller tier (Shopee Mall, Preferred+, verified) for logistics, payments, SaaS or agency outreach.
- **Company due diligence (KYC / KYB)** — link a shop to its legal entity through the registered business number (Indonesian NIB, Thai company registration) and check its address and trading history.
- **Brand protection** — find unofficial resellers and look-alike shops selling your brand, and compare them against your official store.
- **Pricing and discount research** — compare listing prices, original prices and discount levels across sellers and markets.
- **Product and trend research** — spot best-selling products by units sold and monthly sales within a category or brand.
- **Cross-border expansion** — compare the same category across Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil before entering a new market.
- **Academic and economic research** — study e-commerce seller distribution and SME activity across the regi

tools.description:
Search Shopee shops. Filters are ANDed. Defaults to most followers.

Shops are complete. Some shops have no username. The latest data point is 22 Sep 2026.

Use registrationNumber for a legal id (Indonesia NIB, Thailand company registration). Use username for an exact handle. Street, city, and district are substrings. City is stored with a prefix such as "KOTA JAKARTA UTARA" or "KAB. TANGERANG"; province for Indonesia is uppercase, e.g. "DKI JAKARTA". followerCount and ratingStar are indexed — set minFollowers or minRating when scanning a market. sortBy is any ShopeeShop column.

Returns { data, total, page, limit }. Each row includes a Shopee url.

city.description: City substring.

country.description: Market: id Indonesia, my Malaysia, th Thailand, vn Vietnam, ph Philippines, sg Singapore, tw Taiwan, br Brazil, mx Mexico, co Colombia, cl Chile.

openedFrom.description: Shop opened on or after, YYYY-MM-DD.

openedTo.description: Shop opened on or before, YYYY-MM-DD.

query.description: Substring on name, username, or registration number.

tools.name: Shopee_search_shops

tools.description: Fetch one Shopee shop by id, or by country plus username. Shops are complete. Some shops have no username, so a username lookup can miss a shop that exists; use id when you have it. The latest data point is 22 Sep 2026. Includes address, ratings, and the top stored products by units sold. Product coverage is not complete yet: embedded products are only the listings we have loaded, not the shop's full catalog. itemCount is the shop's total listing count on Shopee. Returns { data: null } when missing.

country.description: Market: id Indonesia, my Malaysia, th Thailand, vn Vietnam, ph Philippines, sg Singapore, tw Taiwan, br Brazil, mx Mexico, co Colombia, cl Chile.

id.description: Numeric Shopee id, as a string.

productLimit.description: Top products to embed. 0 omits them.

tools.name: Shopee_get_shop

tools.description:
Search Shopee listings. Filters are ANDed. Defaults to most units sold. Prices are in the market currency (IDR, MYR, THB, VND, PHP, SGD, TWD, BRL, MXN, COP, CLP), not converted.

Product coverage is not complete yet. Totals and soldCount rankings only cover stored listings, not the full Shopee catalog. A shop with no matches may still sell the item.

Pass shopId when you already have a shop. category matches a category name and includes its child categories. price and soldCount are indexed.

Returns { data, total, page, limit }. When category is set, matchedCategories lists the named matches (children are searched but not all listed).

category.description: Category name. Also searches direct child categories.

country.description: Market: id Indonesia, my Malaysia, th Thailand, vn Vietnam, ph Philippines, sg Singapore, tw Taiwan, br Brazil, mx Mexico, co Colombia, cl Chile.

inStock.description: true = still listed for sale, false = sold out.

query.description: Substring on product name or brand.

tools.name: Shopee_search_products

tools.description: Fetch one Shopee product by item id, with its shop and category. Price is in the market currency. Product coverage is not complete yet, so { data: null } means the listing is missing or not loaded.

id.description: Numeric Shopee id, as a string.

country.description: Market: id Indonesia, my Malaysia, th Thailand, vn Vietnam, ph Philippines, sg Singapore, tw Taiwan, br Brazil, mx Mexico, co Colombia, cl Chile.

tools.name: list_tools

tools.description: Return the input fields, filterable columns, and response shape for the named tools.

detail.description: How much schema to return. `summary` (default) is the common filter columns plus a pointer to the rest; `detailed` is the full filterable-column list plus an example response.

group.description: Expand ONE projectable group (or dotted prefix) to its exact `fields` sub-paths, for narrow projection. When set, the response is just that group's leaf paths per tool — call this only for a group you intend to project narrowly.

names.description: Tool names to describe (max 50; duplicates are ignored).

tools.name: get_schema

tools.description: Run a plain-JavaScript script that drives Crustdata — the only I/O is `const r = await callTool(name, params)`. The `code` field carries the contract; read crustdata://catalog for the rules and a section index.

budget.description: Optional context budget + client capabilities, injected by a client hook. `maxOutputBytes`/`maxOutputTokens` size the return when `maxOutputBytes` (top-level) is absent (tighten only); `clientCapabilities.fileWrite` tells the overflow `truncated` note whether this client can persist pages to disk.

clientCapabilities.description: Capabilities of the calling client, injected by a client hook. `fileWrite` tells the overflow `truncated` note whether this client can persist pages to disk.

fileWrite.description: If true, the overflow `truncated` note tells the model this client can persist pages to disk.

freeTokens.description: Remaining tokens in the client's context window, injected by a client hook. Informational; the server sizes the return from `maxOutputBytes`/`maxOutputTokens`, not this field.

maxOutputBytes.description: Cap this run's returned value to ~this many bytes when top-level `maxOutputBytes` is absent; over it the result comes back as a head + a `truncated` note. Only tightens the server default, never loosens it.

maxOutputTokens.description: Alternate size cap in tokens; used as `maxOutputTokens * 4` bytes when neither top-level nor budget `maxOutputBytes` is set. Only tightens the server default.

checkpoint_every_ms.description: How often this run saves recoverable progress, in ms. Set it BELOW your client's cancellation timeout — the calls a cancelled run already dispatched are billed either way, and a committed checkpoint is what lets you resume instead of re-paying. Cursor cancels at a hard 60s; other clients run longer. Only tightens the server default, never loosens it, and cannot be disabled from here: progress you were charged for is not yours to throw away. Rarely needed — the default already sits under the tightest known client ceiling.

code.description:
The script. It MUST begin with a source-labeled query comment — `// user query: <the user's request in their own words>` (e.g. `// user query: find engineering leaders at Stripe and get their work emails`) when this run serves the user's literal ask, and/or `// model query: <what THIS run does>` when it's your own derived query rather than the user's words. At least one is required (a run/session issues many execute calls — label the call carrying the user's ask `user`, your follow-up calls `model`); recorded for operators, never shown to the user. A script with no labeled comment is rejected before running (verification_failed, zero spend) and must be resubmitted with the line prepended. Use `return` to send back a value.

Write a plain-JavaScript body. Author it against the TypeScript-typed tool surface from get_schema, but write NO type annotations — a `: Type`/`as`/generic fails the whole run at parse, zero spend. The ONLY I/O is `const r = await callTool(name, params)` → `{ok:true,data}|{ok:false,status,errorType,message}`; always branch on `r.ok` (or `unwrap(await callTool(...))` to throw instead of silently proceeding on empty data). A toolkit is preloaded in the sandbox — no import, and (except `paginate` and `parallelMap`) do NOT await it: query builder (eq, and_, or_, gte, in_, any_of, field, chunk), result shapers (project, pick, compact, paginate, parallelMap, firstArray, unwrap), response accessors (profileUrl, currentCompanyIds, businessEmails), introspection (keys, shape). await only callTool, sleep, paginate, and parallelMap. Progress survives a bad run: when the run times out OR fails (a thrown error, a crashed pipeline, a client cancelling), the result carries a `partial`. The host fills it automatically with the results of every tool call that completed — you are billed for those either way, so they come back for you to resume from. `checkpoint(accumulator)` (synchronous) additionally saves YOUR value — call it after each costly stage when your own accumulator is what you want back, and it takes precedence over the automatic capture. If the captured rows overflow the size cap, `partial.resume` still carries each paginated call's `next_cursor` (and any `batch_id`), so you continue from where the run stopped instead of re-walking it — no paid re-run to recover it. Recovery is NOT automatic: pass the failed run's `partial` back to the next execute as `inputs` (the script reads it as `inputs.partial`) and write that script to skip the stages it already completed. Run INDEPENDENT calls (bulk enrich/lookup, per-entity sub-queries) concurrently with parallelMap instead of an await-loop. Return the smallest projection you need. Before a long or expensive script, `dry_run: true` rehearses it against fixtures for zero credits and reports where it breaks — a lint, not a check that the answer is right. Its values come from committed fixtures rather than from the API, so they are sample data with no bearing on the real answer (crustdata://catalog/dry-run).

dry_run.description: Rehearse instead of running: every callTool is answered from a committed response fixture, so the whole script executes for ZERO credits and zero network. Returns where it broke, the tool calls it would make, and the SHAPE of what it would return, rather than data: the values are committed fixtures rather than API responses, so they are sample data and carry no information about the real answer. It is a lint, not a rehearsal of the answer: it cannot tell you a result is wrong, and cannot see anything that depends on real values (a 403 on your plan, a 429, an empty result set). Worth it before a long or expensive script; skip it for a one-call lookup, where just running it costs the same.

inputs.description: Data made available to the script as the `inputs` global (e.g. `inputs.ids`), not interpolated into code. Carry IDs/cursors from a prior run forward instead of re-fetching.

maxOutputBytes.description: Cap this run's returned value to ~this many bytes; over it the result comes back as a head + a `truncated` note. Only tightens the server default, never loosens it.

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.

Connect directly (Streamable HTTP): https://knownfix-backend-28.b-hash88.deno.net/mcp

Using a Smithery proxy? Replace only the KnownFix entry before October 31, 2026. Smithery run.tools and server.smithery.ai connections shut down that day. No Smithery API key is needed for the direct connection; do not transfer proxy credentials. Migration steps: https://b-hash88.github.io/knownfix/mcp-connect.html#smithery-migration

Search developer fixes, retrieve six free workflow skills, or use three browser-local tools. Install the portable SKILL.md toolkit and offline response-inspection/retry-planning commands from the repository. Start with get_overview for the complete catalog. Ten scoped paid services; current pricing and authorization terms are on the website. Setup: https://b-hash88.github.io/knownfix/mcp-connect.html

tools.description: Use this first for an exact error or distinctive symptom. Returns up to three confident ranked matches. A free top match includes the full fix. A paid top match includes a free diagnosis, confidence and compatibility, dollar price, signed USDC/Base Pay and exact-ETH rails, and one pay-and-redeem action; do not call get_offer. Use list_catalog to browse, get_fix only with a known id or payment proof, and request_fix only after an honest miss.

query.description: Preserve the exact error code and distinctive text; add tool or runtime context needed to disambiguate it. Omit credentials, tokens, private hostnames, and private paths.

tools.name: search_fixes

tools.description: Ask for a fix this store does not have yet. If we already stock it (matched on either field) you get the id straight back and no ticket. Otherwise you get a ticket; when we stock THAT fix, check_request returns it to you FREE, once. A ticket only ever redeems a fix created after the request: fixes that already existed when you asked are not free, whatever the request said. No contact details are collected. Set publish: true ONLY if the text may appear on a public wanted board — never include secrets, tokens, internal hostnames, or file paths.

publish.description: Allow this text on the public board (default false)

signature.description: The exact error text you are stuck on

tools.name: request_fix

tools.description: Check a private ticket from request_fix. Returns pending, declined, not-eligible, redeemed, or the full fix free once an eligible new fix is stocked. This call may atomically consume the ticket's one-time delivery, so save the returned body. Use get_fix when you already have a catalog id; do not create another request while this ticket is pending.

ticket.description: Private req_ ticket returned once by request_fix. Reuse it unchanged and never publish it. A stocked eligible result can be redeemed only once, so save the returned fix body.

tools.name: check_request
