tools.description: Compare KnownFix's $49 website first-look report and deeper website, public-codebase, agent-commerce, and release-pipeline reviews. Returns bounded scope, deliverables, delivery time, limitations, sample-report links where available, and exact prices. Call order_service only after choosing a service and confirming authority over the public target.
tools.name: list_services

tools.description: Create a private ticket and signed Base USDC/ETH checkout for one published professional service. Accepts public HTTPS websites or public GitHub repositories only. Never include credentials, tokens, secrets, private repository URLs, or confidential data. The returned svc_ ticket is shown once and is the only report-retrieval credential.

authorizationConfirmed.description: Must be true: confirms the target is public and the requester is authorized to commission a passive, non-destructive review.

notes.description: Optional review focus. Never include credentials, tokens, secrets, private URLs, or confidential data.

publishTarget.description: Optional explicit consent to show the target and status in the public work queue. Defaults to false.

targetUrl.description: Public HTTPS website or exact public GitHub repository URL. Do not include credentials, query parameters, or fragments.

tools.name: order_service

tools.description: Check a private service order by its svc_ ticket. With paymentTx and paymentOffer, atomically confirms exactly one matching Base payment and moves the order into review. Without payment fields, returns current status; once complete, it returns the private Markdown report and SHA-256 digest. Keep the ticket and signed offer private.

paymentOffer.description: Matching private signed offer returned by order_service. Omit after payment is confirmed.

paymentTx.description: Base Pay UserOperation hash for USDC or mined Base transaction hash for ETH. Omit after payment is confirmed.

ticket.description: Private bearer ticket returned once by order_service.

tools.description: Readiness audit of any agent-facing URL: MCP handshake, CORS, discovery docs (llms.txt, mcp.json), and payment-offer behaviour. First call with url alone for the FREE grade and failing-check list. For the full findings and remediations, call get_offer with productType "audit" and productId "conformance-report", pay, then call audit_endpoint again with the same url plus paymentTx and paymentOffer. This tool both previews and redeems the paid report; no separate delivery tool is needed.

External stylesheets are counted but not fetched. Use audit_endpoint instead for MCP, CORS, discovery, and payment readiness.

description:
The official JustGains MCP server. Let your AI agent build and save workouts, read your training history and progress, search the exercise library, plan routes, and log meals and bodyweight in your JustGains account.

- **Workouts**: generate a workout from a plain-language request, or create and edit one with exact exercises, sets, reps, loads and set types.
- **History and progress**: completed workouts, every set of a lift with personal bests, top exercises, weekly recap, streaks and consistency.
- **Programs and routes**: browse, create, start or leave multi-week programs; plan road-snapped run, ride, walk or hike routes.
- **Food and bodyweight**: log a whole meal in one call with disclosed estimates, read the diary and daily macros, remove entries, log bodyweight.

Sign in with your JustGains account over OAuth. Exercise search and workout generation also work without an account.

tools.description: Display a workout in the preview editor by its ID

workoutId.description: The UUID of the workout to display

tools.name: show_workout

tools.description: Generate a workout based on a natural language description. Examples: "30 minute leg workout", "Upper body workout with dumbbells", "Full body HIIT circuit", "Beginner chest and triceps workout"

muscleGroups.description: Optional muscle group codes to focus on

prompt.description: Description of the workout to generate (e.g., "20 minute leg workout with dumbbells")

tools.name: generate_workout

tools.description: Get the signed-in user's training progress (daily gains, workout volume, steps, active days) over a timeframe. Provide startDate/endDate (YYYY-MM-DD) or a trailing number of days. Defaults to the last 30 days. Requires the user to have connected their JustGains account.

days.description: Alternatively, the number of most recent days to include (e.g. 7, 30, 90).

endDate.description: End of the window (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.

startDate.description: Start of the window (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 30 days before endDate.

tools.name: get_progress

tools.description: Search the JustGains exercise library by name (optionally filtered by muscle group or equipment). Returns exercise codes and supported measurements to use when building or updating a workout.

equipment.description: Optional equipment code to filter by.

muscleGroup.description: Optional muscle group code to filter by (e.g. CHEST).

query.description: Exercise name to search, e.g. "bench press", "romanian deadlift".

tools.name: search_exercises

tools.description: Create a workout in the signed-in user's JustGains account, saved under their own creator profile. Provide a title and an ordered list of exercises (by code from search_exercises, or by name to auto-resolve); each exercise can include sets with reps/weight/RPE. Use this for precise, user-specified workouts (use generate_workout for AI-generated ones).

exercise.description: Exercise code (e.g. BARBELL.BENCH.PRESS) from search_exercises, or a name to auto-resolve.

type.description: normal (default), warmup, dropset, myorep, or failure.

tools.name: create_workout

tools.description: Update an existing workout in the user's JustGains account. Provide the workoutId plus any of: new title, new description, or a replacement list of exercises. Call show_workout first if you need the current exercises before modifying them.

description.description: New workout description. Omit to keep the current one.

exercises.description: If provided, REPLACES the workout's exercise list.

exercise.description: Exercise code (e.g. BARBELL.BENCH.PRESS) from search_exercises, or a name to auto-resolve.

type.description: normal (default), warmup, dropset, myorep, or failure.

title.description: New workout title. Omit to keep the current one.

workoutId.description: The UUID of the workout to update.

tools.name: update_workout

tools.description: List the signed-in user's most recent workouts (title, date, duration, total volume, sets, reps, exercise count). Use to discuss recent training, consistency, and volume trends.
tools.name: get_workout_history

tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific exercise by its code. Returns the exercise name, instructions, equipment, muscles worked, and measurements.

exerciseCode.description: The unique code of the exercise (e.g., 'BARBELL-BENCH-PRESS', 'BARBELL-SQUAT')

tools.name: get_exercise_details

tools.description: Get the CURRENT user's workout-log history (workouts they actually performed and recorded). Use this whenever the user asks about THEIR OWN workouts - 'my last workout', 'what did I do this week', 'how much did I bench Monday', 'show my recent sessions', 'workouts in March', 'last summer's training'. For any historical timeframe, pass `since` and/or `until` (ISO-8601). The tool will paginate deeper automatically until the requested window is covered (or `maxLogs` is reached). For RANKED questions ('what was my best workout', 'longest session ever', 'highest-volume day'), set `rankBy` ('volume' | 'duration') and `topN`. The tool then sweeps the window, computes the metric per log, and returns the top N logs sorted by that metric instead of newest-first. Returns logs with id, title, date, exercise count, and a per-exercise summary of sets/reps/weight; when ranking, each log also carries totalVolumeKg/totalVolumeDisplay and durationSeconds. Returns an error if the user is not signed in.

maxLogs.description: Hard cap on logs returned when scanning a date window (default 100, max 500).

page.description: Page number (1-based, default 1). Ignored when `since`/`until` are set.

pageSize.description: Logs per page (default 10, max 50). Acts as a result cap when filtering by date.

rankBy.description: How to order results. 'recent' (default) is newest-first by createdAt. 'volume' ranks by total tonnage (sum of weight×reps across all sets). 'duration' ranks by `WorkoutLogDuration` (seconds). Set this for 'best workout', 'highest-volume day', 'longest session' questions.

since.description: Optional ISO-8601 lower-bound: only logs with createdAt >= since are returned.

topN.description: When `rankBy` is set, return only the top N logs by that metric (default 5, max 25). Ignored when `rankBy` is unset or 'recent'.

until.description: Optional ISO-8601 upper-bound: only logs with createdAt <= until are returned.

tools.name: get_my_workout_logs

tools.description: Get the CURRENT user's recorded history for a SINGLE exercise (by exerciseCode), plus their personal best. Use when the user asks 'show my bench press progression', 'how heavy have I squatted', 'what's my best deadlift', 'when did I last do pull-ups'. You usually want to call search_exercises FIRST to resolve a name to a code. For ANY HISTORICAL TIMEFRAME ('my bench in 2024', 'squats last summer'), pass `since` and/or `until` (ISO-8601). The tool sweeps deeper pages automatically and returns only sessions in the window: DO NOT page manually. Use `maxSessions` to cap the scan. Returns history items (workout id, completed-at, sets) sorted newest-first by default, plus a personalBest summary if any has been recorded. Requires sign-in.

exerciseCode.description: Uppercase exercise code, e.g. 'BARBELL-BENCH-PRESS'. Use search_exercises if unsure.

maxSessions.description: Hard cap on sessions returned when scanning a date window (default 100, max 500).

page.description: Page number (1-based, default 1). Ignored when `since`/`until` are set.

since.description: Optional ISO-8601 lower bound: only sessions completed at or after this time are returned.

until.description: Optional ISO-8601 upper bound: only sessions completed at or before this time are returned.

tools.name: get_my_exercise_history

tools.description: Search the workout-program catalog. Returns paginated programs with title, description, total weeks/days, rating, creator, and a public link. Use when the user asks about available programs ('show me programs for hypertrophy', 'find a beginner program', 'what programs do you have'). Optional filters: search keyword, creatorId.

creatorId.description: Optional creator profile id (GUID) to limit results to one creator

page.description: Page number (1-based, default 1)

search.description: Optional keyword to filter program titles/descriptions

tools.name: search_workout_programs

tools.description: Get a workout program (template) by id, including its weeks and days. Use after search_workout_programs or get_my_workout_programs to dig into a specific program. Set includeData=false for a lightweight summary that omits per-day workout content.

includeData.description: Include the full week/day breakdown (default true).

tools.name: get_workout_program

tools.description: Update the CURRENT user's enrollment on a workout program. Use to start, abandon, or complete a program: 'start this program', 'I'm done with PPL', 'abandon the cut program'. Requires the program id (use search_workout_programs to find it). Action must be one of: start | abandon | complete. Note: 'start' uses the Purchasing status, matching the existing API behavior.
tools.name: set_my_program_engagement

tools.description: Create a brand-new multi-week/multi-day workout PROGRAM for the user and save it to their account. You write the FULL program out as plain text in `programText`: a title, then each week and day with that day's exercises and their sets × reps (add weight or RPE when relevant). Rest days can be written as 'Rest'. The text is parsed into a structured program (real exercises are matched automatically) and saved. Use this whenever the user asks you to build / create / make / design a training PROGRAM, a multi-week or multi-day plan (PPL, full-body split, 5x5, a cut block, etc.). For a single one-off workout use generate_workout instead. If the user pasted their own program, pass it through verbatim.

programText.description: The complete program written as plain text: a title line, then each week and day with the day's exercises and sets × reps (e.g. 'Week 1, Day 1 Push: Barbell Bench Press 4x6, Overhead Press 3x8 ...'). Include rest days. Be specific and complete, this is what gets parsed.

programTitle.description: Optional explicit program title. If omitted, a title is taken/derived from the text.

tools.name: create_workout_program

tools.description: Generate a real, road-and-path-snapped ROUTE (a plannable run / ride / walk / hike path) starting and ending at the user's location, and save it to their Routes tab. Use when the user asks you to build / make / plan a route, a running loop, a bike ride, etc. Use startLat/startLng from the app-data block's current location when present, or coordinates the user explicitly gives; NEVER guess them. If neither is available, OMIT startLat/startLng and the route starts from the user's last known training location (the start of their most recent GPS activity or saved route). Before calling, make sure you know the activity type and the distance they want (ask if they haven't said). The generated route follows actual streets and paths and lands close to the requested distance.

activityType.description: What the route is for. 'ride' uses cycling roads; the rest use walking/running paths.

direction.description: Optional compass direction to head in. Omit for a sensible random direction.

name.description: Short friendly route name, e.g. '5K Morning Loop'. Omit to auto-name.

routeShape.description: loop = a circuit back to the start (default); out_and_back = straight out to a turnaround point and back the same way.

startLat.description: Start latitude. Only pass a real value (app-data current location or user-given); omit to fall back to the user's last known training location.

startLng.description: Start longitude. Only pass a real value; omit to fall back to the user's last known training location.

tools.name: create_route

tools.description: Get the CURRENT user's bodyweight log (entries plus summary: current, lowest, highest). Use whenever the user asks about their bodyweight: 'what do I weigh now', 'how much have I lost', 'show my weight trend', 'when did I last weigh in', 'what was my lightest'. For ANY HISTORICAL TIMEFRAME ('what did I weigh in March', 'last summer', 'between Jan 1 and Feb 14'), pass `since` and/or `until` (ISO-8601). Summary stats (current/lowest/highest) are returned for BOTH the full history and, when a window is set, the windowed slice. Optional `limit` truncates the entry list. Requires sign-in.

limit.description: Max recent entries to return (default 30, max 200).

since.description: Optional ISO-8601 lower bound: only entries recorded at or after this time are included.

until.description: Optional ISO-8601 upper bound: only entries recorded at or before this time are included.

tools.name: get_my_weight_history

tools.description: Record a new bodyweight entry for the CURRENT user. Pass `weightKg` (kilograms) OR `weightLbs` (pounds), the tool converts lbs → kg before storage. If the user spoke in pounds, prefer `weightLbs` so the round-trip is exact. `recordedAt` is optional ISO-8601 (defaults to now). Valid stored range: 25kg–500kg (≈55–1100 lbs); the API rejects values outside this.

notes.description: Optional notes the user mentioned (mood, time of day, etc.).

recordedAt.description: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp. Defaults to now (UTC).

weightKg.description: Bodyweight in kilograms (25–500). Provide this OR `weightLbs`, not both.

weightLbs.description: Bodyweight in pounds (≈55–1100). Provide this OR `weightKg`, not both. The tool converts to kg.

tools.name: log_my_weight

tools.description: Read the CURRENT user's food diary, daily totals, targets, local date/timezone and last 30 days of foods (up to 100 entries). Call when the user wants to see their diary, when a request depends on a past day ('same as yesterday'), or to find entries to correct or remove that no recent food result returned. Routine logging does not need it: log_my_food resolves the local date and checks recent entries on the backend. Never infer that a planned meal was eaten.

entryDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD local diary date; defaults to the user's today.

tools.name: get_my_food_diary

tools.description: Search the cached food catalog and matching recent diary entries. This never waits on an external nutrition provider. Use only when the user asks to find or compare foods. For logging, call log_my_food directly with estimates instead. Results contain up to five identity-checked candidates and three possible variants; missing results do not prevent logging an estimate. Preserve brand and raw/cooked preparation.
tools.name: search_foods

tools.description: Log foods the CURRENT user actually ate in one call. Call this directly: do not search_foods, browse, research nutrition, or read the diary first. Send every food/drink with quantityGrams and a quick estimatedMacros fallback for the whole portion; round estimates rather than researching exact numbers. The API checks recent foods and the cached catalog, prefers reliable nutrition, and labels estimate fallbacks. Preserve brand and raw/cooked preparation. Use servingQuantity/servingUnit for counts and portionEstimated=true for guessed weights. Briefly disclose assumptions; do not ask for missing flavor or grams. Use a new requestId per meal and keep it unchanged on retries. Follow-up corrections reuse diaryEntryId and expectedUpdatedAt from the last result, keep the serving count, and omit grams to recalculate a corrected catalog serving. Only read the diary for a past-day reference, an explicit repeat, or a correction/removal whose ID is unavailable. Use recentEntryId only for an explicit repeat. After success, give a short confirmation; do not call another tool to verify the save or repeat the card. Never log plans or hypothetical meals.

entryDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD in the user's timezone; defaults to their today.

assumptionNote.description: Briefly disclose assumed variety, brand or serving weight. Saved visibly with the food; omit once those details are confirmed.

brand.description: The user's brand, or an assumed brand explicitly disclosed in assumptionNote.

diaryEntryId.description: For a correction only: the existing diary entry to replace, never a new UUID. Omit for a new food.

estimatedMacros.description: Include your best fallback totals for this entire portion in the first call, never per 100g. Do not look up nutrition first. Reliable catalog values take precedence; otherwise these values are saved as estimated.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Required with diaryEntryId: copy updatedAt (or createdAt when updatedAt is absent) from a fresh diary read. A stale correction fails without adding a duplicate; reread before retrying.

name.description: Food identity including preparation, e.g. cooked brown rice.

quantityGrams.description: Total grams for this portion. Include your best estimate without searching; set portionEstimated=true if the user did not supply the weight. A known catalog serving can replace estimated grams.

recentEntryId.description: An entry from the user's recent diary when they explicitly mean the same food/portion. Omit grams to reuse its portion.

servingUnit.description: Catalog serving label, or a display unit when grams are supplied.

loggedAt.description: Time eaten with UTC offset, if known.

requestId.description: New UUID per meal, unchanged on retry.

tools.name: log_my_food

tools.description: Remove foods the CURRENT user asks to delete from their diary, e.g. 'remove those crackers', 'I did not eat that', or 'delete breakfast'. Identify the exact saved entries from the user's request and the latest food result (log, removal or diary read); call get_my_food_diary for the relevant day only if no recent result has them. Pass their diaryEntryId and expectedUpdatedAt exactly as that result gives them. Remove only requested entries; ask which one if the target is ambiguous. For an entire meal, pass all entries in that meal, not the whole day. Removing one pack from a two-pack entry is a portion correction with log_my_food, not removal of the entire row. The API removes the batch atomically, updates day totals and syncs deletion to mobile. Repeating the same IDs is safe. This removes diary entries, never catalog foods. Do not call unless the user requested removal.

diaryEntryId.description: Exact saved entry ID from get_my_food_diary.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Copy updatedAt, or createdAt if absent, from the latest diary read.

tools.name: remove_my_food

tools.description: Fetch the CURRENT user's full profile snapshot: name, email, bio, measurement system, timezone, plus private meta (age/birth date, height, gender, experience level, fitness goals, injury tracking, baseline weight). Use whenever the user asks 'what's my profile', 'how old am I', 'what's my height', 'what experience level am I set as', 'what goals do I have'. Pair with `update_my_profile` if they want to change any of these.
tools.name: get_my_profile

tools.description: Bundle a one-call snapshot of the CURRENT user's recent training: count of workout logs in the last `days` (default 7), per-muscle-group recovery data, weight delta vs `days` ago, and the most recent log id. Use for "how was my week", "quick recap", "how am I doing". For HISTORICAL questions ('how was my week ending June 1, 2024'), pass `endDate` (ISO-8601), the window becomes (endDate - days, endDate) instead of anchoring to today. Saves the agent from chaining get_my_workout_logs + get_my_recovery_analytics + get_my_weight_history.

endDate.description: Optional ISO-8601 anchor date, the window ends at this date instead of now. Use for retrospective summaries like 'how was my week ending Mar 30, 2024'.

tools.name: summarize_my_week

tools.description: Analyze the CURRENT user's workout consistency over a window: longest streak, current streak (today/yesterday inclusive), distinct training days, total logs, and average workouts per week. Use for 'how's my consistency', 'what's my streak', 'how often have I trained lately'. Default window 60 days, max 365. For HISTORICAL consistency questions ('how consistent was I in 2024'), pass `endDate` (ISO-8601), the window becomes (endDate: days, endDate). Current-streak only counts when the window ends today/yesterday.

endDate.description: Optional ISO-8601 anchor date, the window ends here instead of today. Use for retrospective consistency like 'how consistent was I in 2024'.

tools.name: analyze_my_consistency

tools.description: Cross-exercise leaderboard for the CURRENT user. Use whenever the user asks about their TOP / MOST / HEAVIEST exercises across the board: 'what's my most used exercise', 'top 3 lifts', 'heaviest exercises', 'what do I lift the most'. Scans the user's workout logs (default 365 days, capped at `maxLogsScanned`) and returns three rankings in one call: byFrequency (session + set count), byMaxWeight (peak single-set weight), and byVolume (total tonnage). Each entry includes the exerciseCode + name so the agent can drill into a specific lift via get_my_exercise_history. For HISTORICAL questions ('most-used in 2024', 'top lifts last summer'), pass `since`/`until` (ISO-8601). Use `topN` to widen/narrow each list (default 5, max 25). Requires sign-in.

lookbackDays.description: When neither `since` nor `until` is set, how far back to scan (default 365, max 1825).

maxLogsScanned.description: Hard cap on logs scanned across the window (default 200, max 500). Bump for long histories.

since.description: Optional ISO-8601 lower bound: only logs with createdAt >= since are scanned.

topN.description: How many entries to return per ranking (default 5, max 25).

until.description: Optional ISO-8601 upper bound: only logs with createdAt <= until are scanned.

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.
tools.name: marketplace

description:
Manawa Terminal gives AI agents a finance research desk backed by live data,
with every figure traceable to its source.

Research: prices, company financials and filings, earnings results and call
transcripts, analyst estimates, FX, crypto, commodities, macro indicators,
ETF holdings, insider and institutional activity, and news across 34 data
domains and 10,000+ tickers. Ask in plain language; answers come back with
the underlying source attached.

Workspace: watchlists you can screen by financial criteria, portfolios with
positions, transactions and mark-to-market P&L, price alerts, a versioned
research library that keeps revision history across sessions, and a daily
journal.

Multi-currency portfolios hold cost basis at the trade-date exchange rate and
mark to market at today's, so foreign holdings show the currency effect
separately from the underlying price move.

Sign in with your Manawa account through OAuth. No API keys to paste. A free
tier is available.

tools.description:
Search financial data and return an answer with an inline widget.

    Covers stocks, macro, forex, crypto, commodities, earnings, technicals,
    and related market questions. Pass the user's question in `query` without
    rephrasing.

    To screen a named watchlist or portfolio, call list_watchlists or
    list_portfolios first, then pass the symbols here with filter criteria in
    `query`.

    Exclusive modes when a Deep Dive exists:
      focus=ai + section=… → narrative section
      focus=raw + source=… → thin data slice
      focus=catalog → list available Deep Dives

    Args:
        query: The user's financial question
        symbols: Optional ticker universe to screen (e.g. from list_watchlists)
        section: Optional Deep Dive section (competition, valuation, thesis,
            forecast, analyst_consensus, people, financials, earnings,
            technicals, overview, moves)
        focus: Optional exclusive mode: ai | raw | auto | catalog
        source: Optional thin raw slice when focus=raw (comparison_peers,
            price_targets, consensus, quote, key_financials, …)

Unknown fields are null, never guessed. Not a contact or CRM record. Price: $0.10 USDC on Base per call via x402; this MCP call returns payment instructions and the paid HTTP route POST /v1/basic returns the brief. Read-only.

Every item cites its source. Price: $0.75 USDC on Base per call via x402; this MCP call returns payment instructions and the paid HTTP route POST /v1/enriched returns the record. Read-only.

description:
Connect an MCP-compatible client to https://0bull.net/mcp. 0bull Phone Farm manages posting accounts on TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube, publishes videos as submissions, and exposes direct controls for granted physical phones. Available operations include account management, device commands, taps and swipes, screenshots, OCR, named macros, and GUI-agent tasks. Billing tools can return approval links for phone rentals and phone-count changes.

The server uses OAuth, has no token to copy, and scopes every call to the authenticated user's accounts and phone grants. Phone and platform work is asynchronous. Poll the returned account or submission to observe the final state.

tools.description: List the authenticated user's posting accounts on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, newest first, 50 per page. Every platform is included unless `platform` narrows it to one.

page.description: Page number to fetch (defaults to 1). Each page holds up to 50 accounts.

platform.description: Only accounts on this platform: "tiktok", "instagram" or "youtube". Omit for every platform, merged newest-first.

tools.name: list-accounts-tool

tools.description: Fetch a single posting account the authenticated user is allowed to view, on any platform: TikTok, Instagram or YouTube.

account_id.description: ID of the account to fetch, on any platform.

tools.name: get-account-tool

tools.description: Link a posting account for the authenticated user on TikTok, Instagram or YouTube; platform defaults to tiktok. The account must already be signed in on the phone at the given slot. YouTube also needs the Google account address (google_email).

google_email.description: The Google account address of this YouTube channel. Required for YouTube, rejected on every other platform.

notes.description: Free-form notes about this account. Optional.

platform.description: Where the account posts: "tiktok", "instagram" or "youtube". Defaults to "tiktok".

slot.description: Phone slot the account is bound to, given as the `slot` UUID from list-phones (its display name like "slot12" is not accepted). Required on TikTok, where a slot holds at most 4 accounts. Optional on Instagram and YouTube.

account_id.description: ID of the account to update, on any platform.

google_email.description: The Google account address of this YouTube channel. Only editable on YouTube; rejected on every other platform.

notes.description: Free-form notes about this account. Optional.

slot.description: Phone slot the account is bound to, given as the `slot` UUID from list-phones. Optional. A TikTok slot holds at most 4 accounts.

tools.name: update-account-tool

tools.description: Delete a posting account the authenticated user is allowed to manage, on any platform — TikTok, Instagram or YouTube. This removes the account from the farm; it does not delete the account on the platform itself.

account_id.description: ID of the account to delete, on any platform.

tools.description:
Send a device command to a farm phone.
The slot must be cast/live. Supported ops:
  - clipboard_set (text): set the phone clipboard
  - clipboard_get: read the phone clipboard back
  - open_url (url): open a URL / deep link
  - reboot: restart the phone
  - clear_photos: empty the camera roll
  - get_ip: report the phone's LAN IP
  - brightness (level): set screen brightness (0-1)
  - wifi / airplane / cellular / flashlight (on): toggle the named radio/flashlight
Op-specific fields (text, url, level, on) are only sent when provided.
Returns a run id. The run succeeds once the phone has run the command; for
get_ip and clipboard_get its result.value holds the IP or clipboard text.

on.description: Desired on/off state (for wifi, airplane, cellular, flashlight). Optional.

op.description: Command op: clipboard_set, clipboard_get, open_url, reboot, clear_photos, get_ip, brightness, wifi, airplane, cellular, flashlight.

slot.description: Phone slot to command, given as the `slot` UUID from list-phones (its display name like "slot12" is not accepted). Must be cast/live.

text.description: Text to set on the clipboard (for clipboard_set). Optional.

url.description: URL or deep link to open (for open_url). Optional.

tools.name: phone-command-tool

description:
> CreativeScope gives your AI agent live access to mobile-game advertising creative intelligence — compiled from publicly available ad placements across major SDK ad networks (AppLovin, Mintegral, Unity, ironSource, Vungle, Pangle, AdMob, TikTok and more).
>
> Built for UA and growth teams: search creatives by natural language, track Rising and Evergreen rankings, profile any advertiser or studio, find similar creatives (including by reference image), and get confidence-scored AI hook analysis your agent can reason over — not just another ad feed.
>
> Works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible client. Remote server, streamable HTTP, one API key. Free tier available.

tools.description: Search mobile game ad creatives by keyword or visual-description-like natural language. For an English request, send the original English concepts only. The service internally expands genre, hook, mood, art-style, and gameplay-mechanic concepts to Chinese source-label equivalents for retrieval; generated translations must not be inserted into the public request. Use this for finding UGC-style ads, winning creatives, opening hook examples, playable ads, and platform/country/genre slices. Results include the original creative asset as media_url when available. Creative tag fields are normalized to English in the result. Example: 'Find UGC-style match-3 video ads in the US.'

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, for example US, JP, KR, GB.

date_range.description: Date range. Supports last_7_days, last_30_days, last_90_days, or 'YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD'. Defaults to last_90_days.

format.description: Creative format: image, video, or playable.

genre.description: Game genre or sub-genre in the user's original language, for example match-3, puzzle, or SLG. Chinese source-label expansion is internal.

limit.description: Number of creatives to return. Maximum 20.

orientation.description: Optional creative orientation: portrait, landscape, or square. For video, this is derived from existing media width and height metadata.

platform.description: Ad platform filter. Supported values: facebook, instagram, messenger, audience_network, threads, admob, youtube, tiktok, mintegral, unity, applovin, ironsource, vungle, pangle.

query.description: Natural-language search query in the user's original language. Do not append generated Chinese translations to an English query; the service performs Chinese source-label expansion internally.

tools.name: search_creatives

tools.description: Get one creative's delivery metadata and English creative insights, including opening hook signals, scene descriptions, and creative patterns when available. Example: 'Why does this winning creative work?'

creative_id.description: Creative ID returned by search_creatives, find_similar_creatives, or get_creative_rankings.

tools.name: get_creative_detail

tools.description: Get global or genre-level rising creative rankings by day, week, or month, or evergreen creative rankings from the monthly snapshot; platform and country filters are not supported. Evergreen data is monthly only; day/week requests are normalized to month and disclosed in request_echo. Use this to answer what's rising this week, what evergreen creatives keep working, or which hook patterns repeat in a genre. For platform- or country-filtered discovery, use search_creatives and do not describe those results as an official rising or evergreen ranking. Creative tag fields are normalized to English in the result. Example: 'Which SLG creatives are rising this month?'

genre.description: Optional genre/category filter in the user's original language, for example match-3 or SLG. Chinese source-label expansion is internal.

limit.description: Number of ranked creatives to return. Maximum 20.

period.description: Ranking period: day, week, or month. Evergreen supports month only; other values are normalized to month.

type.description: Ranking type: rising or evergreen.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, for example US, JP, KR, GB.

date_range.description: Date range. Supports last_7_days, last_30_days, last_90_days, or 'YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD'. Defaults to last_7_days.

genre.description: Game genre or sub-genre in the user's original language, for example match-3 or puzzle. Chinese source-label expansion is internal.

tools.description: Submit a reference-image similarity search as an asynchronous job. Use this when the user provides a directly downloadable public HTTPS image URL. The URL must resolve to image bytes without login or hotlink protection; HTML pages, local paths, and base64 are not supported. The embedding provider validates image format and size asynchronously and returns IMAGE_FETCH_FAILED, INVALID_IMAGE, or EMBEDDING_MODEL_ERROR when processing cannot continue. Genre aliases are normalized internally. If a normalized genre produces no candidates, the completed result explicitly marks a visual-only fallback instead of silently returning an empty set. Example: 'Find ads visually similar to this reference image.'

country.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, for example US, JP, KR, GB.

format.description: Optional creative format: image, video, or playable.

genre.description: Optional game genre or sub-genre, for example SLG, match-3, puzzle, RPG. Aliases are normalized internally. If the normalized genre has no candidates, results may use an explicitly disclosed visual-only fallback.

image_url.description: Directly downloadable public HTTPS image URL. It must return image bytes without login or hotlink protection. Do not pass an HTML page, local path, base64, or expiring authenticated URL.

limit.description: Number of similar creatives to return when the job completes. Maximum 20.

platform.description: Optional platform filter, for example facebook, instagram, tiktok, youtube, admob.

tools.name: submit_reference_image_search

tools.description: Find visually similar creatives using the stored vector of an existing creative. For a concept without an ID, query selects an explainable seed from available creative metadata and then uses the same vector-neighbor search. For an English concept, send the original English terms only. The service resolves Chinese source-label equivalents internally before selecting the seed. Returns creative records ordered from most to least visually similar; low-similarity and near-duplicate results are excluded, and raw similarity scores are not exposed. If request_echo.seed_basis identifies a proxy seed, clearly disclose that limitation instead of presenting the results as an exact concept match. Example: 'Show variants of the toilet run viral creative concept.'

creative_id.description: Optional creative ID returned by search_creatives, get_creative_rankings, or get_reference_image_search_results. Supply creative_id or query.

limit.description: Number of similar creatives to return. Maximum 20.

query.description: Optional concept query in the user's original language used to select a seed before vector similarity. Do not append generated translations; source-label expansion is internal. Supply query or creative_id.

description:
Convert DWG/DXF drawings into reviewable GIS and QGIS delivery with source hashes and validation evidence. CAD2GIS 0.8.0 exposes 63 local MCP tools; four wrappers add 15 verified optional CAD tools for source-preserving 2D edits through an isolated MIT runtime.

Supports Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code through repository plugins or stdio MCP configuration. Original code: Apache-2.0. Requires uv and a selected local project root; optional CAD runtime is installed separately. Demo cases remain CONDITIONAL; absolute surveying accuracy is not independently verified.

中文：把图纸转换为可以审查和交接的 GIS 成果，保留原图、记录修订，并将 CAD 编辑返回统一的 GIS 检查流程。安装与中英文 Wiki：https://mola-maker.github.io/CAD2GIS/wiki/
