description:
Local business leads from Google Maps in any country, with emails, phones, websites and lead scores; UK leads add Companies House directors.

**Tools:** `find_local_businesses`, `find_uk_business_leads`, and `get_run_results` for long runs.

**How it works:** each tool call runs an [AutomationNation](https://apify.com/automationnation) Actor on your own Apify account and returns compact JSON plus a link to the run. Paste your Apify API token when you connect: a [free Apify account](https://console.apify.com/sign-up) includes monthly credit, and the token is at [Settings → API & Integrations](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations). Every run carries a spending cap of about 3x its expected cost.

**Pricing (billed by Apify, per result):** Google Maps business leads: $0.03 per lead ($0.024 on Gold) · UK business leads with directors: $0.05 per lead ($0.04 on Gold).

Source, other clients and all toolsets: https://github.com/retracn/automationnation-mcp

tools.description: Find local businesses on Google Maps in any country, as sales leads. Returns name, category, address, phone, email (found on the business website), website, rating and review count, social profiles, opening-date estimate, unclaimed-listing flag and a lead score with reasons. Search any business type in any city, e.g. "dentist" in "Austin, TX". Filters for businesses without a website, recently opened businesses and review counts. Optional AI outreach drafts. About 1–3 minutes for 10 leads because it visits each website. Cost on your Apify account: $0.03 per lead ($0.024 on Gold).

business_type.description: What to search for on Google Maps, e.g. "dentist", "vegan restaurant" or "roofing contractor".

country.description: Two-letter country code for the location, e.g. us, gb, ca, au, de.

find_emails.description: Visit each business website to find an email address. Slower, but most leads are useless without it.

include_outreach_drafts.description: Add AI-written cold email, LinkedIn and SMS drafts for each lead.

location.description: City or area, e.g. "Austin, TX" or "Berlin, Germany". Add the state or country when a name is ambiguous.

max_results.description: How many businesses to return, 1–100. Each result is billed, so ask for what you need.

max_reviews.description: Skip businesses with more reviews than this, e.g. 30 to find newer businesses.

min_reviews.description: Skip businesses with fewer reviews than this.

opened_within_days.description: Only businesses that opened within this many days; 30, 60 or 90 work best. 0 means any age.

with_website_only.description: Only businesses that list a website.

without_website_only.description: Only businesses with no website (good prospects for web design and marketing services).

tools.name: find_local_businesses

tools.description: UK business leads from Google Maps, enriched from Companies House: everything find_local_businesses returns plus the company director's name, company number, incorporation date, company age and SIC codes, with a match-confidence rating. Search UK cities or postcodes for any business type. Use it for UK B2B prospecting. About 1–3 minutes for 10 leads. Cost on your Apify account: $0.05 per lead ($0.04 on Gold).

business_type.description: What to search for, e.g. "plumber", "dentist" or "coffee shop".

cities.description: UK cities, towns or regions, e.g. ["Manchester", "Leeds"]. Give cities or postcodes.

find_emails.description: Visit each business website to find an email address. Slower, but most leads are useless without it.

include_outreach_drafts.description: Add AI-written cold email, LinkedIn and SMS drafts for each lead.

max_results.description: How many businesses to return, 1–100. Each result is billed, so ask for what you need.

max_reviews.description: Skip businesses with more reviews than this, e.g. 30 to find newer businesses.

min_reviews.description: Skip businesses with fewer reviews than this.

opened_within_days.description: Only businesses that opened within this many days; 30, 60 or 90 work best. 0 means any age.

postcodes.description: UK postcodes or districts to search around, e.g. ["M1 1AA", "LS1"].

radius_miles.description: Search radius around each postcode: 1–5 for a neighbourhood, 10–20 for a town.

unclaimed_only.description: Only businesses that haven't claimed their Google Business Profile.

with_website_only.description: Only businesses that list a website.

without_website_only.description: Only businesses with no website (good prospects for web design and marketing services).

tools.name: agent-tool-index

description: Access 17M+ geocoded French property transactions (DVF), 22M+ DPE energy ratings, and 20M+ building records via MCP or REST API. Search transactions, get market stats, find comparables, track price trends, analyze rental yield, detect flips, and score renovation potential. Free tier: 500 credits/month, no credit card required.

tools.description:
Resolve free-form French administrative locations to the canonical Normi filters.

Use this before another Normi tool when the location is informal, accented, abbreviated, or ambiguous. It accepts postal codes, communes and arrondissements such as "Paris 11e", "75011", "Saint-Étienne" or "st etienne".

It returns ranked canonical commune, postal-code, department and INSEE filters. "Paris" intentionally returns all 20 arrondissements rather than silently choosing one.

Cost: 1 credit per call

query.description: Free-form administrative location, e.g. 'Paris 11e', '75011', 'Saint-Étienne', or 'st etienne'.

tools.name: resolve_location

tools.description:
Search French property transactions (Demandes de Valeurs Foncières).

REQUIRED: You MUST provide at least one location filter:
- code_postal (e.g., "75011" for Paris 11e)
- commune (e.g., "PARIS 11", "LYON", "MARSEILLE" - uppercase; Paris uses arrondissements: "PARIS 01"–"PARIS 20")
- code_departement (e.g., "75" for Paris, "69" for Rhône)
- latitude + longitude for radius search (e.g., 48.8566, 2.3522 for Paris center)
- address + code_postal for automatic geocoding (e.g., address: "12 rue de Rivoli", code_postal: "75001")

Common examples:
- Paris 11e apartments: {commune: "PARIS 11", type_local: "Appartement"}
- Near a location: {latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522, radius_m: 500}
- By postal code: {code_postal: "69001", type_local: "Maison"}
- By address: {address: "12 rue de Rivoli", code_postal: "75001", radius_m: 300}

Options:
- summary_only=true: Get stats + 3 samples (~500 tokens vs ~3500 for full results) — use this for overviews
- limit: 1-100 results (default: 5)
- type_local: "Appartement", "Maison", "Terrain", "Local commercial"

Note: radius_m > 1000m is automatically restricted to the last 12 months of data.

Cost: 5 credits per call

address.description: Street address for automatic geocoding — alternative to explicit lat/lon. Example: '12 rue de Rivoli'. Best used with code_postal for precision. Resolves via api-adresse.data.gouv.fr.

code_departement.description: Department code (e.g., '73' for Savoie, '83' for Var)

deduplicate.description: Group duplicate sales (same date, address, price) into single entries

exclude_bulk_sales.description: Exclude bulk sales and aggregated transactions (default: true for clean market data)

exclude_outliers.description: Exclude price outliers (default: true for clean market data)

exclude_vefa.description: Exclude VEFA (new-build, vente en l'état futur d'achèvement) sales (default: true — keeps 'ancien' results from double-counting new-build activity)

radius_m.description: Radius in meters for location search (default: 500)

summary_only.description: Return only summary statistics with 3 sample transactions instead of full list (reduces context usage)

use_original_type.description: Use original type_local instead of smart computed_type_local (default: false)

tools.name: search_property_transactions

tools.description:
Get market statistics: avg/median prices, price per m², surface areas.

REQUIRED: You MUST provide at least one location filter:
- code_postal (e.g., "75011")
- commune (e.g., "PARIS 11" - uppercase; Paris uses "PARIS 01"–"PARIS 20")
- code_departement (e.g., "75")
- latitude + longitude for radius search

Examples:
- Paris 11e market: {commune: "PARIS 11", type_local: "Appartement"}
- 500m radius: {latitude: 48.8566, longitude: 2.3522, radius_m: 500}
- Department stats: {code_departement: "69", type_local: "Maison"}

Returns: count, price (min/max/avg/median), surface stats, price_per_m2

Note: radius_m > 1000m is automatically restricted to the last 12 months of data.

Cost: 5 credits per call

code_departement.description: Department code (e.g., '73' for Savoie, '83' for Var)

exclude_bulk_sales.description: Exclude bulk sales and aggregated transactions (default: true for clean market data)

exclude_outliers.description: Exclude price outliers (default: true for clean market data)

exclude_vefa.description: Exclude VEFA (new-build, vente en l'état futur d'achèvement) sales (default: true — keeps 'ancien' results from double-counting new-build activity)

include_pouvoir_achat.description: Add a price-to-income ratio field (INSEE Filosofi × DVF). Ignored on radius searches.

include_terrain.description: Include terrain-only transactions in search results (default: false)

radius_m.description: Radius in meters for location search (default: 500)

use_original_type.description: Use original type_local instead of smart computed_type_local (default: false)

tools.name: analyze_market_statistics

tools.description:
Price-to-income ratio: how many years of median income to buy the median property here.
Crosses DVF price/surface medians with INSEE Filosofi commune-level median income.

REQUIRED: You MUST provide one of:
- code_postal (e.g., "75011")
- commune (e.g., "LYON", "PARIS 11" - uppercase)
- code_commune: explicit 5-digit INSEE code (e.g., "75111")

NOT SUPPORTED: code_departement alone, or latitude+longitude — a department spans hundreds of
communes with no single meaningful income figure, and radius circles cross commune boundaries.
Use analyze_market_statistics or find_property_comparables for those scopes instead.

Returns: ratio_prix_revenu (years of income), prix_bien_median, revenu_median_annuel_uc, annee_reference.
ratio_prix_revenu is null when INSEE suppresses the commune's income figure (small population).

Cost: 5 credits per call

code_commune.description: 5-digit INSEE commune code — bypasses commune resolution (e.g., '75111')

date_debut.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD) — subject to an auto-applied cap on large scopes

tools.name: analyze_purchasing_power

tools.description:
Detects short-hold resales ("flips") in one French commune.

REQUIRED:
- code_insee: 5-digit INSEE commune code (e.g., "33063" for Bordeaux)
  code_commune is accepted as a compatibility alias.

OPTIONAL:
- type_local: "Maison" or "Appartement"

A flip is a clean DVF sale followed by a resale of the same property 18 to 24 months later.
Matching uses cadastral section + plan first, then a conservative normalized-address + surface fallback.

Returns aggregate-only indicators: flip rate, median gross margin, median margin percentage,
median holding period, and matching-method counts. It never returns transaction addresses or owners.
The 24-month window is anchored to the latest DVF mutation available in the requested commune.

Cost: 10 credits per call

code_commune.description: Legacy 5-digit INSEE-code alias for code_insee (not DVF's raw commune fragment)

type_local.description: Property type filter (default: both houses and apartments)

tools.name: detect_flips

tools.description:
Estimate gross rental yield for one French commune using ANIL asking-rent indicators and clean DVF sale prices.

REQUIRED:
- code_insee: French 5-character INSEE commune code (e.g., "33063" for Bordeaux; Corsica codes such as "2A004" are supported)

OPTIONAL:
- type_local: "Appartement" (default) or "Maison"
- appartement_profile: "all" (default), "t1_t2", or "t3_plus" — apartments only

Returns the latest available 24-month DVF sale window, median sale price/m², ANIL's charges-included rent/m², estimated gross yield, confidence interval, and data-quality flags.

Important: this is a commune-level estimate, not a property valuation. It excludes taxes, financing, vacancy, maintenance, and management costs. ANIL rents are unfurnished advertised rents including charges.

Cost: 10 credits per call

appartement_profile.description: Apartment profile: all (default), t1_t2, or t3_plus. Only applies to Appartement.

code_insee.description: INSEE commune code (e.g., '33063' for Bordeaux or '2A004' in Corsica)

tools.name: analyze_rental_yield

tools.description:
Find comparable properties for valuation - the #1 tool for real estate agents.

REQUIRED parameters:
- latitude, longitude: Target property coordinates
- type_local: "Maison" or "Appartement"
- surface_min, surface_max: Surface range in m² (typically ±20% of target)

Optional:
- pieces: Number of rooms (±1 tolerance applied)
- code_postal, commune: Optional administrative fallback when GPS comparables are sparse
- radius_m: Search radius (default: 500m, max: 2000m)
- max_age_months: Transaction age limit (default: 12, max: 36)
- limit: Max comparables (default: 10, max: 20)

Returns:
- Comparable properties with similarity scores (0-1)
- Distance from target, age of transaction
- Adjustment suggestions (e.g., "+2% for 10m² larger")
- Valuation estimate with confidence level, plus a data-calibrated 50%
  interval (interval.*) and traceable confidence_factors — see
  estimate_property_value's description for the full field reference

Example: Find comps for a 75m² apartment near Tour Eiffel:
{latitude: 48.858, longitude: 2.294, type_local: "Appartement", surface_min: 60, surface_max: 90}

Cost: 10 credits per call

code_postal.description: Postal code fallback when GPS comparables are sparse

commune.description: Commune fallback when GPS comparables are sparse

max_age_months.description: Maximum transaction age in months (default: 12, max: 36)

surface_max.description: Maximum surface in m² (typically target surface + 20%)

surface_min.description: Minimum surface in m² (typically target surface - 20%)

tools.name: find_property_comparables

tools.description:
Analyze price evolution over time - essential for market timing and investment decisions.

REQUIRED: At least one location filter:
- code_postal, commune (e.g., "PARIS 11"), code_departement, or latitude+longitude

Optional:
- type_local: "Maison", "Appartement", "Terrain", "Local commercial"
- granularity: "month", "quarter" (default), or "year"
- date_debut/date_fin: Date range (default: last 5 years)

Returns:
- Time series with median/avg prices per period
- Year-over-year changes (%)
- Overall trend: "increasing", "decreasing", or "stable"
- Total change over the period

Example: Paris 11e apartment price trends:
{commune: "PARIS 11", type_local: "Appartement", granularity: "quarter"}

Note: DVF data covers 2014–2025 (annual cadence). Use date windows ≥ 12 months for reliable results.

Cost: 10 credits per call
tools.name: analyze_price_trends

tools.description:
Compare 2-5 neighborhoods side-by-side - perfect for investment location decisions.

REQUIRED:
- locations: Array of 2-5 objects with {code_postal} or {commune}

Optional:
- type_local: "Maison" or "Appartement" (default: Appartement)
- date_debut: Start date (default: 1 year ago)

Returns per location:
- Transaction count, median price/m², median price
- Year-over-year price change
- Rankings (cheapest, most expensive, highest volume, fastest growing)

Example: Compare Paris arrondissements by postal code:
{locations: [{code_postal: "75011"}, {code_postal: "75020"}, {code_postal: "75019"}]}

Example: Compare cities by commune:
{locations: [{commune: "LYON"}, {commune: "BORDEAUX"}, {commune: "NANTES"}]}

Note: DVF data covers 2014–2025 (annual cadence). Use date windows ≥ 12 months for reliable results.

Cost: 10 credits per call
tools.name: compare_locations

tools.description:
Get price statistics aggregated by postal code or commune zones — returns JSON data suitable as input for heatmap visualizations (not a rendered map or image). Hosts with MCP Apps support additionally render this as an interactive bubble map.

REQUIRED: At least one scope filter:
- code_departement: Department code (e.g., "75" for Paris)
- commune: Major city (e.g., "PARIS" - returns all arrondissements)

Optional:
- type_local: "Maison" or "Appartement"
- group_by: "code_postal" (default) or "commune"
- min_transactions: Minimum transactions to include zone (default: 10)
- date_debut/date_fin: Date range (default: last year)

Returns per zone:
- Centroid coordinates (lat/lon) for map plotting
- Median and average price/m²
- Transaction count
- Relative position: "expensive", "average", or "affordable"

Use this when you need to: compare price levels across an entire department, find the most/least expensive zones, or provide data to build a price heatmap.
Do NOT call this expecting a rendered image — it returns structured JSON data only.

Example: Paris zones by postal code:
{commune: "PARIS", type_local: "Appartement"}

Cost: 15 credits per call

commune.description: Major city name (e.g., 'PARIS' - returns all arrondissements)

min_transactions.description: Minimum transactions to include a zone (default: 10)

tools.name: get_zonal_price_distribution

tools.description:
Monthly transaction volume time series — use when you need to show how activity has changed over time, not when you need a single comparable number.

WHEN TO USE THIS vs score_market_health:
- Use analyze_market_activity when the question is "show me how volume has evolved" or "is there seasonality?"
- Use score_market_health when the question is "is this market good or bad?" or "compare two markets"

REQUIRED: At least one location filter:

Optional:
- type_local: Property type filter
- months: Analysis period (default: 24, max: 60)

Returns:
- Monthly transaction volumes with YoY changes
- Trend direction: "increasing", "decreasing", or "stable"
- Activity level: "hot", "normal", or "slow"
- Seasonality: peak and low months
- Market signal with description

Example: Lyon market activity:
{commune: "LYON", type_local: "Appartement", months: 24}

Note: DVF data covers 2014–2025 (annual cadence). Use months ≥ 12 for reliable results.

Cost: 10 credits per call
tools.name: analyze_market_activity

tools.description:
Get transaction history for a specific address - essential for due diligence.

REQUIRED: One of these combinations:
1. address + code_postal: Street name search
2. section + no_plan + code_commune: Cadastral reference lookup

Returns:
- All transactions at this address (chronological)
- Each transaction includes an id field — pass it to get_building_characteristics for BDNB building data
- Price, surface, type, buyer type for each
- Price evolution: appreciation %, annualized return
- Period between first and last sale

Workflow: lookup_property_history → use transaction id → get_building_characteristics

Example by address:
{address: "rue de rivoli", code_postal: "75001"}

Example by cadastral:
{section: "AB", no_plan: "123", code_commune: "101"}

Cost: 20 credits per call

address.description: Street address to search

code_commune.description: DVF commune code — NOT the full 5-digit INSEE code. Strip the 2-digit department prefix and any leading zeros. Examples: Paris 16e → '116', Paris 1er → '101', Lyon 6e → '386', Nice → '88', Bordeaux → '63'.

tools.name: lookup_property_history

tools.description:
Get an automated valuation (AVM) for a property — low / mid / high price range.

Use find_property_comparables instead if you want the raw comparable transactions with similarity scores. estimate_property_value returns only the AVM summary (low/mid/high range).

REQUIRED: latitude, longitude, surface

Optional:
- type_local: "Maison" or "Appartement" (default: Appartement)
- pieces: Number of rooms
- code_postal, commune: Optional administrative fallback when GPS comparables are sparse
- radius_m: Search radius (100–2000m, default: 500)
- max_age_months: Max transaction age (1–24, default: 18)

Returns:
- price_range: { low, mid, high } in euros
- price_per_m2: { median, used_surface }
- confidence: "high", "medium" or "low". It reflects comparable count and
  average similarity; it is not a calibrated probability of accuracy.
- based_on_count: number of comparables used
- interval: { method, coverage_label, basis, cohort, cohort_eligible_n,
  ratio_low, ratio_high, contract_version, calibration_generated_at } — how
  price_range was derived.
- confidence_factors: { comparable_count, average_similarity, fallback_used,
  positive_factors[], limiting_factors[] } — traceable inputs to confidence.

Returns estimate: null with a message if fewer than 3 comparables are found.
Tip: increase radius_m or max_age_months to get more data.

Note: the low/high range is a data-calibrated 50% interquartile interval
(P25/P75 of observed-price / published-mid, backtest-measured on 2,000 masked
DVF sales), not a fixed percentage. Its width is driven first by how much the
retained comparables *agree* on price/m² — the dispersion cohort, (P75-P25) /
median, e.g. interval.cohort = "dispersion=<15%" — then by comparable density,
property type and surface band, and it widens to the global cohort when a
segment lacks enough measured data (interval.basis). Agreeing or contradicting
comparables also surface as confidence_factors comparables_agree /
comparables_disagree. The mid value is unaffected by any of this.
DVF data covers 2014–2025 (annual cadence). Use max_age_months ≥ 12 for
reliable results.

Cost: 10 credits per call

WHEN TO USE THIS vs analyze_market_activity:

- Use analyze_market_activity when you need volume trends over time or seasonal patterns

Score interpretation:
- 0–30: Low activity — weak volume, stagnant/declining prices
- 31–60: Moderate — decent activity, neutral trends
- 61–80: Active — good volume, slight price increase
- 81–100: Very dynamic — strong demand, fast-rising prices

description: Haulest for AI assistants: research cost ranges, vet movers with dated reviews and licence records, pull guides and checklists, and request written quotes.

tools.description: Returns Haulest's research planning range (low and high, with currency) for a household move in the United States, Canada, or the United Kingdom, from home size and distance. Pass a distance band, a mileage, or an origin and destination; the tool resolves the distance from stored route data where it can. The range is compiled from published industry tables and public quotes, not a bid from a mover. Use it when someone asks what a move might cost.

distanceBand.description: Distance band when known: local (under 50 mi; UK under 20), regional, mid, long, cross-country.

from.description: Origin city or town, e.g. "Austin, TX" or "London".

homeSize.description: Home size: studio, 1bed, 2bed, 3bed, or 4bed (4bed covers larger homes).

market.description: Country: us, ca, or uk. Inferred from the places when omitted; defaults to us.

miles.description: Driving distance in miles when the user already knows it.

tools.name: estimate_moving_cost

tools.description: Facts about a city-to-city moving lane that Haulest has a route page for: driving miles and hours, the research cost range by home size, how many households moved between the two states in the latest Census flow, and the page URL. Covers the main US, Canadian, and UK lanes. Use it when someone names both ends of a move; returns a clear not-covered message otherwise.

from.description: Origin city, e.g. "Austin" or "Austin, TX".

tools.name: get_route_facts

tools.description: Lists moving companies Haulest holds dated, attributed reviews for in a city, state, province, or country (US, Canada, UK), with the average rating, the number of reviews on record, the newest review date, the USDOT number where there is one, and the profile URL. Ratings are means of real reviews on record; Haulest does not rank companies by payment. Use it when someone wants movers in a place; follow with the profile tool for one company.

limit.description: How many companies to return, 1 to 10. Default 6.

market.description: Country to prefer when a place name exists in more than one: us, ca, or uk.

minReviews.description: Only companies with at least this many dated reviews on record.

place.description: City, state or province, or country, e.g. "Denver, CO", "Ontario", "Manchester", "Canada".

sort.description: recommended (default), newest review, highest rating, or lowest rating.

tools.name: find_movers

tools.description: One moving company in detail from its Haulest profile: rating and review counts, the three newest dated reviews, licence identifiers (USDOT, MC) with the live FMCSA authority and insurance summary when available, the company's own phone number from a public record, what reviewers paid, short checkable strengths and questions to ask, and the profile URL. Use it after find_movers or when someone names a company that has a Haulest page.

slug.description: The company slug from find_movers, or the last part of a haulest.com/movers/... URL.

tools.name: get_mover_profile

tools.description: Looks a moving company up in the official register: for the United States, the FMCSA census by USDOT, MC, or legal name, with live operating authority, insurance on file, and safety rating when available; for the United Kingdom, Companies House by name or number. market.description: us (FMCSA, default), uk (Companies House), or ca (guidance only; Canada has no federal mover licence).

query.description: USDOT number, MC number, or company legal name (US); company name or number (UK).

tools.name: check_mover_licence

query.description: What the person wants to know, e.g. "binding estimate", "tipping movers", "deposit", "damage claim", "when to book".

tools.name: search_moving_guides

tools.description: Returns one of Haulest's checklists in full, grouped by section: the 8-week countdown, moving day, the first-night box, change of address for the US, Canada, or UK, or the 12-week international list. Use it when someone wants a to-do list for a move.
tools.name: get_moving_checklist

tools.description: Submits a quote request to Haulest so licensed movers can call and email the person with written estimates for the move. Haulest is not a carrier; it introduces the request to movers through its lead desk, and in the US and UK the desk may phone within minutes. Call this only after the person has given their name, phone, and email for this purpose and has explicitly agreed to be contacted (consent must be true); confirm the details back to them first. Each call creates one request; a repeat with the same phone or email within a day is recognised and not duplicated. Returns a request reference and what happens next.

consent.description: Must be true: the person has explicitly agreed that Haulest may share these details with licensed movers who will call and email about this move.

from.description: Where the move starts: city and state/province, or a postcode.

moveDate.description: Planned move date, YYYY-MM-DD, today or later.

name.description: The person's name.

notes.description: Anything else the movers should know: stairs, piano, elevator booking, access.

packing.description: Packing wanted: full pack, fragile only, or self pack.

phone.description: A phone number the movers may call.

description:
Everpop is an AI clipping tool that turns a creator's own uploaded videos into published YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and Facebook Reels, plus TikTok drafts the creator posts, never downloads from YouTube, publishes to the creator's own connected channels after their confirmation, and reports 48-hour and 7-day YouTube Analytics receipts for eligible Shorts.

Its MCP server at https://everpop.app/api/mcp/mcp (Streamable HTTP) gives an agent 16 tools for that loop: upload the user's own video file, clip it, publish a finished clip only to the destinations the user confirms, and read back the measured receipts for eligible YouTube Shorts; campaign tools group published clips into a payout report. A YouTube link is never downloaded: clipping a video without its file returns upload_required. Sign in with OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, or send a per-user API key as Authorization: Bearer epk_…. Tool calls need the Pro or Scale plan; other accounts get a 402 result with reason "subscription" or "plan".

tools.description: The 20 most recent source videos known to Everpop (the user's own uploads), newest first, with id, title, status, detection time and whether each can be clipped (clippable; when false, notClippableReason is the error clip_video would return, e.g. upload_required), plus latestJob (the newest clip job's jobId, status and error, or null — where an automatic render started by finalize_upload shows up). Pass the returned nextCursor as cursor for older videos; nextCursor is null on the last page. The result also carries browserUploadUrl: the page, behind the user's own sign-in, where they can upload a new file themselves when you can't send the bytes (no upload slot needed).

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous list_videos result, to fetch the next (older) page.

tools.name: list_videos

tools.description: Starts an exact-size upload for the user's own video file. filename and sizeBytes are required. Returns a short-lived presigned URL, expectedBytes, requiredHeaders that must all be sent with the raw bytes, and the durable key. Accepts .mp4, .mov, .webm, .mkv or .m4v up to 5 GB — the most one PUT can carry; a file up to 32 GB goes through the user's browserUploadUrl from list_videos. If you can't send the bytes yourself, don't call this: give the user list_videos' browserUploadUrl, since every slot counts against the user's open uploads until it expires.

filename.description: The video file's name, extension included — .mp4 / .mov / .webm / .mkv / .m4v

sizeBytes.description: Exact file size in bytes; the signed upload contract binds this value

tools.name: request_upload

tools.description: Cancels a request_upload slot after a failed/abandoned PUT. A 503 cleanup_pending result means cleanup is durably recorded and will retry automatically. Never cancel after finalize_upload succeeds or returns an ambiguous acknowledgement.

key.description: The storage key returned by request_upload.

tools.name: cancel_upload

tools.description: Turns a previously uploaded file into a clippable video in the user's library. Eligible accounts begin creating draft clips automatically unless renderMode is manual. These clips require explicit review and publishing, even with Autopilot enabled. An optional link id attaches the file to an already-detected video, preserving its attribution. Returns videoId, title, existing, linked, autoClipping, and parked='quota' when monthly allowance prevents the automatic clip. Retry ambiguous failures with the same key; never re-upload or cancel them.

key.description: The storage key identifying the uploaded file.

linkSourceVideoId.description: Id of an already-detected video to attach this file to instead of creating a new entry; preserves its attribution.

renderMode.description: auto (default): an account with automatic clipping on starts a render with its saved settings, and that render uses this video's monthly allowance. manual: no automatic render; call clip_video with your own options.

rightsConfirmed.description: Whether the user holds the rights to this footage; must be true to proceed.

title.description: Library title; defaults to the filename

tools.name: finalize_upload

tools.description: Registers metadata for a video from the user's own connected channel (idempotent). The video becomes clippable once its file has been uploaded. Returns the video id and title.

url.description: YouTube watch / shorts / youtu.be URL, or a bare 11-character video id

tools.name: import_video

tools.description: Creates draft short vertical clips from one of the user's source videos. The clips require explicit review and publishing, even with Autopilot enabled. An optional prompt directs which moments to clip; archetype picks the cut (top_moments, summary, punch, action, or all for one of each) and targetSeconds the length. Returns a job id whose status can be checked. A source without an uploaded file returns an upload_required error (list_videos marks it clippable: false).

archetype.description: Editorial cut: top_moments, summary (a stitched montage), punch, action, or all (a Summary, a Top-moment and a Punch from one pass). Omit for the normal best-moments pick.

clipCount.description: How many clips (1–20); the plan's per-video cap applies and the result's clipCountApplied says what was used. Omit for the account's saved clip count.

language.description: Omit to use the saved language choice (English text by default). Null explicitly selects English captions, headlines and hooks with auto-detected speech. A lowercase ISO-639-1 code such as bg pins that spoken language and keeps text native. Original audio is retained.

operationId.description: Client operation UUID: retries carrying the same id never create a second metered render.

description:
CAJAS MCP connects AI clients to CAJAS accounting workflows through a standard MCP interface.

It supports workspace discovery, RAW entry search, event search, RAW and CoA import preview flows, explainable Assembly recommendations, historical Assembly context, criterion/standard reference discovery, and optional community validation.

Authentication is required for CAJAS data access. Use CAJAS OAuth where supported, or provide a CAJAS MCP Personal Access Token as an Authorization header.

Recommendations are non-binding review signals and do not approve, finalize, sign, or mutate accounting judgments automatically.

tools.description: Searches CAJAS RAW entries with pagination and filters. Supported status values are draft, queued, assembled, and voided. project and department are returned only when stored by CAJAS; missing values are not inferred. created_by_name is a stored actor label and may differ from created_by_display profile identity. This read-only tool does not modify RAW status, create an Assembly, or create an Event.
tools.name: cajas.search_raw_entries

tools.description: Searches CAJAS accounting events. This read-only tool does not confirm, void, sign, approve, finalize, or alter events.
tools.name: cajas.search_events

tools.description: Returns one CAJAS accounting event and CAJAS-provided judgment support context. This read-only tool does not confirm, void, sign, approve, finalize, or alter the event.
tools.name: cajas.get_event

tools.description: Analyzes selected RAW entries and returns non-binding Assembly candidates for human review. The recommendation identifies RAW entries that may share an operational context. Community validation is opt-in only and uses public, untrusted operational context when requested. It does not create an Assembly, modify RAW status, create an Event, determine accounting treatment, approve accounting judgment, sign, finalize, or alter immutable CAJAS history.
tools.name: cajas.recommend_assembly

description:
# SEFAZ PI: Solicitar Certidão Negativa da Dívida Ativa (CNDA)

SEFAZ PI: Solicitar Certidão Negativa da Dívida Ativa (CNDA), consulta em fonte oficial. Hospedado pela plataforma, sem credenciais da plataforma, pague por consulta com crédito pré-pago.

Funciona em qualquer cliente MCP. Servidor remoto: `https://api.mcp.ai/p_sefaz_pi_cnda`

tools.description: SEFAZ PI: Solicitar Certidão Negativa da Dívida Ativa (CNDA), consulta em fonte oficial. Hospedado pela plataforma, sem credenciais da plataforma, pague por consulta com crédito pré-pago. Consulta informação de fontes e órgãos oficiais brasileiros (a mesma disponível ao cidadão), não é dado sigiloso. O cliente é o controlador dos dados e responde pela finalidade legítima (LGPD).

tools.name: connect

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.

description:
EU AI Act compliance for AI agents, grounded in Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus, in force 27 July 2026). Operative law is the default in every answer; pending changes are opt-in and labelled by source status.

Ten deterministic tools, no LLM in the loop, so the same input always returns the same output. euaiact_assess_system takes one normalized system profile and returns separate legal-classification, impact and implementation-readiness blocks with field-level provenance. euaiact_classify_system returns a risk tier (prohibited, high-risk, limited, minimal) from free text or structured signals, naming both the signals it matched and the ones it still needs. The rest cover Annex III and Annex IV, provider and deployer obligations, the Art. 6(3) exception including the profiling carve-out, GPAI systemic risk at the Art. 51 threshold of 10^25 FLOPs, penalties, deadlines, and article lookup with stable EUR-Lex citations. Five resources and four prompts included.

Sparse input fails closed: the server answers "undetermined" and names the decisive missing facts instead of guessing a classification.

No API key, no telemetry, two runtime dependencies; installed locally it makes no network calls. MIT licensed. A first-pass technical output, not legal advice and not certification. By Lexbeam Software.

tools.description: Classify an AI system's risk level under the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689). HOW TO CALL: derive the structured `signals` from the user's description yourself and pass them together with `description`. The result is decided deterministically on the signals; free text alone is only matched against keywords and often returns insufficient_information. Set a signal only when the description supports it and leave it out otherwise; never guess, and never infer `signals.domain` from the sector a system operates in (read that field's description). missing_signals lists unprovided fields, including optional context; it is not a checklist of facts required for the reported result. Relay next_questions where present, then call again with the answers. A matched route does not establish that every other route has been ruled out. Returns risk classification, applicable Annex III category, relevant articles, provider/deployer determination, matched signals, and follow-up questions the agent should relay. Note: Art. 6(3) exceptions require documented justification and cannot be auto-applied; use euaiact_assess_art6_3_exception.

description.description: Free-text description of the AI system and its functionalities

affects_fundamental_rights.description: System materially affects health, safety, or fundamental rights of natural persons

biometric_law_enforcement.description: Biometric system is used by or for law enforcement

biometric_publicly_accessible_space.description: Real-time remote biometric identification takes place in publicly accessible spaces (Art. 5(1)(h))

biometric_realtime.description: Biometric processing happens in real time

biometric_remote_identification.description: System performs remote biometric identification, not merely one-to-one biometric verification

biometric_sole_purpose_verification.description: Biometric use is solely to verify that a specific natural person is the person they claim to be, which is excluded from Annex III(1)(a)

domain.description: The Annex III area whose LISTED use the system itself performs. Annex III regulates specific uses, never a sector: choose an area only when the system does one of the uses listed for it below, and choose `other` when it merely operates in that sector (a utility's billing chatbot, a school timetable, a payroll check, fleet maintenance for the police, appointment booking at an immigration office, a court-room scheduler, legal research for a law firm). Leave it out when the description does not let you tell. Listed uses: biometrics: for remote biometric identification, biometric categorisation according to sensitive or protected attributes, or emotion recognition of natural persons, in so far as their use is permitted under Union or national law. Sole-purpose biometric verification to confirm that a specific natural person is who they claim to be is excluded from Annex III(1)(a). | critical_infrastructure: as safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or the supply of water, gas, heating, and electricity. | education: to determine access to or admission to educational and vocational training institutions, to evaluate learning outcomes, to assess the appropriate level of education, or to monitor and detect prohibited behaviour during tests. | employment: for recruitment, selection, job advertising targeting, application filtering, candidate evaluation, promotion and termination decisions, task allocation, and monitoring or evaluation of work performance and behaviour. | essential_services: for the specific essential-service use cases listed in Annex III(5): public-authority eligibility decisions for essential public assistance benefits and services, creditworthiness or credit scoring of natural persons (with the exception of AI systems used for the purpose of detecting financial fraud, Annex III(5)(b)), risk assessment and pricing for life and health insurance, and emergency-call classification, dispatch, prioritisation, or emergency healthcare triage. | law_enforcement: by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities for victim risk assessment, polygraphs and similar tools, evaluation of evidence reliability, assessing the risk of a natural person offending or re-offending, assessment of personality traits or past criminal behaviour of natural persons or groups, or profiling natural persons in criminal detection, investigation, or prosecution. | migration: by competent public authorities in migration, asylum, and border control as polygraphs or similar tools, for assessing risks posed by natural persons entering a Member State, for examining applications for asylum, visa, and residence permits, and for detecting, recognising, or identifying natural persons in border control. Verification of travel documents is excluded from Annex III(7)(d). | justice: to assist judicial authorities in researching and interpreting facts and law and in applying the law to concrete facts, or to be used to influence the outcome of elections or referendums or the voting behaviour of natural persons. Campaign administration or logistics tools are excluded where natural persons are not directly exposed to the output. | health, gpai, product_safety: not Annex III areas; use them for a health context, a general-purpose AI model, or a safety component of a product under Annex I.

generates_synthetic_content.description: System generates or manipulates images, audio, video, or text (Art. 50(2)/(4))

interacts_with_natural_persons.description: System is designed to interact directly with natural persons (Art. 50(1))

is_safety_component_of_regulated_product.description: System is a safety component of a product covered by EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I)

performs_emotion_recognition_workplace_o.description: System infers emotions of natural persons in the workplace or educational institutions (Art. 5(1)(f))

performs_social_scoring.description: System evaluates or classifies natural persons or groups over time based on social behaviour or personal/personality characteristics, leading to detrimental treatment (Art. 5(1)(c))

performs_social_scoring_by_public_author.description: Legacy alias: public-authority social scoring. Art. 5(1)(c) is not limited to public authorities.

requires_third_party_conformity_assessme.description: The product or AI system is required to undergo third-party conformity assessment under the applicable Annex I legislation

social_scoring_unjustified_or_disproport.description: Social scoring leads to detrimental or unfavourable treatment that is unjustified or disproportionate to the social behaviour or its gravity (Art. 5(1)(c)(ii))

social_scoring_unrelated_context.description: Social scoring leads to detrimental or unfavourable treatment in social contexts unrelated to the contexts in which the data was originally generated or collected (Art. 5(1)(c)(i))

targets_children_or_vulnerable.description: System is directed at or materially affects children or other vulnerable groups (Art. 5(1)(b))

uses_biometrics.description: System processes biometric data (face, fingerprint, iris, voice, gait)

use_case.description: Specific context where the system is deployed

tools.name: euaiact_classify_system

tools.description: Returns key implementation milestones and deadlines for the EU AI Act with days remaining, a `next_milestone` shortcut, and a summary of the Digital Omnibus. The milestone timeline always reflects the operative law. Set `include_pending_omnibus: true` to also receive the structured Digital Omnibus pack (each item source-status labelled; its `status` and `enacted` fields carry the current legislative state). Use `only_upcoming: true` to drop past milestones.

include_pending_omnibus.description: If true, also return the structured Digital Omnibus pack with per-item source-status labels. OFF by default: the milestone timeline always reflects the operative law only. Check the pack's `status` and `enacted` fields for its current legislative state; non-enacted content must not be treated as current law.

only_upcoming.description: If true, return only milestones that have not yet come into effect.

tools.name: euaiact_check_deadlines

tools.description: Returns specific compliance obligations for providers or deployers based on AI system risk level.

annex_iii_point.description: If high_risk_source is annex_iii, the Annex III point number. Point 2 has special Art. 49/27 treatment.

gpai_model_placed_on_market_before_2025_.description: For GPAI providers, whether the model was placed on the market before 2 August 2025, triggering the Art. 111(3) transition to 2 August 2027.

high_risk_source.description: For high-risk systems, whether classification comes from Annex III/Art. 6(2), Annex I/Art. 6(1), or is unknown

risk_level.description: AI system risk level. Use 'gpai' for general-purpose AI model obligations (Art. 51-56).

tools.name: euaiact_get_obligations

tools.description: Search frequently asked questions about the EU AI Act and get best-match answers with article references. Covers classification, deadlines, roles, governance, documentation, risk assessment, penalties, GPAI systemic risk, FRIA, transparency, and sector-specific guidance.

question.description: User question about the EU AI Act

tools.name: euaiact_answer_question

tools.description: Calculates the maximum possible fine for an EU AI Act violation based on violation type, global annual turnover, SME status and SMC (small mid-cap) status. Implements the Art. 99 penalty framework including the SME/startup lower-of rule (Art. 99(6), tiers 99(3)-(5)) and the narrower SMC rule (Art. 99(6a), tiers 99(4)-(5) only; no SMC cap on Art. 5 fines and none under Art. 101). Returns a comparative block so the agent can show the SME reduction to the user.

annual_turnover_eur.description: Global annual turnover in EUR (a non-negative, finite number)

is_smc.description: Whether the entity is a small mid-cap (SMC): Art. 99(6a) applies the lower-of rule ONLY to the Art. 99(4) and 99(5) tiers, not to Art. 99(3) prohibited-practice fines and not to Art. 101

is_sme.description: Whether the entity is an SME or startup (eligible for lower fines under Art. 99(6), covering paragraphs 3, 4 and 5)

violation_type.description: Type of AI Act violation: 'prohibited' (Art. 5), 'high_risk' (Art. 99(4) operator/notified-body/transparency obligations), 'gpai' (Art. 101 general-purpose AI model provider infringements), or 'false_info' (Art. 99(5) misleading notified bodies or national competent authorities; GPAI-provider false information falls under Art. 101)

tools.name: euaiact_calculate_penalty

tools.description: Retrieve an operational summary of a specific article of the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), plus a stable EUR-Lex URL to the canonical text. Supports a subset of the most-cited articles (Art. 3, 4, 5, 6, 9-17, 26, 27, 43, 47, 49, 50, 51, 53, 55, 72, 73, 99, 100, 113). For articles outside this subset the tool returns the EUR-Lex base URL. The summary is not statutory text: follow the URL and verify the official provision before quoting it.

article.description: Article number (e.g. '5', '4a', 'Art. 99', 'Article 4', 'Artikel 4'). Case-insensitive; prefix optional. Returns the whole article summary, not an individual paragraph.

tools.name: euaiact_get_article

tools.description: Determine whether a general-purpose AI model qualifies as a GPAI model with systemic risk under Art. 51. This tool uses an adjudicated conservative boundary at or above 10^25 cumulative training FLOPs for the Art. 51(2) presumption. The Commission may also designate models with equivalent capabilities or impact under Art. 51(1)(b). Returns baseline GPAI obligations under Art. 53 plus systemic-risk-only obligations under Art. 55, and the Art. 52 notification duty.

commission_designated.description: Whether the Commission has formally designated the model as GPAI with systemic risk under Art. 51(1)(b).

model_name.description: Optional model name for traceability in the response.

training_flops.description: Cumulative training compute in FLOPs (e.g. 2e25). The adjudicated product boundary triggers the Art. 51(2) presumption at or above 1e25. Omit if unknown; the tool then abstains instead of answering.

tools.name: euaiact_check_gpai_systemic_risk

tools.description: Walk through the Art. 6(3) exception for Annex III high-risk AI systems. An Annex III system is NOT high-risk only if the provider affirmatively assesses no significant risk to health, safety, or fundamental rights, AND the system falls under one of the four conditions: (a) narrow procedural task, (b) improves prior human activity, (c) detects patterns without replacing human assessment, (d) preparatory task. Set no_significant_risk_to_health_safety_fundamental_rights=true only when that threshold has been assessed. CRITICAL: The exception does NOT apply if the system performs profiling of natural persons (Art. 6(3), third subparagraph). Providers invoking the exception must document the assessment (Art. 6(4)) and still register in the EU database (Art. 49(2)).

annex_iii_number.description: Annex III category number (1-8). Provide if known - helps the response reference the right rules.

detects_patterns_without_replacing_human.description: Art. 6(3)(c): intended to detect decision-making patterns or deviations, not replace/influence human assessment without proper review.

documented_assessment.description: Has the provider documented the Art. 6(3) exception assessment? Required by Art. 6(4) regardless of which condition applies.

improves_prior_human_activity.description: Art. 6(3)(b): intended to improve the result of a previously completed human activity (e.g. improve drafting style).

narrow_procedural_task.description: Art. 6(3)(a): intended to perform a narrow procedural task (e.g. transform unstructured to structured data, classify documents, detect duplicates).

no_significant_risk_to_health_safety_fun.description: Has the provider affirmatively assessed that the system does not pose a significant risk of harm to health, safety, or fundamental rights, including by not materially influencing decision-making outcomes? Required for Art. 6(3).

performs_profiling.description: Does the system perform profiling of natural persons? If true, Art. 6(3) exception is UNAVAILABLE regardless of other conditions (Art. 6(3), third subparagraph).

preparatory_task.description: Art. 6(3)(d): intended to perform a preparatory task for an assessment relevant to an Annex III use case.

tools.name: euaiact_assess_art6_3_exception

tools.description: The nine titles and descriptions summarise Annex IV. `sub_items` are non-binding implementation prompts, are not verbatim Annex IV text, and do not create additional legal requirements. Under Article 11(1), SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs may provide the Annex IV elements in a simplified manner only by using the Commission form referred to in that paragraph.

format.description: Output shape: 'json' returns structured items; 'checklist' adds a markdown checklist string.

sme_simplified.description: Indicate whether SME-simplified preparation is being used (Art. 11(1) second subparagraph).

tools.name: euaiact_annex_iv_checklist

tools.description: Assess one normalized EU AI Act system profile against the pinned sealed corpus. Returns separate legal-classification, impact, and implementation-readiness blocks with field-level facts, decisive missing facts, complete finding provenance, warnings, and recommended atomic follow-up calls. Sparse inputs fail closed. Impact never changes legal classification, and classification never implies implementation readiness. HOW TO BUILD THE PROFILE: every fact is an object {fact_id, value, origin, verification, evidence_reference_ids}. For a fact the user told you, use origin "explicit_structured_input", verification "caller_asserted", evidence_reference_ids [] and any unique lowercase fact_id such as "identity.system_name". A useful minimum is identity.system_name, intended_use.intended_purpose (intended_use also needs reasonably_foreseeable_uses, which may be []), role_facts.roles, geography with jurisdictions, affected_person_groups and one of used_in_eu, placed_on_eu_market or output_used_in_eu, and decision_context.decision_consequence. Set annex_iii.domain and annex_iii.annex_iii_point only when the system itself performs a use Annex III lists for that area, never because it operates in that sector. Supply only facts you were given: a missing decisive fact comes back in missing_facts with the question to ask.
tools.name: euaiact_assess_system

description: Num is an AI travel concierge covering 119 cities in 39 countries. This connector lets Claude search Num’s place directory for a destination, see what’s open at a given time, read a venue’s own published menu and prices, check its rating summary (public rating plus Num’s verified-guest average), and get the right way to book: the venue’s booking system, phone, email or its own page. It can also return a short concierge answer for a travel question. Read-only, no account needed. Num never contacts guests and never charges a card through this connector. If booking links carry affiliate tags, add one sentence here saying so.

tools.description: Find real, currently-operating places in a destination — restaurants, bars, beaches, spas, viewpoints, temples. Ranked by quality (rating weighted by how many reviews stand behind it). When `near` is a "lat,lng" coordinate pair, results are limited to about 5 km of that point, ranked by a blend of quality and distance — so a 4.8★ institution two streets away beats an unrated snack bar next door — and each carries `distance_m`. When `near` is a neighbourhood name it filters by area and NO distance is returned. Returns name, category, area, rating, review count, phone, address and opening hours where known. NEVER invents a place: if Num does not hold it, it is not returned. You MUST display the returned `attribution` string wherever you show these results.

category.description: restaurant | bar | beach | spa | viewpoint | temple | waterfall | cafe (any case). Omit for all.

destination.description: Destination slug or city name, e.g. "phuket", "bangkok".

near.description: A "lat,lng" pair (e.g. "7.8208,98.2976") for distance-ranked results, or a neighbourhood name to filter by area, e.g. "Kata Beach".

query.description: Free text, e.g. "thai seafood", "rooftop".

tools.name: search_places

tools.description: Ask Num the way a traveller would — "where should we eat tonight near Kata?", "which beach for sunset?" — and get a short concierge answer grounded in Num's verified directory, plus the places it names as structured data so you can render your own cards. This is the whole product in one tool. It answers about the place asked and NEVER substitutes a different city. If Num has no coverage there it says so rather than guessing. It does not book, charge, or take personal details — send none. You MUST display the returned `attribution`.

destination.description: Where they are, if you know it. Improves grounding.

language.description: BCP-47 tag for the reply, e.g. "th", "ru". Defaults to the language of the question.

near.description: Neighbourhood or hotel area, if known.

question.description: The traveller's question, in their own words. Any language.

tools.name: concierge_answer

tools.description: Which destinations Num covers, with the number of verified places in each. Call this FIRST when you do not know whether a city is supported — it is cheaper than a failed search and stops you promising a traveller coverage that does not exist. Coverage is honest: a destination appears here only when it has a real, maintained directory.
tools.name: list_destinations

tools.description: Everything Num holds on one place, by place_id from search_places: contact details, hours, rating, review count, area, category, cuisine, the venue's own short description (`about`), coordinates, `open_now` computed in the destination's timezone (true / false / null — null means Num has not verified the hours, NOT that it is closed), the booking platform and — only where a verified owner chose it — the venue's own booking page, a recently-read published price line where Num holds one, and up to 8 approved member photos plus the listing photo, each with its own `attribution` you MUST show alongside it. Use before showing a detail page or handing a traveller a phone number. Returns only what is verified — absent fields are absent because Num does not know them, never because they were omitted for brevity. Do not fill gaps from memory; an invented phone number is worse than a missing one.
tools.name: place_details

tools.description: Places that are OPEN RIGHT NOW in a destination, computed in the destination's own timezone. Businesses whose own website is a dead domain or a 404 are excluded entirely — they have closed down. IMPORTANT: only venues whose opening hours Num has verified can appear here, so a short list means thin hours coverage, NOT an empty city. Never tell a traveller "nothing is open" on the strength of this tool; say that these are the ones Num can confirm are open. Use search_places for the full directory.

bookable_only.description: Only venues Num can hand off a booking page for.

category.description: Exact category, e.g. "Restaurant". Omit for all.

tools.name: open_places

tools.description: A booking page for one place with the party size, date and time ALREADY FILLED IN. This does NOT make a reservation and Num does not hold a table — the traveller completes it on the venue's own platform (OpenTable, Resy, Tock, SevenRooms, Square and others). The response always carries `booked: false` and `mode: "deeplink"`. You MUST NOT render this as a confirmation, and you MUST NOT tell a traveller a table is held. If the venue has no booking platform the response says so and returns the phone number instead — offer that rather than implying it cannot be visited.
tools.name: booking_link

tools.description: The venue's own published menu or list of offerings — dishes, treatments, tours — grouped by the venue's sections in the venue's order. Free: included in the no-fee free tier, no key needed to try it. Written by the venue itself in its Num dashboard, not scraped: prices are exactly as the venue set them, in its own currency, each with the formatted amount, the currency code and the integer minor units. A price is what the venue says it charges, NOT a quote — never tell a traveller their bill will be that figure. An item with no price has `price: null` (or only a note such as "market price"); do not estimate one. If the venue has not published a menu, `sections` is empty and `note` says so — say that, never invent dishes. Age-restricted items are never shown on this surface. You MUST display the returned `attribution`.
tools.name: get_menu

tools.description: A rating SUMMARY for one place, free (included in the no-fee free tier) — no review text and no reviewer identities, ever. Returns `external` (the public rating and review count the listing carries, with `source`, the site it was read from) and `num_verified`: the average, count and 1–5 star distribution of ratings from verified guests — people who booked through Num and checked in at the venue by scanning its own code. Guests the venue comped or worked with are excluded, and Num publishes no verified average until a place has 5 such ratings (below that every number is null and `note` says why). Keep the two numbers separate; do not average them together. You MUST display the returned `attribution`.
tools.name: get_reviews

tools.description: Bulk, paged sync of every place Num lists in one destination — free (included in the no-fee free tier; one call returns up to 200 places), for keeping your own copy of the directory current instead of searching it call by call. Places Num has positive evidence have closed are excluded; `trading: null` means not yet checked, NOT closed. Contains no menus, reviews or photos — call get_menu, get_reviews or place_details for those. You MUST display the returned `attribution` wherever the data is shown.

description:
SubmitMyStartup is a free, AI- and MCP-ready guide to where to submit your startup. It covers startup directories, launch directories, SaaS directories and Product Hunt alternatives, with real submission results: whether each is really free, the catch, the fees and the wait. Get a shortlist from the planner, or connect Claude or ChatGPT to submitmystartup.com/mcp and ask where to launch your startup.

Remote MCP server at https://submitmystartup.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, read-only, no sign-in or API key). It is also in the official MCP Registry as com.submitmystartup/mcp. Docs: https://submitmystartup.com/api/#mcp

tools.description: Shortlist places to submit or launch a startup (directories, launch sites, communities, editorial sites) that fit a founder's product and limits. Use it when someone asks where to list, launch, or promote their startup or product. Returns a ranked list: Free with no catch first, then free with a catch, then paid by lowest listed price, then cost not on record. Within each group: shortest wait, then fewest unknown facts, then name. Never ranked by my own traffic results. Each result gives the cost and catch (cost, free), what the free path needs (needs), the wait, why it fits (why), which facts the query needs that are not on record (unknown), the list's notes, when it was last checked, and rowUrl, the place's row on the website. Leave out any filter that doesn't matter. Use get_directory for every fact about one place, and list_filters for allowed values and example arguments.

audience.description: Who the product is for. b2c drops places that only take business-to-business products (G2 and similar).

budget.description: The most the founder will pay for one listing, in USD unless currency is set. 0 means free paths only (free, and free with a catch). Leave out for any cost.

can_add_badge.description: false if the founder can't put a badge or backlink on their site. Default true.

cannot.description: Other requirements the founder can't meet: account, engagement (upvote, comment on, or rate other products first), socialProfile, phone, captcha, ownDomain, invitation, revenueProof. badge and domainEmail also work here.

categories.description: Only these sections of the list: directories, specialist (only for some startups), reddit, paid, problems.

country.description: Where the startup is based, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (AU, US, GB, IN); a country name such as Australia also works. Regional places limited to other countries drop out. Leave out for no region filter.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of budget. Default USD. Prices in another currency count as unknown.

domain_rating.description: The product site's domain rating, for places that set a minimum.

early_stage.description: true if the startup meets early-stage rules (for example under 5 years old, at most two institutional rounds).

formats.description: Only these listing formats: directory, launch (a dated launch), profile, editorial (a pitch for coverage), community (a post), app-review, review-site, gallery, beta-testing.

has_domain_email.description: false if the founder has no email address on the product's own domain (only Gmail or similar). Default true.

include_problem_sites.description: true to include places reported broken, inactive, closed, or dead. Default false.

limit.description: How many results to return, 1 to 50. Default 20.

markets.description: Markets the founder wants to reach (ISO alpha-2 codes or country names), for regional sites that cover a market or language rather than requiring a headquarters there.

offset.description: Skip this many results, for paging. Default 0.

product_types.description: What the product is, as tags (see list_filters), for example ["web-apps"] or ["saas", "developer-tools"]. Give only tags that are true of the product: a product without AI features leaves out ai-tools, so places that only take AI products drop out. web-apps also counts as software and websites; saas also counts as software, web-apps, and websites. Without tags, places limited to some products count as unknown.

released.description: true if the product is publicly released and usable, false if it is pre-release or in beta.

strict.description: true to drop places where any fact the query needs isn't on record. Default false: they stay in, with the unknown facts listed.

subdivision.description: ISO 3166-2 state or province, when a place is limited to one (US-WA). Implies the country.

within_days.description: The listing must go live within this many days on the free path. A place whose wait isn't on record counts as unknown.

tools.name: find_directories

tools.description: Every fact about one place on the list, for when a founder asks about a specific directory or launch site. Returns a short summary (cost and catch, what the free path needs, the wait, review, backlink, rowUrl), then the full record: the list's notes and Free? label, structured facts (cost, what it accepts, free-path requirements, wait, review, backlink), where each fact came from and when, the status of the maintainer's own attempt, and links. Look it up by id (from find_directories or search), name, or website URL.

id_or_name.description: The place's id (for example "indie-hackers"), its name ("Indie Hackers"), or its website ("indiehackers.com").

tools.name: get_directory

tools.description: The allowed values for find_directories: product types (and the types each implies), audiences, formats, sections of the list, requirements for cannot, the limited regions on record, price currencies, counts, and example arguments for common questions.
tools.name: list_filters

tools.description: Keyword search over the list of places to submit a startup. A place's exact name or website ("Indie Hackers", "indiehackers.com") puts it first. Asking for free ("free", "no cost", "$0") leaves out places that are paid only. Product words ("web app", "SaaS", "AI tool", "mobile app") keep only places that take that kind of product. Kind-of-place words ("launch site", "directory", "community") put places of that kind first. Other words match names, websites, regions, and the list's notes. For example "free launch sites for a web app", "AI tool directories", or "Australia". Returns up to 20 places, best match first, each with id, title, url (its row on submitmystartup.com, for citing), and a one-line summary. A query with no specific words returns the best free places. Use fetch with an id for the full record, and find_directories to shortlist by a founder's product and limits.

query.description: What to look for, in a few words.

Takes an id from search or find_directories; a name or website also works. Returns id, title, text, url (the place's row on the website, for citing), and metadata.

description:
# Cálculo Trabalhista

**Cálculo trabalhista** para IA. Atualize verbas e condenações da Justiça do Trabalho com correção oficial, juros e o salário mínimo do período. Índices e salário mínimo ao vivo, sem login.

Funciona em qualquer cliente MCP. Servidor remoto: `https://api.mcp.ai/p_calculo-trabalhista`

tools.description: Atualização monetária / liquidação de débito judicial: corrige parcelas por um índice oficial (IPCA, INPC, IGP-M, SELIC, TR…) e aplica juros, multa e honorários. Retorna detalhamento por parcela e totais. ATENÇÃO ao regime legal: SELIC já engloba correção+juros (não somar 1% a.m. por cima); pós-set/2024 o cível usa IPCA + taxa legal (Lei 14.905/2024).
tools.name: calculo_atualizar

tools.description: Consulta de índice oficial: fator de correção acumulado entre duas datas (mês inicial excluído, mês final incluído — convenção BACEN/IBGE). Se `valor` informado, retorna o valor corrigido; se `incluir_valores` true, retorna as variações mensais publicadas (puxar os índices crus).
tools.name: calculo_indice

tools.description: Salário mínimo nacional vigente de um ano (dinâmico, IPEADATA). Base para dosimetria (dia-multa), pensão por % do SM e mínimo existencial.
tools.name: calculo_salario_minimo

tools.description: Aluguéis em atraso (Lei 8.245/91): reajusta o aluguel ao longo do contrato pelo índice, corrige cada mês atrasado até hoje, aplica juros de mora (1% a.m.) e multa moratória. Retorna detalhamento por mês + total.
tools.name: calculo_aluguel

tools.description: Pensão alimentícia em atraso (art. 528 CPC): por mês do período calcula o devido (% do salário mínimo do mês, valor fixo ou % da remuneração), subtrai pagamentos e aplica correção (INPC) + juros 1% a.m. desde cada vencimento.
tools.name: calculo_pensao

tools.description: Verbas rescisórias / liquidação trabalhista (CLT): saldo de salário, aviso prévio indenizado (Lei 12.506/2011), 13º proporcional, férias proporcionais + 1/3, férias vencidas, multa de 40%/20% do FGTS, com descontos de INSS e IRRF (tabelas 2026). Verbas indenizatórias isentas.
tools.name: calculo_trabalhista

tools.description: Correção do FGTS (tese TR → INPC/IPCA-E, STF): por depósito calcula a diferença entre corrigir pelo índice de inflação vs pela TR, com juros de 3% a.a. da conta. Aceita depósitos manuais (ou, futuramente, extrato OCR).
tools.name: calculo_fgts

tools.description: Dosimetria da pena (art. 68 CP, sistema trifásico): pena-base pelas circunstâncias judiciais (art. 59), pena intermediária por atenuantes/agravantes (Súmula 231 STJ), pena definitiva por causas de aumento/diminuição (ex.: tentativa). Frações configuráveis.
tools.name: calculo_dosimetria

tools.description: Progressão de regime (LEP art. 112, Lei 13.964/2019): percentual de cumprimento por primário/reincidente × comum/hediondo × violência/resultado morte, descontando remição (trabalho/estudo) e detração, e retorna a data de progressão.
tools.name: calculo_progressao

tools.description: Partilha de bens no divórcio por regime (Código Civil): apura a massa partilhável (bens − dívidas conforme o regime) e a quota de cada cônjuge, com torna por desequilíbrio. Marque entra_partilha por bem para sobrepor o default do regime.
tools.name: calculo_partilha

tools.description: Tempo de contribuição (CNIS): soma os vínculos contando concomitância uma vez e converte atividade especial em comum (fatores EC 103/2019, só até 13/11/2019). Retorna tempo total e se atinge o tempo antigo (35H/30M).
tools.name: calculo_tempo_contribuicao

tools.description: RMI — Renda Mensal Inicial (pós-reforma EC 103/2019): média dos salários de contribuição × coeficiente (60% + 2% por ano acima de 20H/15M), com piso (salário mínimo) e teto (INSS).
tools.name: calculo_rmi

tools.description: Revisional de contrato bancário: recalcula o financiamento pela taxa média de mercado do BACEN (busca ao vivo por modalidade+mês) e apura o excedente por parcela (Price ou SAC). A taxa média é referência, não teto (STJ).
tools.name: calculo_revisional

tools.description: Superendividamento (Lei 14.181/2021): % da renda comprometida, mínimo existencial (R$600, parametrizável), renda disponível e capacidade de pagamento de um plano de até 5 anos.
tools.name: calculo_superendividamento

tools.description: RMC/RCC — reserva de margem consignável de cartão (INSS, códigos 217/268): limites de 5% e restituição corrigida dos descontos. Tese: cartão rotativo vendido como consignado que nunca amortiza.
tools.name: calculo_rmc_rcc

tools.description: Restituição de descontos indevidos no INSS (fraude associativa, códigos 280/304/310/378): soma as parcelas descontadas corrigidas. Ressarcimento administrativo via acordo STF (ADPF 1.236).
tools.name: calculo_restituicao_inss

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.
tools.name: marketplace
