tools.description: Get full details for a single task by its task code. A SYNC task's message is a JSON envelope: message (the summary line), results[] (type, name, action, status, code, error) and validation_errors[]. A result with status warning is informational; error and blocked results are failures. A local rule that rule placement moved has action renumbered, with its old and new sequence in before/after. A FIRMWARE_TRACK task is a step of a firmware track (enroll, advance or unenroll) created by the control plane, never by a client. Once it completes, firmware_track_result holds the parsed result: action, track, outcome (success, noop, held, released), reason (a closed code; ndcli.firmware.status lists them), drift (the pin had been changed outside NetDefense), reinstall_entries, and from_version, to_version, target_version and pinned_version when the device reported them. An advance that carried a major upgrade (the move to the next OPNsense series) also has kind "major" on every answer from the moment the agent decided to run it, a hold included, with target_version the series, and notes, what the agent found on the way, each one of: boot_environment_made (a ZFS boot environment was made before the upgrade); boot_environment_skipped_no_room (no boot environment was made: the pool had no room for one); boot_environment_off (no boot environment was made: the device's setting is off); boot_environment_unavailable (no boot environment was made: the device has no ZFS, or making one failed); third_party_repository (a package repository from outside OPNsense and NetDefense is enabled on the device); third_party_package (a package from outside OPNsense and NetDefense is installed on the device). A task that is still pending or that failed carries a plain-text message instead.
tools.name: ndcli.task.describe

description: Deep-time biodiversity over the Paleobiology Database — fossil occurrences, taxon ranges, diversity through time, and the geologic time scale, by clade, age, and place.

tools.description: Search fossil occurrences filtered by taxon, geologic time, geography, and depositional environment — the flagship. Use base_name for a clade and all its descendants (what "Tyrannosaurus occurrences" usually means), base_id for that same clade by resolved taxon id, or taxon_name for an exact taxon. Bound the age by a named interval (e.g. "Maastrichtian") or a max_ma/min_ma range, and/or a lng/lat bounding box; scope to a single locality with collection_no (take it from a paleobiology_search_collections row). At least one filter is required — taxon, time, place, environment, or collection_no. Every row carries two distinct coordinate systems — modern lng/lat (where the rock is today) and paleo lng/lat (where the landmass sat at deposition) — plus the formation, age interval, and higher classification (phylum through genus); never plot a deep-time occurrence on a modern coastline. Resolve a name with paleobiology_get_taxon first if unsure. Broad queries return many rows: an inline preview answers the immediate question, and when the set outgrows that preview the matching occurrences — up to the per-call cap — stage on a DataCanvas (canvas_id + table_name, returned only then) for SQL via paleobiology_dataframe_query (count by interval, group by formation/country, map by region). The response reports how many occurrences matched in total, which rows this page covers, and the offset that reaches the next page — page through the whole match set with limit/offset.

base_id.description: Clade-inclusive taxon filter by PBDB taxon id — the taxon_no from paleobiology_get_taxon, or accepted_no on an occurrence row. Same clade-inclusive semantics as base_name, but unambiguous where a name is not (homonyms, synonyms, unresolved spellings). Supply this or base_name, never both.

base_name.description: Clade-inclusive taxon filter — this taxon and all descendants, e.g. "Dinosauria". The usual choice. Supply this or base_id, never both.

canvas_id.description: Canvas id from a prior call to re-stage onto the same workspace. Reusing it REPLACES (overwrites) the prior occurrence table — each search restages the full result, it does not append to or accumulate across earlier ones. Omit to start fresh; the response returns a new id.

collection_no.description: Restrict to one collection (locality) by its PBDB collection_no — the fauna found together at that site. Take the id from a paleobiology_search_collections row to drill from a locality into its occurrences.

environment.description: Depositional environment: "marine", "terrestrial", or "freshwater" (lacustrine + fluvial). Omit for all.

interval.description: Named geologic interval bounding the age, e.g. "Cretaceous" or "Maastrichtian". Alternative to max_ma/min_ma.

latmax.description: Northern edge of the bounding box, decimal degrees (−90…90). Valid on its own — a lone latitude edge filters as a half-plane.

latmin.description: Southern edge of the bounding box, decimal degrees (−90…90). Valid on its own — a lone latitude edge filters as a half-plane.

limit.description: Maximum occurrences to pull per page (1–500). Caps the pull (further bounded by PBDB_MAX_OCCURRENCES); broad queries stage that page on the canvas for SQL. Pair with offset to walk the whole match set.

lngmax.description: Eastern edge of the bounding box, decimal degrees (−180…180). Longitude is a closed pair — supply lngmin with it or neither.

lngmin.description: Western edge of the bounding box, decimal degrees (−180…180). Longitude is a closed pair — supply lngmax with it or neither.

max_ma.description: Older age bound in millions of years ago. Alternative to interval. When paired with min_ma it must be strictly greater — max_ma is the deeper-time end of the window.

min_ma.description: Younger age bound in millions of years ago. Alternative to interval. When paired with max_ma it must be strictly smaller — min_ma is the nearer-to-present end of the window.

offset.description: Number of matching occurrences to skip before this page — page with limit by advancing offset. The response notice names the exact offset that reaches the next page.

taxon_name.description: Exact taxon filter — only this taxon, not descendants. Use instead of base_name when you want a single taxon.

tools.name: paleobiology_search_occurrences

tools.description: Resolve a taxon by name (e.g. "Tyrannosaurus") or by integer taxon_no to its accepted name, rank, higher classification, immediate parent, fossil occurrence count, and first/last appearance (FAD/LAD) range in millions of years — "when did this clade exist, and what is it." Run this first to resolve a name into the accepted name and taxon_no, then pass that id as base_id to paleobiology_search_occurrences, paleobiology_get_diversity, or paleobiology_search_collections for a clade-inclusive filter that carries no name ambiguity (the same id also appears as accepted_no on occurrence rows). Set show_children to also list immediate child taxa. PBDB taxonomy is opinionated and can differ from GBIF's backbone, so the accepted name may differ from the name you searched.

children_offset.description: Number of immediate children to skip before the returned page — used only when show_children is true. Advance it by 200 while children_truncated is true to walk the whole child list.

name.description: Taxon name to resolve, e.g. "Tyrannosaurus" or "Ammonoidea". Provide this or taxon_no.

show_children.description: When true, include a page of the immediate child taxa of this taxon (at most 200 per call — children_truncated says whether more remain).

taxon_no.description: PBDB taxon id from a prior get_taxon, or accepted_no on an occurrence row. Provide this or name.

tools.name: paleobiology_get_taxon

tools.description: Compute a diversity / origination / extinction curve for a clade across geologic time, binned by period, epoch, or age — answers "plot dinosaur genus diversity across the Mesozoic." Pass a clade-inclusive base_name (or base_id, the same clade by resolved taxon id — exactly one of the two) and bound the span by a named interval (e.g. "Mesozoic") or a max_ma/min_ma range; choose what to count (genera, species, or families) and the bin resolution. The full bin set returns inline — a diversity series is a bounded set of geologic intervals — so you read the curve, the turnover, and the per-bin origination/extinction directly. Counts reflect SAMPLED diversity, biased by collection effort and rock availability, not true past diversity.

base_id.description: Clade-inclusive taxon to count, by PBDB taxon id — the taxon_no from paleobiology_get_taxon, or accepted_no on an occurrence row. Same semantics as base_name, but unambiguous where a name is not (homonyms, synonyms, unresolved spellings). Supply this or base_name (exactly one is required, never both).

base_name.description: Clade-inclusive taxon to count, e.g. "Dinosauria" or "Ammonoidea" — this taxon and all descendants. Supply this or base_id (exactly one is required, never both).

count.description: What to count per bin: "genera" (default), "species", or "families".

interval.description: Named geologic interval bounding the span, e.g. "Mesozoic". Alternative to max_ma/min_ma.

max_ma.description: Older bound of the span in millions of years ago. Alternative to interval. When paired with min_ma it must be strictly greater — max_ma is the deeper-time end of the span.

min_ma.description: Younger bound of the span in millions of years ago. Alternative to interval. When paired with max_ma it must be strictly smaller — min_ma is the nearer-to-present end of the span.

tools.name: paleobiology_get_diversity

tools.description: Look up the geologic time scale — eons, eras, periods, epochs, and ages with their absolute-age boundaries in millions of years (Ma) and nesting. This is the reference that grounds every temporal filter on the other tools and translates a named interval like "Late Cretaceous" to its 100.5–66.0 Ma boundaries (and back). Filter by a name substring, a Ma range (overlap match), and/or a level; call with no filters to browse the full scale. Browsing and every name on the bundled ICS international-scale snapshot are answered offline. A name the snapshot does not carry — the sub-stage and regional names that occurrence and collection rows report, such as "Late Maastrichtian" or "Lancian" — costs one PBDB lookup across its other time scales; the response names which source answered and which scale the interval belongs to.

level.description: Restrict to one rank of the international scale: eon, era, period, epoch, or age (finest). Browsing is bounded to that scale, so the sub-stage and regional ranks are not selectable here.

max_ma.description: Older bound of an age window (Ma); intervals overlapping [min_ma, max_ma] match.

min_ma.description: Younger bound of an age window (Ma); intervals overlapping [min_ma, max_ma] match.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring of the interval name, e.g. "cretaceous" or "Jurassic". A name the bundled international scale does not carry is matched exactly against PBDB's other time scales.

tools.name: paleobiology_list_intervals

tools.description: Find fossil collections (localities) by area and geologic time — "what has been dug up here, and from what rock." Each locality returns its location, age (named interval and Ma), formation and strata, lithology, depositional environment, and the count of co-occurring fossils. Filter by a clade-inclusive base_name (or base_id, the same clade by resolved taxon id), a named interval or max_ma/min_ma range, a lng/lat bounding box, a formation or lithology name, and/or an environment. Results page inline via limit/offset (the response discloses when more remain). Take a collection_no from a row and pass it — or the same bbox+interval — to paleobiology_search_occurrences to see the actual fauna found together.

base_id.description: Clade-inclusive taxon filter by PBDB taxon id — the taxon_no from paleobiology_get_taxon, or accepted_no on an occurrence row. Same semantics as base_name, but unambiguous where a name is not (homonyms, synonyms, unresolved spellings). Supply this or base_name, never both.

base_name.description: Clade-inclusive taxon filter — localities yielding this taxon or its descendants, e.g. "Dinosauria". Supply this or base_id, never both.

environment.description: Depositional environment: "marine", "terrestrial", or "freshwater" (lacustrine + fluvial). Omit for all.

formation.description: Geologic formation name to filter by, e.g. "Hell Creek".

interval.description: Named geologic interval bounding the age, e.g. "Maastrichtian". Alternative to max_ma/min_ma.

latmax.description: Northern edge of the bounding box, decimal degrees (−90…90). Valid on its own — a lone latitude edge filters as a half-plane.

latmin.description: Southern edge of the bounding box, decimal degrees (−90…90). Valid on its own — a lone latitude edge filters as a half-plane.

limit.description: Maximum localities to return per page (1–500).

lithology.description: Lithology (rock type) to filter by, e.g. "sandstone".

lngmax.description: Eastern edge of the bounding box, decimal degrees (−180…180). Longitude is a closed pair — supply lngmin with it or neither.

lngmin.description: Western edge of the bounding box, decimal degrees (−180…180). Longitude is a closed pair — supply lngmax with it or neither.

max_ma.description: Older age bound in millions of years ago. When paired with min_ma it must be strictly greater — max_ma is the deeper-time end of the window.

min_ma.description: Younger age bound in millions of years ago. When paired with max_ma it must be strictly smaller — min_ma is the nearer-to-present end of the window.

offset.description: Number of localities to skip — page with limit by advancing offset.

tools.name: paleobiology_search_collections

tools.description: Run a read-only SQL SELECT against occurrence result sets staged on a DataCanvas by paleobiology_search_occurrences. This is how you analyze a large fossil set without re-fetching it: count occurrences by early_interval, group by formation, country (cc), or accepted_name, or filter by a paleo/modern coordinate range. The classification column is JSON — roll up by rank with json_extract_string(classification, '$.family') (also $.phylum, $.class, $.order, $.genus). Staged rows are occurrences, so collection-only fields such as lithology are not present. Reference tables by the table_name that search_occurrences returned — call paleobiology_dataframe_describe first if you do not know the table or column names. SELECT only; writes and file-reading functions are rejected.

canvas_id.description: Canvas id returned by paleobiology_search_occurrences when its result spilled.

sql.description: A read-only SQL SELECT. Reference tables by the names paleobiology_search_occurrences / _describe returned.

tools.name: paleobiology_dataframe_query

tools.description: List the tables and their columns staged on a DataCanvas by paleobiology_search_occurrences. Call this before paleobiology_dataframe_query to discover the exact table_name and column names to reference in SQL.

tools.description: Le catalogue du droit formalisé : actes, prédicats avec signatures, frontières de couverture. C'est d'ici que viennent les NOMS des prédicats — ils ne doivent jamais être inventés. Mais ne commencez PAS par le catalogue pour trouver le bon acte : l'aperçu est vaste, et le titre d'un acte coïncide rarement avec les mots d'une question (« Newton's laws of motion » ne contient pas le mot « physics »). Une question dans vos propres mots va d'abord à law_search, qui renvoie des adresses ; le catalogue sert à la signature exacte de ce que vous avez trouvé. Sans arguments — l'aperçu : une ligne par acte (clé, titre, ordre juridique, compteurs de règles, faits, signatures, normes, constantes) ; un acte entier — package="kz-gpk" ; une recherche sur les signatures, étiquettes et constantes de tous les actes — query="substring". Les trois modes sont PAGINÉS : limit et offset, le reste nommé dans le texte (`showing a–b of N; k more`) et dans structuredContent (total, truncated, next — un appel de continuation tout prêt). L'unité d'une page est nommée par pageUnit : l'aperçu et query paginent les ACTES (20 et 20 par défaut), package=… pagine les SIGNATURES d'un acte (20 par défaut, 300 au plus) — les grands codes en portent des milliers. package=… avec catalog=… pagine une liste séparée de l'acte : "questions" — le CATALOGUE DES QUESTIONS : quelles demandes sont prévues (une question en mots, une forme, un prédicat ou des normes) et à quoi l'acte NE répond PAS, avec le type de motif ; une fiche est un modèle de demande, non une réponse, et tous les actes n'en ont pas ; "norms" — les NORMES de l'acte, "constants" — les CONSTANTES (noms des déclarations). "task-guides" — les PARCOURS DE TÂCHE : l'ordre d'application d'un canon à un document — quoi recueillir, quelles cartes interroger et comment lire les réponses ; un parcours ne répond à rien. catalog="task-guides" est admis aussi sans package — tous les parcours du profil ; guide=… — le détail d'un parcours ; le parcours lui-même — MCP Prompts sous le même nom. Le détail d'un acte imprime un aperçu de ces listes et nomme le compte et l'appel tout prêt du mode.

catalog.description: avec package : paginer le catalogue des questions, les normes, les constantes ou les parcours de tâche de l'acte au lieu de ses signatures ; "task-guides" aussi sans package : tous les parcours de tâche du profil

guide.description: avec catalog="task-guides" : le détail d'un parcours — un nom <paquet>/<id> (comme dans prompts/list) ou un id avec package

limit.description: combien par page : actes (aperçu 20, query 20), signatures d'un acte (20, 300 au plus) ou éléments d'une liste catalog (questions 20, normes 20, constantes 100, parcours de tâche 20)

offset.description: à partir de quel élément de la page (0) ; l'unité est le pageUnit de la réponse

package.description: les signatures complètes de cet acte

query.description: un filtre de sous-chaîne sur signatures, étiquettes et constantes (sans distinction de casse)

tools.name: law_packages

tools.description: Poser une question au droit formalisé. Quand la réponse est « non établi », elle porte whyNot — le rapport why_not du moteur : les règles candidates et l'état de chaque conjonct (satisfait / non satisfait / indéterminé) ; les faits manquants y sont visibles et n'ont pas à être inventés. AVANT LE PREMIER appel, obtenez les noms de prédicats par law_search (une question dans vos propres mots → adresses) ou law_packages (les signatures d'un acte connu) — un nom inventé sera rejeté. Si l'outil a renvoyé une erreur ou « non établi », C'EST LA RÉPONSE : transmettez-la à l'utilisateur et ne la substituez pas par des connaissances générales sur le droit d'un autre pays. Mais « je n'ai trouvé aucun acte convenable » N'EST PAS une réponse tant que law_search n'a pas été interrogé : le silence du catalogue est une propriété de la recherche par titre, non une conclusion sur le corpus. kind='truth' — si un fait est établi ; kind='collect' — énumérer les enregistrements ; kind='deadline' — calculer un délai sur le calendrier officiel ; kind='positions' — quelles OBLIGATIONS sont nées des faits et quels sont leurs statuts ; kind='why_not' — le rapport why_not sur le même but, quel que soit le statut de la réponse. La réponse porte les règles appliquées, les avertissements et la provenance avec empreintes ; truth/collect portent aussi un bloc signature pour la présentation. Le serveur n'invente pas : là où une norme n'est pas formalisée, la réponse est « non établi » ou une erreur.

args.description: les arguments du prédicat dans l'ordre de sa signature ; avec kind='collect', exactement l'un d'eux est la variable de sélection ?name (par exemple ['urn:x:water', 'urn:x:mix', '?value']), les autres sont des valeurs. Les valeurs suivent le type du paramètre : une entité — 'urn:…' ou un nom court ; Date — 'YYYY-MM-DD' ; Money — '<nombre> <devise>' ('43250 KZT') ; Quantity — '<nombre> <unité>' avec l'unité exactement telle que le paquet l'écrit ; une constante du paquet — son nom

calc.description: kind='calc' : un arbre {op,left,right}, op ∈ add|sub|mul|div|le|lt|ge|gt|eq|ne (les synonymes divide/multiply/plus/minus et les signes sont acceptés) ; les feuilles sont 5 | '3932 KZT' | '2 mrp' | {lookup: 'mrp', args: [2026]} — une valeur légale du corpus ; les agrégats sont {aggregate: 'sum', element: '?v', over: [{predicate, args with '?variables'}]} sur les faits donnés dans facts

context.description: Contexte temporel explicite : timezone est un nom IANA ; decisionTime et knowledgeTime sont des instants complets avec UTC ou un décalage, conservés sans substitution. legalTime est aussi requis avec context ; le profil peut exiger tous ces champs

cutoff.description: deadline : l'heure de clôture des opérations

days.description: deadline : la durée de la période

deadlinePolicy.description: la politique de décompte des délais exprimés en jours : le StableId d'une deadline policy déclarée dans le monde de la question (p. ex. 'urn:kz:corpus:clir:administrative-code#AC_WORKING_DAY_TERMS'), ou son nom court lorsqu'une seule déclaration le porte. Un objet en ligne {start_count: 'same_day'|'next_day', include_end: true|false, roll: 'no_roll'|'next_working_day'|'previous_working_day'[, month_end: 'last_day_of_month']} n'est accepté que par un monde 0.1 ; un monde 0.2 le refuse, et le refus nomme les politiques déclarées. Sans politique, une norme portant un délai répond MISSING_POLICY — la politique est fixée par le droit de la procédure et le serveur n'en suppose jamais une. L'instantané du calendrier officiel pour les jours ouvrables est fourni par le serveur lui-même dès qu'un acte les compte.

evidence.description: documents de l'affaire, section 74, nœuds evidence_item. Un document est référencé depuis provenance.evidence de plusieurs faits. payload.confidence est une donnée pour l'EvidencePolicy ; le moteur n'évalue pas le nombre

evidencePolicy.description: StableId d'un nœud evidence_policy, section 78.2. Sans lui, les appels précédents gardent leur comportement. Le seuil de confidence est une règle de cette politique, pas un argument de l'appel

facts.description: faits de l'affaire : [{predicate, args, provenance, negated?, package?, judgment?}]. provenance est obligatoire et doit être un objet ; {} est accepté. Ses champs sont facultatifs : {origin?, evidence?: StableId, span?: {page?, quote?, offset?}, extractor?: {name, version?, confidence?}, observedAt?, recordedAt?}. origin vaut case_input par défaut. evidence et observedAt ne sont pas obligatoires ; l'extracteur est abaissé en was_generated_by et le document en was_derived_from. confidence est une chaîne décimale ; le seuil est lu par l'EvidencePolicy du paquet, pas par l'hôte. package résout un nom court ambigu ; args suit la même notation que les args de la question

focused.description: kind='truth' : poser la question en focused_truth — la même réponse que le truth complet, mais la preuve et les avertissements ne couvrent que le cône de la question ; la réponse porte evaluationKind et les empreintes de la coupe (focus) ; dans focus, le cône est réduit à coneHash et au nombre de prédicats, le manifeste complet du cône vient dans evaluation.focusManifest avec proof=true. Une coupe n'est pas un document d'audit : law_prepare_answer ne l'accepte pas pour publication

kind.description: le type de question (truth par défaut)

package.description: restreindre la question à un paquet de droit

predicate.description: ce qui est demandé, p. ex. 'duty_amount'

responseMode.description: full (défaut) — la réponse complète. compact est accepté par compatibilité : ce serveur ne construit pas de réponse courte et renvoie la même réponse complète dans les deux modes ; il n'y a ni référence fullAnswer ni instantané enregistré de la réponse.

selectedInterpretations.description: lectures nommées ; pour un groupe exactly_one, choisir exactement un StableId parmi law_packages/law_rules

supportEdges.description: appuis, section 75, nœuds support_edge : from est l'id du document, to est le littéral du fait, relation est supports ou refutes. L'admission est décidée par l'EvidencePolicy du paquet, pas par l'hôte

version.description: la version exacte du paquet figée par le client (open('name@version')) ; si elle diffère de la composition du profil, l'hôte refuse au lieu de répondre avec une autre version

tools.description: Construire une condition nécessaire — un surensemble — pour la présélection de lignes d'une source externe. Ce n'est PAS une réponse juridique et PAS du SQL : le résultat est un arbre typé et un manifeste des extensions jusqu'à TRUE. Chaque ligne qui passe doit ensuite être calculée en entier par le moteur, avec un graphe de preuve, sur le même instantané des données. Le binding est passé comme objet épinglable ; sourceSchemaContentHash est l'empreinte réelle du schéma source et est comparée bruyamment avec l'épingle. Les faits d'affaire qui portent une provenance (origin, document, citation, extractor) sont fournis à law_ask, pas ici. Le nombre confidence est lu par l'EvidencePolicy du paquet, pas par cet outil et pas par le moteur.

tools.description: Déplier la preuve d'une réponse law_ask en une chaîne « règle ← prémisses → conclusion ». L'entrée compacte : question (les arguments law_ask d'origine, truth/collect), resultHash et codeHash issus de la provenance de la réponse. Le serveur répète le calcul et compare les empreintes ; si quelque chose a changé, il refuse explicitement. Autrement, passer l'évaluation de law_ask(proof=true). answerResource=fullAnswer.uri explique un instantané compact stocké sans recalcul et sans que le client charge des pages ; par défaut seulement la chaîne proofRef. nodeId sélectionne un nœud et toutes ses prémisses (jusqu'à 24 Ko, sinon un refus explicite). proofHash se rapporte au graphe entier ; scope marque la partie sélectionnée.

Rien n'est évalué ni recalculé : la source est evaluation de law_ask(proof=true) ou un answerResource. Une donnée absente est un état de limite (limits), jamais une négation.

La question est du JSON selon query.schema.json (query), une chaîne evaluate (evaluate + queryId), un queryId enregistré sans query, ou card + args. tools.description: Une requête LawQL déterministe sur le CLIR d'une formalisation : une question sur le modèle de l'acte lui-même, pas sur une affaire. Relations (14) : anchors, edges, fields, imports, interpretations, labels, links, literals, nodes, norms, positions, rules, variables, windows. Listes des champs : `law query --schema`. Fonctions (9) : anchor/1, labels/1..2, short/1, contains/2, overlaps/2, starts_with/2, ends_with/2, position/2, derivation/2. exists/not exists sur une variable liée ; égalité et appartenance seulement, sans arithmétique ni comparaisons d'ordre. Périmètre : corpus par package.name (par exemple kz.corpus.labour_code, pas un nom de fichier) ou un glob ; sans corpus, toute la tranche du profil ; un périmètre hors profil est vide (CORPUS_EMPTY). Exemples : `from r in rules where r.head_predicate == "urn:…#eligible" select r.id as producer, r.strength as strength, anchor(r.id) as anchors` — qui produit ; `from l in literals where l.predicate == "urn:…#eligible" select l.node as reader, l.context as context` — qui lit ; `query eligible over "pkg" { for x: Person; where applicant(x); select eligible(x); }` — inférence par le noyau. C'est une orchestration au-dessus du CLIR et du noyau ; aucune sémantique juridique nouvelle n'est implémentée ici. Au lieu du texte, une question du catalogue avec arguments : anchors-of, imports-of, links-of, producers, readers, type-step (composition : `law query --list`) (les paramètres predicate/node/type sont des URN, pkg un package.name ou un glob). La réponse structurelle est une queryPage : resultHash du queryResult complet, snapshot (hachage de la liste des paquets du périmètre), rowCount, rows selon rowLimit (20, au plus 5000) et rowOffset, next avec le snapshot pour continuer ; full: true renvoie le queryResult complet quand le périmètre est un seul paquet. Chaque ligne porte sa provenance (nœuds CLIR) ; une réponse vide porte l'entonnoir explain (emptyAt nomme la clause) ; les erreurs portent des codes LDC-Qxxxx avec des indices ; un produit de sources trop large est refusé avant exécution (QUERY_TOO_BROAD), une continuation sur un autre instantané — SNAPSHOT_CHANGED.

question.description: le nom d'une question du catalogue de questions nommées (producers, readers, anchors-of, imports-of, links-of, type-step) ou d'un lint ; à la place de query

tools.description: The official mcp.ai marketplace — the in-platform catalog of every MCP/tool, AND the way to run them. Covers capability requests like "find an MCP that does X", "consulta um CPF", "is there a tool for Y". Core flow: action=search discovers MCPs by intent → describe returns one MCP's full profile (every tool with its id + params, pricing, auth) so you pick the right tool_id → invoke RUNS that tool. KEY: invoke works even when the MCP is NOT installed — it runs the tool pontualmente (one-off), without adding the MCP to the toolkit and without bloating the tool list. If the MCP needs a credential/login, invoke returns a connect link; if it is paid and the wallet is empty, invoke returns a checkout/top-up link (the user opens it, then you retry). Use install only to make an MCP PERMANENT in the active toolkit (its tools then show up natively in future sessions); prefer invoke for a single/occasional use. list_tools lists what is callable right now. subscribe/cancel handle per-MCP billing; report_bug sends feedback; request_mcp asks us to build a NEW MCP when nothing fits. Search/describe flag installed_in_toolkit vs installed_in_workspace. Writes (install/uninstall/subscribe/cancel and the one-off install behind invoke) require workspace owner/admin. It also carries the mcp.ai PROMPT LIBRARY, which is about ready-made prompt TEXT rather than MCPs: search_prompts finds one, get_prompt returns its full text with {{variables}} filled, and publish_prompt saves a prompt and returns a shareable mcp.ai/p/<slug> link that opens without login.

activityUrn.description: The post's activity URN (e.g. "urn:li:activity:7404116397871607808") or a LinkedIn post URL. Obtain from linkedin_get_post_comments or linkedin_get_person_posts output.

cursor.description: Continuation cursor from a previous call. Pass this to fetch the next batch of nested comments.

Returns reactor profiles and reaction types (like, celebrate, support, love, insightful, funny).

activityUrn.description: Activity URN from a prior linkedin_get_person_posts call (e.g. "urn:li:activity:7139995994070454272"). Preferred over postUrl.

commentId.description: Optional. commentId of a comment on the post (from linkedin_get_post_comments / linkedin_get_nested_comments output). When provided, returns the reactions on that comment instead of the post. Requires a connected LinkedIn account.

cursor.description: Continuation cursor from a previous call. Pass this to fetch the next batch of reactions.

postUrl.description: LinkedIn post URL (e.g. https://www.linkedin.com/posts/john-doe-...-activity-123-xxxx). Use when activityUrn is not available.

tools.name: linkedin_get_post_reactions

include_demographics.description: Include top demographics breakdown (seniority, location, industry, etc.) of who viewed the post. Defaults to false.

post.description: A LinkedIn post URL or activity URN. Accepts /feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>, /posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<hash>, or urn:li:activity:<id>.

Some entries are aggregated (e.g. "1 person at <Company>", "N people using LinkedIn Recruiter") and have no profile URN.

start.description: Offset into the viewer list for pagination. Use the `nextStart` value from a prior response. Defaults to 0 (first page).

Use linkedin_get_person_posts to fetch full post detail for any returned activityUrn. Paginate by passing the `nextStart` from a prior response as `start`.

start.description: Offset into the saved-items list for pagination. Use the `nextStart` value from a prior response. Defaults to 0 (first page).

type.description: Which saved-items section to fetch. Currently only "posts" is supported (more variants — jobs, learning, projects — may be added later).

tools.name: linkedin_get_my_saved_items

Every item carries the permalink of the engaged post (postUrl + activityUrn) — pass either to linkedin_get_post_comments / linkedin_get_post_reactions to see who else engaged. For comments, commentId can be used as parentCommentId in linkedin_get_nested_comments to list replies to your comment; for reactions left on a comment, commentId identifies the comment you reacted to. Paginate by passing the returned cursor back with the same type (cursors are type-specific; the final page may be empty).

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response of the same type.

type.description: Which engagement activity to list: "comments" (comments you wrote) or "reactions" (reactions you gave).

tools.description:
Rank teams by how overdue a draw is — the question this database exists to answer.

Every team has a historical draw rate and a run of matches since its last draw. When
the run is long relative to how often that team normally draws, the team is carrying
"draw debt", and this tool ranks the whole field by it, most overdue first. Ask it
"which national teams are most due a draw?" or "who is overdue a draw in the World
Cup 2026 field?" and it answers directly; nothing else here needs to be queried first.

Each entry returns the rank, the score, and the signals behind it: matches played,
draws, draw percentage, the current no-draw streak, the longest ever, and the debt
figure. Filters subset which teams are listed — a team's score and rank are global and
never change with them. Historical pattern, not a betting tip.

Costs 1 point per call (1 point = 1 cent); paginated calls cost 1 point per page.

limit.description: How many ranked teams to return. Default 25, max 500. One call, one point, whatever the limit.

recent.description: Only teams with a recent match, so the answer is about teams currently playing. Default true.

type.description: Restrict the ranking to national teams or to clubs. Omit to rank both together.

wc2026.description: Restrict to the 2026 World Cup team group. Default false.

tools.name: predict_draws

tools.description:
How overdue a draw one named team is, plus the results that made it so.

Returns the team's draw-likelihood rank and score among all ranked teams, the signals
behind it (draw rate, current no-draw streak, longest ever, draw debt), and its recent
form — every match in the current no-draw run, with opponent, score and side. Use this
when the question is about a specific team ("is Brazil due a draw?"); use predict_draws
when the question is about the field.

The prediction comes back null when the team exists but is not currently ranked (no
played matches, or excluded by the `recent` filter). Historical pattern, not a betting tip.

Costs 1 point per call (1 point = 1 cent); paginated calls cost 1 point per page.

recent.description: Rank within teams that have played recently, matching predict_draws. Default true.

team.description: Numeric team id or slug — 431 or "arsenal". Both come from list_teams.

wc2026.description: Rank within the 2026 World Cup team group. Default false.

tools.name: get_team_prediction

tools.description:
Every draw reading FDB4 holds for ONE match — use it when someone asks how likely a
specific fixture is to end level, rather than which teams are overdue a draw
(`predict_draws` answers that).

Five readings come back side by side, because they are not interchangeable: the
Dixon-Coles goals model's own probability with the expected goals behind it; the
historical draw rate at this fixture's Elo rating gap; the one-parameter blend of
those two the site has published since September 2026; the five-feature logistic
model that now sits beside it with a 95% band around it; and the bookmaker's draw
price where one is recorded. Also returned: when the logistic model was last fitted,
over how many matches, and its coefficients — so an answer can explain itself.

Identify the match by `match_id`, or by `team` (id or slug) plus an optional `date`;
with no date you get that team's next fixture. `is_forecast` says whether the
logistic figure is a real forecast (a fixture) or an in-sample description of a
match the model was fitted on. Historical pattern, not a betting tip.

Costs 1 point per call (1 point = 1 cent); paginated calls cost 1 point per page.

date.description: With `team`, the match date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for that team's next fixture.

match_id.description: The match id, from search_results or a fixture list. Give this or `team`.

team.description: A team id or slug (431, arsenal), from list_teams. Give this or `match_id`.

tools.name: get_draw_model

tools.description:
The all-time leaderboard of no-draw runs — the longest any team has gone without drawing.

Answers "what is the longest run of matches without a draw on record?" and "who else has
done it?". Each entry is one run: its length, the dates it started and ended, and the
team. A team can appear more than once, since a great side may have several long runs.
Filter to one team, to national teams or clubs, or to runs above a minimum length.

Paginated, 25 per page by default; `page` walks the leaderboard and each page costs its
own point.

Costs 1 point per call (1 point = 1 cent); paginated calls cost 1 point per page.

min.description: Minimum run length to list. Default 5.

page.description: Page number, from 1. Each page is a separate call and costs its own point.

team_id.description: Restrict to one team. Numeric id from list_teams.

type.description: Restrict to national teams or to clubs.

tools.name: top_streaks

tools.description:
Every no-draw run one team has ever had, plus the one it is on now.

A no-draw run is a sequence of matches that ended in a win or a loss. This returns the
run currently in progress with each match in it — date, competition, opponent, score —
so you can say exactly when the team last drew and what has happened since, together
with every recorded run in the team's history, longest first, each with its start and
end dates.

Runs span all competitions; per-competition runs are not split out.

Free: no key needed, and it costs a key holder nothing either.

team.description: Numeric team id or slug — 431 or "arsenal". Find either with list_teams.

tools.name: get_team_streaks

tools.description:
Find a team and its id — the lookup every other team tool depends on.

Search by name prefix with `q` ("arse" finds Arsenal), or browse by first letter, or
list one kind of team. Each row carries the numeric id and the slug that get_team,
get_team_streaks, get_team_prediction, head_to_head and search_results take.

The database holds thousands of teams, so an unfiltered call returns the first 25 with
the full total beside them. Always pass `q` when you know the name.

Free: no key needed, and it costs a key holder nothing either.

letter.description: First letter A-Z to browse by, or "#" for names starting with a non-letter.

limit.description: How many teams to return. Default 25; the total number of matches is always reported.

q.description: Name prefix, matched against both the short and the full name. The fastest way to find one team.

type.description: Restrict to national teams or to clubs.

tools.name: list_teams

tools.description:
One team's profile and its all-time draw statistics.

Returns the team's name, country and type alongside the numbers this database is built
on: matches played, draws, draw percentage, the no-draw streak currently running, the
longest one ever, the average of its longest runs, its draw debt and its rank in the
draw-likelihood field. Use it to answer "how often does this team draw?" or "how long
since they last drew?".

Takes a numeric id or a slug, whichever you already hold; both come from list_teams.

Free: no key needed, and it costs a key holder nothing either.

team.description: Numeric team id or slug — 431 or "arsenal". Find either with list_teams.

tools.name: get_team

tools.description:
Every competition covered — leagues, domestic cups, continental cups, World Cups — with
how many matches and how many draws each one holds.

Two uses. Without `tournament` it answers "what is in this database, and how draw-heavy
is each competition?", returning each competition's id, slug, country, match count, draw
count and draw percentage. With `tournament` (an id or slug) it returns that one
competition in full: the years it covers, every edition newest first with its champion
where one was decided, and the all-time winners ranking with title counts and years.

The competition ids here are what search_results and head_to_head filter by.

Free: no key needed, and it costs a key holder nothing either.

limit.description: How many competitions to list. Default 25; the total is always reported.

tournament.description: One competition, by numeric id or slug (53 or "norway-cup"). Returns its editions, champions and all-time winners instead of the list.

tools.name: list_tournaments

tools.description:
Every country in the database, with its FIFA code and id.

Use it to turn a country name into the id and FIFA code the rest of the data is keyed
by, or to check which countries are covered at all. Search with `q`, which matches a
name prefix or an exact FIFA code ("ENG"). Countries that no longer exist are included
and flagged, because the match archive still holds their games.

Free: no key needed, and it costs a key holder nothing either.

limit.description: How many countries to return. Default 25; the total is always reported.

q.description: Country name prefix, or an exact FIFA code such as ENG or BRA.

tools.name: list_countries

tools.description:
Search the match archive: finished matches, newest first, with scores.

This is the raw history behind every other tool — decades of results across national
team football, domestic leagues and cups. Filter by team, competition, single season,
outcome (home win, away win or draw) and date range, in any combination: "Arsenal's
draws since 2020", "every match in the 2025/26 Premier League", "all draws in the World
Cup". Each match returns its date, competition and edition, both teams, the score and
whether it was a draw.

Results are paginated, 50 per page by default; `page` walks through them and
`meta.total` tells you how many matches matched before you start.

Free, no key needed, for recent results: the first page of 50, and any `from` date
inside the last 7 days. Reaching further back — an older `from`, a bigger `limit`, or
page 2 onward — is the archive and costs 1 point per call (1 point = 1 cent), one point
per page.

competition_id.description: Restrict to one competition. Id from list_tournaments.

competition_item_id.description: Restrict to a single edition or season. Edition ids come from list_tournaments with a `tournament` argument.

from.description: Earliest match date, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD. Inside the last 7 days the call is free and needs no key; earlier than that it costs 1 point.

limit.description: Page size: 50, 100, 250 or 500. Default 50, which is also the largest free page. Anything else is treated as 100.

outcome.description: H for a home win, A for an away win, D for a draw.

page.description: Page number, from 1. Page 1 can be free; every page after it is a separate call and costs its own point.

team_id.description: Matches involving this team, home or away. Numeric id from list_teams.

to.description: Latest match date, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD.

type.description: Restrict to national-team or club football.

tools.description:
The complete record between two teams, and every match they have ever played.

Answers "who wins more between these two, and how often do they draw?" — matches
played, wins each way, draws, goals each way and the draw percentage, all from team A's
perspective, followed by every meeting with its date, competition and score. Optionally
narrow to one competition type or a single edition to compare only their league games,
or only one season.

Both teams are given as numeric ids, which list_teams returns.

Costs 1 point per call (1 point = 1 cent); paginated calls cost 1 point per page.

description: MCP server for reading and writing Obsidian vault documents via EVC Team Relay

tools.description:
Check which auth mode is active (agent key or email/password) and log in if needed.

    Takes no arguments; call it first, once, before any other tool.

    In agent-key mode (RELAY_AGENT_KEY or RELAY_AGENT_KEYS is set): no login
    is needed — each request carries X-Agent-Key directly, this just reports
    which mode is active.

    In email/password mode: logs in with the RELAY_EMAIL and RELAY_PASSWORD
    env vars. The resulting token is managed internally; subsequent tool
    calls use it automatically — you never need to pass it yourself.
tools.name: authenticate

tools.description:
List the shared folders and documents this key or account can access.

    Only lists what auth mode/key was granted — it does not create or change
    access. Example: `list_shares(kind="folder")`.

    In multi-key mode (RELAY_AGENT_KEYS set): returns metadata for every share
    that has a configured key, fetched via per-share agent-key auth.

    RELAY_AGENT_KEYS is typically keyed by share UUID, but the bare
    share-metadata endpoint (/v1/web/shares/{ref}) only resolves web slugs —
    a UUID always 404s there. When that happens this falls back to the
    UUID-addressable files-index endpoint, which proves the share is real
    and reachable but can't report kind/path/visibility (reported as
    kind="unknown", plus a file_count instead).

    A per-share failure (bad key, wrong share, share genuinely gone) is
    NEVER silently dropped — it lands in the response's `errors` field.
    "Couldn't check this share" and "checked, it doesn't exist" must stay
    distinguishable; collapsing both into an empty list is what let a
    config/auth problem read as "you have no shares".

    In single-key mode (RELAY_AGENT_KEY only): returns an empty list — the
    single key is tied to one share but its identity is unknown; call list_files
    or tr_search directly with the known share_id.

    In email/password mode: returns all shares the user has access to.

    Args:
        kind: Filter by share type — "doc" or "folder". Empty for all.
        owned_only: If true, only return shares owned by the user (email/password mode only).

    Returns:
        On full success: a bare JSON array of shares (id, kind, path,
        visibility, user_role — or id/kind="unknown"/file_count for
        UUID-resolved entries).
        If any share failed to resolve: a JSON object
        {"shares": [...], "errors": {share_ref: "reason"}} instead of a
        silently-shortened array.

kind.description: Filter by share kind: "doc" or "folder". Empty string returns all kinds.
kind.title: Kind

owned_only.description: Only return shares owned by the authenticated user. Email/password mode only; ignored in agent-key mode.
owned_only.title: Owned Only

tools.name: list_shares

tools.description:
List every file in a shared folder with its metadata.

    Read-only; does not download file contents (use read_file for that).

    In agent-key mode (RELAY_AGENT_KEYS or RELAY_AGENT_KEY is set): uses the
    agent-key endpoint; share_id may be a UUID or web slug.

    In email/password mode: share_id must be a UUID.

    Args:
        share_id: UUID or web slug of the folder share, e.g.
            "a1b2c3d4-..." or "research-vault".

    Returns:
        Object with share_id and files map (path -> metadata). The exact set
        of metadata keys per file is server-controlled, hence the loose
        dict[str, Any] shape rather than a strict per-field schema.

share_id.description: UUID or web slug of the folder share, as returned by list_shares.
share_id.title: Share Id

tools.name: list_files

tools.description:
Find files in a shared folder by a case-insensitive match on path or name.

    Read-only; does not download file contents (use read_file for that).
    Example: `tr_search(share_id="research-vault", query="roadmap")`.

    In agent-key mode (RELAY_AGENT_KEY is set): share_id may be UUID or web slug.
    In email/password mode: share_id must be a UUID.

    Args:
        share_id: UUID or web slug of the folder share.
        query: Search string matched case-insensitively against file paths.
        limit: Max results to return (default 20).

    Returns:
        JSON list of matching files:
        [{"id": doc_id_or_null, "title": filename_without_ext, "path": full_path,
          "relay_url": "relay://<slug>/<path>", "updated_at": null}]

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return.
limit.title: Limit

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against file paths.
query.title: Query

share_id.description: UUID or web slug of the folder share, as returned by list_shares.
share_id.title: Share Id

tools.name: tr_search

tools.description:
Read one file from a shared folder by its path.

    Read-only. Returns the full file content in one response — there is no
    partial/range read.

    In agent-key mode (RELAY_AGENT_KEY is set): fetches via the agent-key
    download endpoint; share_id may be a UUID or web slug.

    In email/password mode: fetches via the same CAS download endpoint used by
    agent-key mode, over Bearer JWT instead of X-Agent-Key; share_id must be a UUID.

    Args:
        share_id: UUID or web slug of the folder share.
        file_path: File path within the folder (e.g. "Marketing/plan.md").

    Returns:
        {"path", "content", "format"} on success, or {"error": ...} if the
        file doesn't exist — two distinct shapes on the same 200-equivalent
        outcome, hence dict[str, Any] rather than a strict per-field schema
        (a stricter schema would reject the error shape as invalid output).

file_path.description: Path to the file within the share, e.g. "notes/todo.md".
file_path.title: File Path

share_id.description: UUID or web slug of the folder share, as returned by list_shares.
share_id.title: Share Id

tools.name: read_file

tools.description:
Reserved for live document content; not yet available on the server, use read_file.

    Always raises: the control-plane has no REST route for reading a
    document's live content by ID for either DOC-kind shares or a
    folder-share file's doc_id (that concept doesn't exist in the current
    CAS-based folder sync model). This is a genuine backend gap, not an
    agent-key-vs-JWT restriction. Use read_file for folder shares instead —
    it works in both agent-key and JWT mode.

    Args:
        share_id: UUID of the share (for ACL check).
        doc_id: Document UUID. Defaults to share_id for doc shares.
        key: Yjs shared type key. Default "contents".

doc_id.description: Document UUID. Defaults to share_id when omitted.
doc_id.title: Doc Id

key.description: Yjs shared-type key holding the document content.
key.title: Key

share_id.description: UUID of the share, used for the access check.
share_id.title: Share Id

tools.name: read_document

tools.description:
Create or overwrite a file in a shared folder; it syncs into subscribers' vaults. Agent key only.

    **Write access is agent-key-only by design** — this is the sanctioned,
    permanent policy (not a temporary gap): agent-key mode is the only
    authorized write path in this MCP server.

    **Agent key mode** (RELAY_AGENT_KEY is set):
    - share_id may be the share UUID or web slug (e.g. "research-vault")
    - Folder shares use /sync-upload → file enters the CRDT sync store and
      appears in subscribers' local Obsidian vaults on the next sync cycle
    - Doc shares fall back to /upload (web-publish only)
    - list_files, read_file, and tr_search also work with the same agent key

    **Email/password (JWT) mode** — always raises; intentionally read-only.
    There is no write route reachable by JWT for an arbitrary (non-web-
    published) folder share, and even if one existed, JWT mode stays
    read-only by policy. Use agent-key mode for writes.

    Args:
        share_id: Share UUID (email/password mode) or web slug (agent key mode).
        file_path: File path within the share (e.g. "notes/todo.md").
        content: Full text content to write.

    Returns:
        Object with path, size/operation, and optional public_url (agent-key
        mode). The exact set of keys is server-controlled (plus the
        "operation" key added here), hence dict[str, Any].

content.description: Full text content to write, replacing the file if it already exists.
content.title: Content

file_path.description: Path to the file within the share, e.g. "notes/todo.md".
file_path.title: File Path

share_id.description: Share UUID (email/password mode) or web slug (agent-key mode).
share_id.title: Share Id

tools.name: upsert_file

tools.description:
Reserved for live document writes; not yet available on the server, use upsert_file.

    Always raises: the control-plane has no REST route for writing a
    document's live content by ID (doc-share content is CRDT/WebSocket-only).
    This is a genuine backend gap in BOTH agent-key and JWT mode, not an
    agent-key-vs-JWT restriction — but were a route ever added, per the
    sanctioned write policy (agent-key writes only) JWT mode would still be
    read-only.

    Args:
        share_id: UUID of the share (for ACL check).
        doc_id: Document UUID.
        content: Full text content to write (replaces entire document).
        key: Yjs shared type key. Default "contents".

content.description: Full text content to write, replacing the entire document.
content.title: Content

key.description: Yjs shared-type key holding the document content.
key.title: Key

share_id.description: UUID of the share, used for the access check.
share_id.title: Share Id

tools.name: write_document

tools.description:
Reserved for per-file deletion; not yet available on the server.

    Always raises: the control-plane has no DELETE route for an individual
    folder-share file in ANY auth mode (agent-key or JWT) — this isn't a
    JWT-vs-agent-key gap, per-file deletion simply isn't implemented
    server-side yet. Note this is independent of the agent-key-only write
    policy that governs upsert_file: even once/if a delete route lands, it
    would follow that same policy (agent-key-only, JWT read-only).

    Args:
        share_id: UUID of the folder share.

description: The connector is a production remote MCP server for qualified real-estate investors and wholesalers. It lets each authenticated user connect their own AggREIgator account to review investment criteria and deal inventory, then selectively enable controlled platform workflows.

tools.description: Return the authenticated buyer's current buy-box: markets, strategies, property types, condition range and per-strategy price/ARV/cash-flow bounds. Read-only.
tools.name: get_buy_box

tools.description: Replace the authenticated buyer's buy-box. Requires at least ONE market AND at least ONE strategy — below that floor the buyer is invisible to matching, so the update is refused and nothing is written. Markets in states we do not operate in are dropped. The buyer is emailed that this connection changed their buy-box.
tools.name: update_buy_box

tools.description: Return the deals owned by the authenticated wholesaler's company, newest first. Depth is capped by the account's plan tier. Read-only.
tools.name: get_deals

tools.description: Read a deal package the AGENT already has (a signed purchase agreement, scan or photo) and create a DRAFT deal from it. The document is passed as base64 — we do not fetch it, and we never touch the agent's own storage. It lands as a DRAFT and is NOT submitted. The response returns `merged` (the full stored field set) and `missing_for_submit` (the exact gaps that would block submit_deal, computed by the SAME check submit_deal runs) — resolve those, then submit. Two gaps are documents, not prefill values: if `missing_for_submit` lists `photos`, attach them with add_deal_photos (from a shared Drive folder); if it lists `assignment_contract`, attach the signed PDF with add_assignment_contract. Accepted document types: application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp. Counts against the account's 30 document reads per day.

content.description: The deal document (a contract/scan), base64-encoded (no data: prefix). This is NOT a photo of the property.

fileName.description: Original file name, for the audit trail

mimeType.description: One of: application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp

prefill.description: Values the user stated explicitly; each OVERRIDES what the document says. Every value MUST be a string — pass "45000", not 45000. Keys are deal fields; the ones that block submission are: assignment_permitted, property_address, property_type, square_footage, property_condition, occupancy_status, asking_price, estimated_arv, assignment_fee, seller_timeline_to_close, liens_or_title_issues (creative-financing deals also need existing_mortgage, remaining_loan_term, loan_assumable, current_interest_rate, seller_open_to_creative_financing, seller_willing_to_carry_note). "photos" is NOT a valid prefill key — a string cannot satisfy the photos requirement; attach real images with add_deal_photos. After the draft is created, read `missing_for_submit` for the authoritative remaining gaps.

tools.name: create_deal_draft

tools.description: Set or overwrite plain fields on an EXISTING draft — the way to resolve a field in create_deal_draft's `missing_for_submit` WITHOUT creating a second draft. Pass only the fields you're changing in `fields` (each value a STRING); they are MERGED onto the draft's current data (they do not replace it). The response returns the updated `merged` set and a fresh `missing_for_submit` — repeat until it is empty, then submit. NOTE: `photos` and `assignment_contract` are NOT plain fields — use add_deal_photos / add_assignment_contract for those; a value passed here for them is stored but cannot satisfy the gate. Use get_deals / create_deal_draft to get the dealId.

dealId.description: The DRAFT deal's id, as returned by create_deal_draft / get_deals

fields.description: Deal fields to set/overwrite — the SAME keys as create_deal_draft's prefill, each a string. The ones that block submission: assignment_permitted, property_address, property_type, square_footage, property_condition, occupancy_status, asking_price, estimated_arv, assignment_fee, seller_timeline_to_close, liens_or_title_issues (creative deals also existing_mortgage, remaining_loan_term, loan_assumable, current_interest_rate, seller_open_to_creative_financing, seller_willing_to_carry_note).

tools.name: update_deal_draft

tools.description: Attach the mandatory property photos to a DRAFT deal. This is how you resolve a `photos` entry in create_deal_draft's `missing_for_submit`: a prefill string or a photo URL can never satisfy it — real image bytes must land in our storage. Give the photos ONE of two ways: (a) `images` — the photo bytes directly, each base64-encoded (the simplest if you already have the files); or (b) `driveUrl` — a shared Google Drive FOLDER (share it with our service account or set it to 'Anyone with the link', else you'll get `cant-access-folder`; sub-folders aren't scanned). JPG / PNG / WebP / HEIC are accepted (HEIC is converted). With `driveUrl` we import ONE batch per call — if the response has `remaining` > 0, call again with the SAME folder (idempotent, never duplicates). Use get_deals / create_deal_draft to get the dealId.

dealId.description: The DRAFT deal's id, as returned by get_deals / create_deal_draft

driveUrl.description: A Google Drive FOLDER share link (not a single file), shared with our service account. Use this OR images.

images.description: Property photos as base64 bytes — the alternative to driveUrl. Send more with another call.

fileName.description: Original file name, for the audit trail

tools.name: add_deal_photos

tools.description: Attach the executed assignment contract (the signed PDF) to a DRAFT deal. This is how you resolve an `assignment_contract` entry in create_deal_draft's `missing_for_submit`: it is a server-stored document, so a prefill string cannot satisfy it. Pass the contract as base64 in `content` — the SAME bytes you passed to create_deal_draft if that document WAS the signed contract. We store it and run the state's required-language scan (#347): the scan only EVIDENCES — it never approves, and if the state requires language the contract is missing, submit_deal will block with the specifics. Attaching always succeeds; the verdict is enforced at submit. Use get_deals / create_deal_draft to get the dealId. Accepted types: application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, image/jpeg, image/png; max 25 MB.

content.description: The signed contract document, base64-encoded (no data: prefix)

dealId.description: The DRAFT deal's id, as returned by get_deals / create_deal_draft

fileName.description: Original file name, for the audit trail

tools.name: add_assignment_contract

tools.description: Submit a DRAFT deal into the pipeline. It must pass EVERY compliance check first — a prohibited state, a market we're not in, a missing mandatory field (photos included), a missing assignment contract, or contract language the state requires all BLOCK the submission, and the deal stays a DRAFT. If a gate blocks, the reason is returned so the user can fix it; the agent must NOT try to bypass it. Use get_deals to find the deal id.

dealId.description: The DRAFT deal's id, as returned by get_deals

tools.name: submit_deal

tools.description: Archive a SUBMITTED (or reprocessed) deal and replace it with a new DRAFT carrying the supplied changes. The original moves to Dead in the CRM and is pulled from disposition, revoking any buyer links. Use get_deals to find the deal id. A reason is REQUIRED and must be one of: sold_elsewhere, price_change, terms_change, fell_through, other — do not invent one; ask the user which applies.

changes.description: Deal fields to change on the new draft, e.g. { asking_price: 250000 }

dealId.description: The deal's id, as returned by get_deals

reason.description: Why the deal is being revised

Use this tool when the user offers, attaches, or asks you to use their CV to find assignments that suit them. Pass the document as base64 in `document_base64`. If you have already read the document's text, pass it as `cv_text` as well, which avoids re-parsing the file. Matching starts immediately; call my_matches afterwards to read the scored results. Before using this tool, make sure the user actually wants their CV uploaded, and tell them what it does: the CV is stored on their consultant.dev account and REPLACES any CV already on file; it is processed by AI to extract skills and experience, which the account holder must have consented to once on consultant.dev (this tool cannot collect that consent and will say so if it is missing); and if the account has match alert emails switched on, a stored CV is used to generate those emails. description: Search Airbnb stays by location and dates, and read a single listing in full, as structured JSON. Runs on HasData's hosted API.

tools.description:
Get Airbnb Listings

Searches Airbnb for available stays by location or map bounding box (neLat/neLng/swLat/swLng) and date range (check-in/check-out) with guest composition (adults, children, infants, pets) and nextPageToken pagination. Returns listing id/url, title, price per night and total, rating, review count, coordinates, and photos. Use for travel planning agents, short-term rental market analysis, pricing/occupancy research, and lead lists for property management.

checkIn.description: The check-in date for the listings.

checkOut.description: The check-out date for the listings.

location.description: The location to search for listings. Required unless a full map bounding box (neLat, neLng, swLat, swLng) is provided.

neLat.description: North-east corner latitude of the map bounding box. When all four bounding-box coordinates are provided, listings are searched within the box instead of by location.

neLng.description: North-east corner longitude of the map bounding box.

nextPageToken.description: The token used to retrieve the next page of results.

swLat.description: South-west corner latitude of the map bounding box.

swLng.description: South-west corner longitude of the map bounding box.

tools.name: hasdata_airbnb_listing_getAirbnbListings

url.description: The URL of the Airbnb listing. Must be a valid Airbnb listing URL.
